reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a great day!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach was definitely a must see stop on our trip to Sydney. The beach was pristine. We went on a Tuesday and the area of beach where we parked our towels was not in the swimming area so it was somewhat secluded with just a few other visitors around us you were able to go into the water to Wade not Swim. We were able to splash and keep ourselves cool, which is about all I was inclined to do as a surf was very rough. The beach is simply beautiful. There's a nice pavilion where you can change and have restrooms and there was also a spot to have lunch were utilized all of the services. The restrooms and changing areas were very clean. We had beverages and pastries as an afternoon snack. My husband really enjoyed his pastry! It was about a 20 to 25 minute drive from the Fullerton hotel in Sydney. We spent the entire day and will be going back after a one day break from the sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney visit from Perth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Sydney for four days and did a boat trip to Manley beach, there was a surfing competition going on which was fun to watch. It was very busy lots going on everywhere due to the competition and crowds nice little shops to wander round and get you’re gifts, a lovely place to visit.Having got the bus to Bondi which was about 30 minutes we arrived and were pleasantly surprised the beach was lovely clean white sand and beautiful ocean. Cafe’s and bars a plenty market stalls with all different things of interest, The promenade walk was lovely as the beach curved around lots of people again sunbathing on a beautiful day. Both places had different vibes but equally good.In all we crammed a lot into our 4 days but loved every minute before returning to sunny Perth.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here on our way from Sydney to Bowral. There's plenty of parking. Somewhat strange was the payment of the parking fee, because you don't get a parking ticket at the end of the process. However, the police can trace that payment has been made by entering the license plate. The beach wr well attended and also some surfers in the water. Climbed past the poll the way in to look at some artwork. The stop was definitely worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Post Tragedy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the beach one day after the tragedy, the foreshore reserve area was still full as many had come laying flowers to pay respects to the victims, but the beachfront area was almost completely empty. That aside there's a skate ramp to the south end of the beach, and good sweeping views of the beach offered from up at Notts Avenue next to the Icebergs swimming club.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very attractive place and amazing view on the ocean. It's easy to get here from the center of Sydney by public bus. I didn't swim because of high waves, but it was lovely to spend time on the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sydney’s most famous beach. Prone to dangerous currents. Swim between the flags or don’t swim at all if you don’t know how.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Classic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: THE classic beach of Sydney and a good place to take your first dip as well. Lots of restaurants and pubs and a good place to carry on walking southbound along the coastal trek which is lovely

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best place for honeymoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best place to be for your honeymoon experience. Nice beach and environment. Pure breathtaking and winds. I recommend it to anyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: For a walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach. There are usually surfers.To the right over the hill there is a viewpoint.We had a hard time finding parking in the area. There are plenty of bars and joints for a drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I made sand castles and pee'd in the water! (Review by my 6yo nephew). The water was cold. It was still fun though!.......

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good … but very windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this beach as a part if group tour. Unfortunately it was a windy day and bit cool too so we couldn’t go to splash the waves. Just watched the surfing activities from a distance. It had very long stretch of clear waters. Looked great

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach. Crowded on Australia Day Monday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most iconic beach of Sydney, even the name that comes to mind to first-time visitors when thinking of beaches in Australia as a whole. Bondi was  and technically is still a suburb of Sydney although urban sprawl means the 2 are contiguous now. The beach is the closest to the city’s CBD and most easily accessed from Circular Quay where we were staying by bus (379).  Our friends, however, picked us up and drove us there.It was the Monday of the Australia Day weekend holiday and the beach and surrounding area was packed. Needless to say the parking lots were full and we were lucky to find a spot.  We elected to stay on the grass under the trees closer to the parking lots rather than hang out on the sand. The younger ones among us swam while we walked along the beach and  sidewalks enjoying the view. There were many surfers making the most of the waves rolling in.We spent a couple of relaxing hours people-watching and enjoying the views and energetic vibes of Bondi

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated location - but stop by if you're in town anyway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you’ve been on Australia’s east coast for a while and seen the typical and less prominent locations, you’ll have a somewhat sober view of Bondi Beach.It is a place with a lot of see-and-be-seen factor. Of course,ä is also surfed there as on many other beaches.The lagoon on the right edge of the beach is world-renowned, but as good as any major beach resort in Queensland. And New South Wales has such a lagoon. However, it differs in that it is permanently filled by the waves of the sea, or water flows back into the sea.  At Bondi Beach, there is not much else that would not be in the form or other popular beaches, except for the sculptures on the boardwalk that winds southward from the beach and offers a beautiful view of the surrounding area. Quite typical of Australia is further that the beach offers no shade, no trees, no umbrellas etc apart from a few picnic pavilions at the car park. You just sizzle in the sun in front of you.All in all, so, on, quite a place, but not as spectacular as it is often portrayed. Places like Byron Bay, or Airlie Beach, I think offer at least as much. Surfers Paradise beach is much longer and also offers plenty of glamour.For Sydney residents, the beach is of course an absolute hotspot, as it is right on the doorstep.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Special place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a Saturday so it was busy…..  full of life and fascinating to watch the movement.Many many training schools on view………. Quite a few for children all in bright orange tops.The sand is soft and white.Deserves its reputation

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Got to be done right? It’s iconic for its  surf scene and the Icebergs swimming pool. Plenty of people on the beach and in the water. Was a little surprised that the T4 train didn’t take you closer than Bondi junction so whilst we had anticipated a fair walk I just wonder why the line was never extended. That said it was nice to just sit and people watch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: City 2 Surf - Bondi Beach Finish Line
reviewsWithKeywords.text: City2Surf Finish Line and one of the prettiest and scenic finish line for a Fun Run in Australia.  Plenty of space even on a crowded event such as the City2Surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach with its golden sand and clear blue waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach as a top tourist destination is great for swimmimg and strolling.The golden sand with its clear blue waters is best for great photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach with loads of energy. Great for people-watching, surfing, or just soaking up the sun. Only downside is it gets packed (yes I know), especially on weekends, so don’t expect peace & quiet. Still, it’s a must-visit if you’re in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Average
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I personally find Bondi beach very average. Sydney has more than 100 beaches that are better than Bondi. Parking is very difficult and expensive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the most picturesque but iconic Australian beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the best known surf beach in SydneyPaid it a visit at the start of a walk down the eastern shores to Coogee to meet relatives Frontage a bit tired (reminded me of a uk seaside town) but nice beach and surfquite busy - not too busy but it is their winter

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved it here. Such a great spot. It’s public, beautiful and spacious.I’d highly recommend coming here. It’s gorgeous and relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach, sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach sydney ...Winter with sunny day, looks bondi beach so busy ....Surrounding by people activities such, running, sunbathing, swimming, playing around .....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the ferry from Circular Quays to Rosewater Bay and from there got the bus down to Bondi Beach which took around 20 minutes. Bondi Beach is exactly how people describe it. It’s a vibrant, busy beach which is perfect for surfing and swimming. There are plenty of places to eat and drink along the beach and different walks that you can take along the coastline. If you are into fitness, there is an outdoor gym space. Get the bus back into the city from Bondi Junction.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So we didn’t realise we went to Bondi on a public holiday…boy, was it busy!!  However… we still had a great day!  The sea was clean and warm; plenty of activities, shopping and food outlets around.  Do the Bondi to Coogee walk… you won’t regret it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing and Iconic Beach Spot in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a stunning spot in Sydney with golden sand, clear waves, and a great vibe. Whether you're swimming, surfing, or just relaxing by the water, it's a perfect place to unwind. Plenty of cafés and the scenic coastal walk make the visit even better. Definitely worth it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, surf and sydney vibes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We joined locals gathering at Bondi on a gloriously sunny day and immediately understood its appeal. The atmosphere was electric with a perfect mix of relaxation and activity.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My opinion - over rated !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach - well, iconic beach in Sydney and probably most widely known globally.In my opinon - Surfer's Paradise / Gold Coast is better than Bondi beach. This is in terms of general crowd, weather, facilities, cafe/pub/restaurant in/around the beach.However, many will differ wrt Bondi beach vis a vis Gulf Coast / Surfer's Paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful ❤️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everything you want in a beach, soft sand, clear water, waves and  a beautiful view. There's shops a short walk away where you can find  great sushi, pizzas and Anita's ice creams. There's also swimwear boutiques that made me wish I hadn't bought one in the UK, and obviously everything a surfer needs, a Billabong T actually from Australia is a must buy !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A bucket list place, But I dont know why.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well, If you are visiting Sydney, you just have to visit Bondi Beach its a bucket list place.. But in all Honesty, I could not understand what all the fuss is about... Its just a beach, and not too spectacular at that. I suppose it was not helped by the fact it was a cool miserable sort of day, no glistening sunshine.. We used the hop on and off bus to go there .. There is also a couple of cafes, with a limited range of food.. Nice murals along the sea wal... lAnd that is it really..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As impressive in reality as on TV
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful unmissable beach easily accessible from the centre of Sydney!I recommend taking the boat from Circular Quay to Rose Bay Wharf. Just walk and cross the Bellevue Hill neighborhood to Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: People always say Bondi Beach is a must-visit in Sydney, so I decided to check it out.The beach itself is beautiful, but it felt a bit too touristy and crowded for my taste. That said, I did find a few nice cafes around the area that are great for relaxing and people-watching.Bondi is definitely iconic, especially known for its surf and coastal walk—but probably better if you don’t mind the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a world-famous destination known for its stunning coastline, golden sands, and energetic surf scene. Whether you're an experienced surfer or just looking to relax by the shore, Bondi offers a picturesque setting with breathtaking ocean views. The surrounding area is filled with lively cafes, coastal walks, and vibrant street art, making it a perfect spot for both adventure and relaxation. With its welcoming atmosphere and iconic beauty, Bondi Beach is a must-visit for anyone exploring Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I had a blast while in Sydney. Got a chance to learn to surf and see the lifestyle it has in the area. Beautiful view and vibe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Riesiger Strand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Toller, riesiger Strand. Perfect for walking, relaxing but also for swimming. Either in the nature pool or in the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Scenic and Popular Destination with a Lively Atmosphere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is undoubtedly one of Sydney’s most iconic and beautiful beaches, offering a pristine stretch of golden sand and clear, inviting waters. The beach is well-maintained, making it an excellent spot for various activities, whether you're swimming, surfing, or simply enjoying the coastal views.The surrounding area is vibrant, with a variety of cafes, restaurants, and shops offering both casual and more refined dining options. The convenience of having amenities close by enhances the overall experience, making it a great place to spend a day.However, it’s important to note that Bondi Beach can become quite crowded, especially during peak tourist seasons or weekends. The large crowds can sometimes detract from the tranquility one might expect from a beach outing. Additionally, the parking can be challenging, with limited spaces available around the area, making access a bit more difficult for those driving.Overall, Bondi Beach remains a must-visit destination for both locals and tourists. It offers a dynamic, lively atmosphere, combined with beautiful scenery and a wide range of activities. While it can be busy at times, the beach’s appeal and offerings make it well worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful & dangerous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I've ever been to. Listen to the frickin lifeguards and you'll be fine! Read the signs and stay within the flags. I'm a strong swimmer who knows the ocean, and this is the toughest ocean experience I've had. I loved it, and my partner did too, but you should be aware of the ocean here and trust the lifeguards and flags as a result. Don't go in too deep - the undertow is very strong. We were stung by bluebottles, but the signs were up, so it was no surprise, and we got through it just fine.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney Beach, although a little too touristy, is still a stunning spot.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For a more intimate experience, you can take a lovely walk along the coast to Clovelly. It’s a much quieter and more peaceful area, making it a great escape from the crowds.Just minutes from the heart of Sydney, this beautiful sandy beach offers great views and a lively atmosphere. It's a fantastic surf spot, and the outdoor pool is perfect for watching the surfers' performances while also being a place to see and be seen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic location worth visiting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: spent the day in the Bondi area, easy to get to from Sydney by bus, we swam in the iconic Icebergs Pool, sad to see it was damaged by storm weather after our visit.   We walked along the beach and then to the shops, had fantastic brunch in one of side streets.  Loved the vibe and when we were there it wasn't too busy, bucket list item ticked off on my Australian travels.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoyed the views and a gelato
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Last stop on our tour, time enough allowed to visit the beach, enjoy the views or a snack. We choose to enjoy the views as we headed to the gelato outlet nearby.  A good number of the 'beautiful' people enjoying the beach, a few peacocks flexing their muscles and showcasing bronzed torsos, many of the peahens equally interesting. Great vibe in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Famous Aussie Beach itself !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The great famous Aussie beach ! Shops, bars, restaurants the famous Icebergs !It has everything for a great day or evening out ! Great coastal walks too !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went here for a few hours.  The beach is wide and looks like it would be nice on a day with better weather.  The waves were massive today!  The beach is surrounded by a main street with a few shops and lots of small restaurants.  We took the 333 bus from the city but there are other ways to get there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picturesque beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this famous beach as part of a group tour. This was a windy day, after a cool front had just come in. The beach looked very nice, with good rolling waves. There some men working out and showing off. Near the beach, we had a brief tour of the Bondi Surf Bathers Life Saving Club, established in 1907. A nice place and well-worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best view of Bondi for photos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best view and to take photos of Bondi is the high footpath on Campbell parade just near the North Bondi RSL. A beautiful view facing south. Bondi is one of the great city beaches of the world. It’s a majestic wide fine sand beach. There is nearly always somewhere relatively calm to swim. Pools, close to shore etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy place! Listen to the  life guards
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is an absolute icon! The golden sand, rolling waves, and buzzing atmosphere make it a must-visit in Sydney. The surf is amazing, but it can be dangerous if you don’t follow the flags and listen to the lifeguards—they’re there for a reason! It gets super busy, so expect crowds, but that’s part of the experience. Tip: Bring plenty of water and sunscreen because the Aussie sun is no joke!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy beach with lots to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a fun time! Easily accessible by transit. Parking (especially free parking) was exceptionally hard to find. Lots of amenities around the beach - change rooms, wash rooms, restaurants, outdoor gym, water fountains, etc... The beach is patrolled by many lifeguards, so we felt very safe. The north end (farthest from the Icebergs pool) is by far the calmest area. If you are into surfing the south end is the best. This is definitely not a "float around in the water" type of beach - the waves are quite big but great for body-surfing. The actual beach can get crowded, but it is so big that finding a spot to set up is not difficult. Stay between the flags!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing. Too big, too crowded, too dirty.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very disappointing. Very much mill in the sand, great distance to the water, strong waves, no umbrellas or sunbeds for rent. It wasn't fun.We stayed at 4 beaches in Sydney. Dear Manly Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun to check off of the Sydney bucket list
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As something that is a must do on a Sydney bucket list, I had a good time. The beach is nice and there’s lots of room to spread out from others. If you want to swim, north side is for you, surfers are on the south side. It was fun watching surf school and the professionals. There are umbrellas for rent on the boardwalk - I believe the sign said $15/hr. Lots of lifeguards and surf patrol making sure everyone is ok. It enjoyed it a lot but if you want less of an “attraction” there are prettier, quieter beaches to the south of Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunny afternoon at Bondi Beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach itself is not special, but people and animals add a lively and relaxed flavour to it. Enjoy a nice sunny afternoon here! Very good experience, love comes from above the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun with friends
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing pristine beaches with a swimming pool pristine white sand turquoise blue water excellent surf conditions boutique shopping in Sydney. I went with a group of friends and had a really great day in the sun. Don’t forget to slip slop slap because the sun is strong.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to holiday plenty to do for the kids and lovely places to go out and enjoy a fantastic meal fantastic place.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place great spot for kids . We loved every single thing about the area the weather was amazing and the people where lovely

reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a poo beach.  No reason for coming other claiming going to Bondi.Dirty and run down.Sand was full of rubbish.Don’t waste your time go to the other beaches down the coast

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ocean dive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazingly huge beach for sunbathing and dive into the Pacific Ocean! The waves are great for surfing as well! The sand as smooth and you can walk without shoes!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must go
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach, clear water I have been here many times with my family and it is the most wonderful beach ever it is sometimes a little crowded but over all it is beautifulTips:Go early in the morning it is less crowded and the sunrise is amazing Grab an ice cream from Anita’s or Messina’s (I think Messina is better) and sit at the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go elsewhere for cleaner water and better waves.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are far better beaches in Sydney. Try Manly, Palm Beach, Coogee for example. Bondi is for tourists, the locals know where the water is cleaner

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love the Beach and plenty of Bars & Restaurants
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We jumped on a government bus in Sydney city centre to Bondi Beach just for day trip  It's about 40-45 mins depending on traffic, but worth it to see a bit of Sydney and it's suburbs.   These buses run past Bondi beach almost every 5-6 minutes so it was easy to jump on a bus back to the city.  They don't take cash though so make sure you have a contactless card to board. Bondi beach is a superbly clean beach, well guarded with experienced lifeguards to keep you safe if you're venturing into the waves, which can be very high and there's a strong RIP current to watch out for in certain parts of the beach.  Best advice is swim between the flags!    The facilities are excellent, with showers and toilets all free to use in the changing area.  It's a lovely building with a few shops with local artisan pottery, a small art gallery and clothing stores.     There are a few restaurants directly on the beach in this same area so easy to grab drinks, snacks or lunch without having to go to far.  Above the beach there's some good independent shops for Australian clothing/swim gear etc (go to Budgy Smugglers for some iconic Australian trunks and swimsuits).Overall, we enjoyed the beach, and the small town.  It's not huge (think Margate), but if you're a keen surfer it's ideal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A certainty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach and full of young people. There are no services (except rescue), but it is beautiful for that. Recommend

reviewsWithKeywords.title: super
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach – The most famous beach in this city. Of course, there was a lot going on here. The waves were relatively big, but people were bathing. There were also free toilets available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A day spent at bondi is definitely worth it, but would advise getting there early if looking to park nearby.Some nice food places to grab an early breakfast or snack at lunchtime.We ventured into the iceberg pools at the end of the beach, $10 each for the day well worth it if you want to have a dip without all the sand.As with all the places we visited the cleanliness is of a high standard.Can’t wait to get back there one day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't stop knowing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with a sophisticated atmosphere, beautiful people and many shops, restaurants and good beach! There is a swimming pool that you can pay to just take drops or to enjoy. Many surfers and great places for photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beaches in Australia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's amazing. Another continent, another world. Be sure to visit, and certainly not in the European summer, but in the Australian!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach is a great place for a swim
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach not far from the city center. You can take a bus and you will reach Bondi beach i haft an hour. There, you find nice restaurants, shops and coffee shops. A nice little excursion on a hot day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow, what a wonder full experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean and clear, one of the most active beach. I was able to experience a walk early in the morning and access the beach with showers to rinse off the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice beach but even better starting point for the Bondi to Coogee walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a beautiful and famous beach and while I did enjoy my time here, I definitely recommend walking a little bit along the Bondi to Coogee walk because there are so many better beaches along the way that are way less busy. But the Icebergs poolon the Bondi beach is nice and it wasn’t crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great energy, lots to do, eat and drink.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a beautiful location, huge open beach with a big prom to walk along. The pavilion was always buzzing with energy when we were there. A huge amount of food and drink option. There were tonnes of surfers out and people swimming and playing ball games ect on the beach. Yet very clean and well kept. You can also walk between the beaches on a costal path. The place has a great energy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing day at the beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach very close to the center of Sydney.White sand clear and cold waters small wave enough world but there is plenty of room for your towel.Highly recommended for a relaxing day on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, Sand, and Endless Summer Vibes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A visit to Bondi Beach is a must for any traveler to Sydney. It's a place where you can relax, rejuvenate, and immerse yourself in the vibrant coastal culture.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney Beach, although a little too touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sandy beach just minutes from the centre of Sydney. Beautiful surf spot and incredible outdoor pool to both admire the surfers' performances and see and be seen.Departure of a very nice walk along the coast to Clovely much more intimate

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What an awesome place to go!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach’s full of energy and surf culture. The clear water and reliable waves combined with the breathtaking coastline makes Bondi Beach iconic and picturesque. The Graffiti Wall, which changes every now and then, complements the vibrant atmosphere of the beach as well. So many fun things to do around the beach too! The beachside offers decent restaurants, cozy cafes and great shopping. Definitely a chill hang out place in Sydney! These all explains why Bondi Beach attracts thousands of tourists and locals to visit.The beach is absolutely easy to access by public transport. If you’re taking a train, you can go to Bondi Junction Station first and transfer by bus. There are also different direct buses from CBD. Either way takes you 30-45 minutes. Include this spot in your must-go list!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Bondi in early March. It was a fairly warm day, but it happened to be sprinkling. This small bit of rain guaranteed we had the swimmers section of the beach ENTIRELY to ourselves. The water was warm, the waves were so fun to play in. We had the absolute best time. After we were done playing in the water, we went and got crepes nearby at a creperie, then went and got some great Bondi Beach shirts. Such a fun and memorable day at a great, historic beach. We would go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The place to be!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The name speaks for itself. The heart of Sydney, the place to be. Don’t need to say a lot about this place. Pristine white sand and crystal clear water, everything you could ever want is on and around Bondi. Gets crowded in the afternoon but that comes with the name. Despite that, the beach is spotless

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good to visit but didn’t live up to the hype!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is obviously a must do when you visit Sydney and was a good one to tick off however we found that the actual beach didn’t live up to the hype and can be extremely busy in peak season, on top of that there wasn’t loads to do in the surrounding area. Furthermore, we found that other beaches in the area such as Manly beach were in our opinion far better and had more to do on the actual beach and in the area surrounding.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a must visit just to say you have! Full of mainly young people surfing and posing on the beach. Loads of eateries and bars.If you have take out food, (fish and chips!) watch out for the seagulls!!Best to go by public transport because parking is near impossible!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed in Bronte and did the cliff walk to Bronte a couple of times which is plenty but can get crowded.Bondi beach itself is only 1km so not huge but sandy and surfi with plenty of folk enjoying.Its famous and many flock there, but not as many restaurants as I thought there might be on the front.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: after watched it in tv show, finally i have a chance to visit bondi beach. and its amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a wonderful beach. Australia is so lucky it has many beautiful sandy beaches so close to the city. when i visited australia, i only visited Bondi and Manly. Bondi is more famous because of one of the TV show. i love this place. there is kids friendly pool for safe swimming, the sand is so soft and clean. many cafes, and very easy to access by bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Serene beach for vacationers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its a pristine and beautiful beach for beach surfers. Excellent beach outing for family as well as water sport enthusiasts. The well made promenade is well laid n maintained giving opportunity for joggers n fitness lovers. Wind sand with aquamarine water is a delight to our eyes. One of the very good places of interest near Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely coming again! Great beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very good experience, lots of sand to play with :). There were loads of sunbathers, so snag a spot earlier in the day if you like it. We enjoyed shopping in one of the coastal shopping villages; so awesome! Definitely coming again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty crowded, but still worth a visit. Public transport is probably the best option to get here if you're not a local as parking is tricky.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a gem! The golden sands, vibrant surf, and lively atmosphere make it a must-visit. Perfect for sunbathing, swimming, and people-watching. The coastal walk offers stunning views and the local dining scene is fantastic. A true Sydney highlight

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's just a beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sure it is a famous beach. It is clean, shops and restaurants around and there are nice houses with a view of the beach. But in the end, it is just a beach. The nice thing is that it is a stop on the hop on/hop off bus. We were there on a relative cold day. Not many people around, just some people surfing. We had the beach practically to ourselves. I can imagine that with more people around there is more of a vibe

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really liked Bondi Beach. The vibe is really cool and there are nice restaurants and cafes around the area. Lots of swimming and surfing also. The view on Icebergs Pool is legendary.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a photo stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful views, highly priced shops and very busy even in winter. Would suggest q quick visit unless surfing is your thing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice beach but nothing super special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s very clean and it looks stunning, but at the end of the day it’s just a beach. It’s very crowded, even in winter, so it’s probably not the best choice if you want a calm beach day. Unless you are big into the surfing scene etc. you might find this kind of boring.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very busy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Small but busy beach right off the street. Too crowded for us to feel comfortable swimming. Still worth a trip just to say we went. We grabbed some drinks and snacks and had a little picnic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited during the off season and everything was absolutely lovely. The beach was not crowded and the water was decently warm for the season. We got to visit lots of shops and restaurants on the beach that were very nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Didn’t disappoint beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach was a must-visit for me because of its legendary status, and it certainly lived up to the hype. The beach is stunning, with plenty of surfers and people enjoying the sun and sea. The area also offers great shopping and lots of restaurants, making it a must-visit destination.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I lived on the island for years. That's one of the reasons the beach didn't impress me. Nice restaurants around and parking facilities available.In my opinion probably overrated.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi is a state of mind
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Iconic beach living on its reputation. Bondi is not the most scenic beach in the world, it lacks the white coral sand, it is not all that big or long, the surfing doesn’t seem all that particular. I guess Bondi is more a state of mind more so than anything else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place for early morning walks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is always worth a visit, it is very touristy and there are many other notable beaches but it is still an iconic place that is definately worth a visit whilst in the Sydney area. On our most recent stay we visited quite often in the early mornings before first light when it was busy with joggers doing the Bondi circuit. There have been some changes since the pandemic but it is still a beach that has great appeal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: TV beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice to have been here, easy to take bus 333 from Hyde Park here. 20 minutes and you are there. Good weather and it was a relaxing afternoon on the beach. As for the beach, of course it's lovely sand, but there are many other beaches that are at least as good or better

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with nice soft sand. Got crowded as we went on a Sunday but the atmosphere was great.  Restaurants next to it are pretty expensive..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great and above all clean beach. Easy to reach by public transport. But on the weekend it's more of a matter of luck to get a place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach + coastal walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Parking in the area is 10AUD per hour. Went there on a week day and it was crowded and with a lot of traffic. Better to go as early as possible. You can go in the water but being careful. Water was nice and clear. The coastal walk is beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique Experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like the ocean and watching/participating in surfing, this place is amazing.  It is HUGE.  For me, a walk up and down the beach was a perfect distance.  There are some elite beaches in  the world and  this is one of them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very famous & pretty beach but crowded (it was the weekend though) with shops selling very over priced coffee & ice cream. I ventured down to the water & OMG it was FREEZING!!  Being a soft Brit, I was expecting the water to be a bit warmer than it is in Cornwall but the sand made up for it - so soft, it was like walking on air.When visiting Australia for the first time, you gotta do these things & find out for yourself that it's not all hot weather, warm water & kangaroos - but it is awesome :-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did the walk from Coogee to Bondi and it is a nice long walk, about an hour.  Had lunch at Iceburg Pools (bring ID) and took pictures of the famous pool and beach.  Then walked to the beach, nice clean large beach.  No need for watershoes, the sand is soft.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Jumped at Christmas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sydney's mythical beach, at Christmas it's fun for families with temperatures approaching 40 degrees, a surfer's paradise

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most gorgeous beach with iconic coastal views. You’ll get the best vacation pictures of your life here so head back at sunset. Bondi has a very strong current so keep your sunglasses in your bag or you’ll get hit by a wave and lose them like I did. Be sure to swim between the flags and wear plenty of sunblock. Don’t be deceived by the clouds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was very good. Beautiful scenery and vibe. It is hot with no shade so bring sunscreen. And make sure to swim inside the flags

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice, nothing really special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, smaller than I thought, just wanted to go there and check it outNice to check off my bucket list but Australia has beautiful beaches everywhere

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Australia Icon....wear a hat and use sunblock!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I watch Bondi Rescue frequently. We heard Manly and it's area is nicer to visit. Everyone has heard of Bondi. We went on a beautiful, warm day on a Sunday in January. We got there around 11 am and spent an hour there. We had our bathing suit on, but the water was a bit cold for us. Tickled to death to see the lifeguard building,   lifeguards, surfers,  and the beach. The sand is very fine. A real family beach. Lots of activity of little kids to seniors doing lifeguard camp/training . Another thrill was seeing the Iceberg pool. Shark nets and boars keep an eye out for those unwanted sharks. Took a cab VA using a ferry , or bus. Restaurants nearby. A bit touristy, but around 1 pm it started to get very busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, we went on a Monday so it wasn’t super busy. The water was clear, the lifeguards putting up the red and yellow flags always makes us feel safe. Lots of restaurants and shops on the Main Street.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is iconic, probably the most famous beach in the world. I loved it. People are chilled, beach is great. I was surprised that the sea wasn't as warm as I'd expected. Once you are in the water, it's great. The surf smashes into you and really takes you off your feet. If you have children, they will need you around in the water with them. Great place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this Iconic beach setting in Sydney.  Glad I went, but not as good as Manly Beach.  Plenty of shops and restaurants, but a little pricey!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic surfing beach in Sydney.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Iconic beach in Sydney, especially for surfers, it is very large and open, but what we really liked was taking the walk along the coast from Coogee, about 6 kilometers of walk where you pass other beaches such as Gordon's Bay, Clovelly Beach, Waverly Cemetery, Bronte Beach, Tamarama Beach, ending in Bondi.On the beachfront you can enjoy multiple fast food restaurants.Must visit in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Now to the 4th course
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi. Excellent views. With a pool looking over the sea. Would recommend the bars & restaurants. With a balcony view. With amazing desserts.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had to go to Bondi at least once while we were in Sydney and it was worth it.  The waves were amazing and we had a great time playing in them.  They do get quite large so you need to pay attention and know what you are doing.  We also walked the path  south of the beach and the views are fantastic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous beach -better for fun or surfers than swimmers.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: approx 25 mins from the city or airport Bondi beach is an amazing , huge beach with gorgeous white, clean sand. ( no smoking or dogs).Plenty of space but the majority sit between or near the flags- this is where you are supposed to swim as monitored. Many swim/ surf outside this area but there are rips which can drag you back so take care. Waves are the main fun part of the beach- great for teenagers & adults to have fun in but there are other beaches eg Rose bay nearby which are flat & good for kids & swimming in. Bondi Iceburg pool costs apx £9 for adults- salt water & not always calm but the small pool attached is nicer. You need ID to get into the restaurant there (adults only) & it serves nice food/ drinks.There is a popular walk along the coast ( lots of steps up/ down) to Coogee- worth doing.On the beachfront there are souvenir shops, chemists, supermarket and a Mcdonalds plus lots of smaller cafes and one very popular bar on the corner of Hall st. ( 18-40's range). Most importantly next to the beach there are excellent facilities to change , basic showers & toilets & a lovely restaurant. There are also large grass areas & trees to get shade. The bus stop is next to the beach-333 will take you direct to the city- or go to Bondi junction (10 mins) & change to the train -this is quicker but more hassle- although the transport system in Sydney/Bondi is cheap and very good whether you use bus/ train / tram or uber.You can just pay with your bank or credit card- no need to get an Opal card- same price -tap on/ off. I recommend buying sun protection there as the quality is far better than Europe lotion.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nothing special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Every trip to Sydney includes a stop in Bondi.  I have never been particularly fond of this beach.  While the beach and fine sand is nice, it usually is very crowded, not so much on this visit in July.  I noticed more garbage on the ground than ever before.  Bondi Beach is easy to get to by transit.  I prefer the beaches to the north, particularly Palm Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had the best time looking at tide pools and exploring the area. Some kids pointed out an octopus in the tide pool and that was super cool to see. We saw lots of different sea creatures including starfish and large crabs. It was a beautiful Saturday and quite busy, but we had a lot of fun at this famous beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a very beautiful beach located in Sydney with beautiful fine sand.It was one of the things to see on our group trip. The sea was rough. We got our feet wet and the water was pretty cold.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach 🏖️ in Southern Hemisphere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best Beach 🏝️ in the Southern Hemisphere. Another thing there are big waves 🌊. Also the ocean 🌊 is very clean 🧼 too . Lastly, there are lifeguards at this beach 🏝️ too which is nice  👍.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lot to do by the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great thing about Bondi is that you have plenty of accommodation, shops and restaurants all by the beach. The beach itself is over crowded and the sand is dirty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach to relax and enjoy views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent about an hour on Bondi Beach just walking around and enjoying the views. Took the Sydney Hop On/Hop Off Bus and it was one of our stops on the blue line. Definitely worth the quick stop. Next time I'd bring swimsuit/towel and enjoy 1/2 day there including lunch and shopping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach looked nice, but it was a cold and very windy day, so not much action that day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As part of a tour of Sydney, we stopped at Bondi Beach for 30 minute stop.  Unfortunately, the day was a little chilly and very windy, so it was not very enjoyable as the wind was blowing sand in your face and eyes.  Our tour guide assured us this was a very enjoyable beach on most other days with the weather is cooperative.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views of Bondi Beach from the Coastal Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a walk at Bondi Beach along the Coastal Walk on a Sunday morning.  The weather was sunny and unseasonably warm for July.  There were tons of people around the area just enjoying the beautiful views of the beach.  The Coastal Walk was well paved and is very dog friendly but I would say that it is not an easy low key stroll since there were some sections where there are some stairs to climb.  There was a section along the side of the path that was set up like a small dog park with a water fountain for dogs.  After our walk, we took a stroll around the nearby shops and restaurants.  It was such a pleasant day and I would go back to Bondi Beach if we ever visit Sydney again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach with kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went with family and my kids w such a good time. It was easily accessible via train and bus. Definitely must go with loads of sunscreen lotion

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not to be missed!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went to this beach one day taking a taxi from Sydney. The beach is beautiful, clean, the sea is a little rough but the water is still very clear. On the seafront there are many shops and restaurants. Not to be missed!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You have to have been there
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The ultimate experience in Sydney! The backdrop of the beach with the surfers 🏄‍♂️ is amazing.. the bars are a fantastic experience, as there is something for every taste! Big waves, great atmosphere 🥰

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach with entry level surfing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: lovely beach though smaller than some pictures portray!  Not too many places for such other than the Promede which is excellent and highly recommend.  Though I'd been to Sydney 4-5 times previously had never gone since logistics to get there seemed complicated.  They're not.  Jump on a 333 bus and you're there in 30 minutes.  Won't be disappointed!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Check out the icebergs if you want safe swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a look at the beach and decided to go to the icebergs instead and then do the coastal walk. Well worth walking along to get  to the free pools though rather than paying for the icebergs. The beach was too busy for us but the waves and surf looked good but it wasn’t as spectacular as we were made to believe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not sure what all the fuss is about
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well it’s a beach. Quite busy. A few people trying to surf. Not much in the way of good eating or drinking places. I thought Manly beach was much nicer

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take something to settle in or buy on site.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, quite clean with nice waves.A spot popular with surfers.Luckily it wasn't too busy during our visit.What is missing is beach beds to rent and umbrellas. Which may be a disadvantage or an advantage for others.It is possible to buy all the equipment (parasols, tents, games for children) in the shops opposite.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach is a beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was cool to go. A lot of surfers. Iconic. But just a beach. OK restaurants along the beach promenade. Good that they have showers along the beach though!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi fever - Bondi draws the crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the train and bus to Bondi - head for the beach at Bondi, when we visit Sydney. Beach, glistening ocean still draws the crowds, the life-saver statue is a reminder, though, of caution.  The Bondi Pavilion has been updated and has undergone an amazing transformation. Not been to Sydney in a long time, we'll come again soon. (I have gait/walking challenges (stroke), wear a legbrace.)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family trip 4 days in Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The waverley walk is amazing and very well worth while.I would stay at Bondi Hotel if you can.  The cocktails are $14 about £7 and it is open mon-sat till 12 and till late.   Closed early on a Sunday.Other bars are open but can be expensive as shots can be $30 each.The staff at bondi hotel are amazing and just across the road from the beach.The Pavillion restaurant breakfast from 930-11am is amazing.  The bacon and eggs on toast are fab, as is the yogurt granola (incs liquorice and surprising great).   Breakfast including, coffee 2 drinks, 1 granola bowl and 2 bacon eggs toast about £35.  This is a contract to 2018 when would have been double even though the exchange rate is about the same 1.8 to pound in 2018 and 1.9 in Nov 23.We went to Coggee Bay in 2018 and that was fab too but prefer Bondi Beach as a little more going on and access to other places is great.Tip   - get the 303 bus into Sydney for $20 from the shop.  We had 4 trips into Sydney off peak and a trip on the ferry from Sydney to Darling Harbour and back.  A bargain for £10.  A must.the supermarkets are so much cheaper than 2018, a great surprise.  However, if you smoke they are $65 for 25...yes £33.   My one son smoked so a bit of a shock, but I agree keep them expensive to discourage smoking.Their local chemists are really cheap so no need to pack suncream (a bucket of factor 50 is £7.....to encourage you to use it, great idea), shampoo etc.Really loved Bondi Beach, so clean and beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful area with a great beach and trendy shops and restaurants.  We really enjoyed taking the coastal walk and taking in the stunning views and rock formations.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfers paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Famous beach, 20 minutes by bus out of Sydney Harbour. Incredible fine white sand, a few restaurants to eat or drink. One of the most famous beaches in the world...so you must visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach is synonymous with Australian culture
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is synonymous with the Australian beach culture, to relax and enjoy life and soak up the rays. These days, you can catch some waves and avoid the effluent that once plagued the beach. Bondi Beach is now pristine, and it's only a few miles from the center of Sydney. By the way, be careful with your trash and avoid stubbing cigarette butts into the beach sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunny day!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect weather on Spring time. People are sun-bathing and do water activities. As a tourist and did not research the temperature, we were walking with long pants. Enjoyed walking around.  The restaurants are packed with people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Another visit with new family members. Although parking is a nightmare, the beach is tidy and clean with plenty of space for visitors. There are plenty of restaurants and cafes nearby, and a great place to visit on a warm day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Can’t believe I’m actually in Bondi beach after been watching it on tv for so many years. Beautiful, well kept, and lovely walk on sand . Lovely eating places nearby and parking is very easy close by . Definitely worth a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach and surrounding area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach and surrounding area (with some nice walks around the edges), loads of places to grab food and super clean! Overall impressed

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most important and busiest in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is one of the most important beaches, located 9 km from the center. We arrive by public transport in about 35'.It is extensive with clear sand and waves suitable for surfers who usually come daily in the early hours. Next to it is the Bondi Beach Park (large green space with barbecues) and a wide esplanade that runs along it, ideal for walks or sitting and contemplating on some of its benches. There is also Bondi Pavillion, a pavilion that houses restaurants, a cafeteria, bathrooms, changing rooms and lockers (fees apply).When we went it was a splendid sunny day and the beach was quite busy, even several people in the sea.The avenue that borders it, Campbell Parade, offers a number of cafes and restaurants, as well as some accommodation options.A few meters from the beach is the Icebergs Club and the trail begins that continues to Coogee Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots to see and do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really amazing beach and recommend for everyone visiting Sydney to visit Bondi. Lots to see and do. Great restaurants and bars. Beach is very clean and amazing surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ticks all the boxes....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: With its white sand, accessibility, excellent amenities and cafes for visitors this stunning beach ticks all the boxes, for visitors and locals alike.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Got the t shirt
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was days before showers I was there. I got the feeling that everyone who comes here comes for "been there, done that" experience only. Crowded and overrated.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful beach well worth the visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunning! With soft powder white sand which is clean tidy well looked after with life guards and safe areas to swim / surf. The water was clear and cool on a hot day. There are fresh water showers and a changing area and toilet facilities in the pavilion. Al' top tipsCatch the 333 bus from Circular Quay in Sydney all the way to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: a must-see for any visitor
reviewsWithKeywords.text: With easy public transport access, playgrounds, historic landmarks, and rock pools, there is something for everyone. Whether you're looking for a place to relax, or get your adrenaline pumping, Bondi Beach has it all. From the iconic Bondi Icebergs to the stunning coastal walk, you won't be disappointed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It was nice, BUT not sure what the big deal is...maybe if you're a surfer?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach. It was not crowded the day we went. It was part of a tour we did of Sydney. We had lunch at a restaurant located on the beach and later relaxed here for a short while. The sand was soft, and the water temperature was okay. I'm not a surfer, so I can't address that aspect. Overall, it was a nice beach, but nothing exceptional.  What DID work? I don't generally like beer, but the restaurant waiter suggested one popular in Australia (Bundaberg ginger beer) and I loved it! I have found it here at home!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mandatory
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is an iconic place close to Sydney. It's well known abroad and deserves this qualification. The beach is simply stunning. Brave, big and very beautiful. We obviously took a bath there and the experience was amazing. Then you've got a walking promenade, plenty of shops, restaurants, etc... and the town itself is very nice.  Definitely, a mandatory place to go

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So many better beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want to be seen or people watch this is a great place. It’s busy. The water is rough most days. The sand is lovely though. Beautiful to view from the walking trails north and south. But if you want beautiful beaches with locals go north to one of the 4 other beaches. My pick would be Coogee or Bronte.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Infamous Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not much to say. World renowned surfing location. Sun, sand, people, ocean....Great area of Sydney and there's even a Canadian pub up the road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice beach area. It gets very crowded but it's a nice visit not too far from Sydney proper. If you want a relaxing beach day, there are better places, but this is not a bad stop for a quick stroll along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a cold water. We couldn't swim. The fact that not many people use buses to get here made us unhappy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Over Rated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is ok I went because I felt I should. Mannly Beach is much nicer. Although it was not sunny when I went so that doesn’t help.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Water Views, but Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful water and nice views of nearby housing developments; however, it is very crowded and the water very cold.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyable day out on Boxing Day. Leisurely ride on the bus from Elizabeth Street, Central Sydney. The beach is clean and safe. A lot of places to eat and drink. Friendly service everywhere. Cheerful, caring lifeguards. We had a pleasant conversation with a couple of lifeguards. One used to live in London Putney. Thank you for making our day memorable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is famous for its pristine beach and surfing and since the 1980s topless bathing! It is 4 miles east of Sydney. Bondi is an Aboriginal word meaning surfing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoyed the walk, the views and of course the swim at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Made a day of it and got off the bus at the Waverley Cemetery at Bronte, and strolled through this interesting place with magnificent views of the ocean until we reached the walking trail along the foreshore. We then took in all the fantastic views while walking past Bronte beach and Tamarama beach before reaching the famous Bondi beach. We had a very relaxing swim (between the flags of course), until it was time to leave.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic location that has to be done.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Iconic beach in Sydney, the locals will say it's not there best but if like us it is one you just have to do. Good parking right at the beach and the costal walk that runs along the back of it is great to stroll along.Nice wide white sand, life gaurds are on duty but if not a string swimmer take care with the currents.The street looking into Bondi has a number of shops and cafe's.All in we enjoyed our time at this famous location.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: i would say it's a must see place, once you get here you wont be disapointedas it is spring the waves were not that big, but loads of waves to test your skillsamazing place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a bus to Bondi beach from Sydney, only cost us $3.  It is an iconic beach both for its sands and sharks.  The sand is fabulous, if a little hard to walk on.  Parking is good with plenty around.  The surf was fabulous

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We staryed 5 days near the beach and enjoyed walking the beach. Great surfing spot, beach is busy, especially on the weekends. Lots to do here, even if you get some rays.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi- a small nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice beach with scenic views and walkways.    With bondi iceberg swimming pool on one end and kids pool on the other end of beach... a very nice place for a quie evening or a family day time at beach..  it has surf boards rental available as well..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a very nice beach, no stones. Very good for surfing. There are also rock pools nearby and other walking trails that gives good views along the coastline.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit when in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach to visit when in Sydney. Great selection of shops along the promenade. Don't miss the markets if visiting on the weekend. You can easily spend few hours here just walking along the beach. Children's pool also available at one end. Many rock pools to get down to as well. Lots of grassy areas too to have a picnic and enjoy the views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Charming even in the shoulder season
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A bit off-season, however, some people were braving the water for swimming and surfing.  We found it easy to reach via public bus; it is convenient to downtown Sydney.  Its own neighborhood is less urban than Sydney's core and was a relaxing place to visit.  We walked on the beach and on the trails along the water nearby.  It may be livelier at other times of the year.  Maybe not a must-do for September, however, I was glad we went there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach. There are far better in Oz but it’s still worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Virtually everyone who comes to Australia has heard of Bondi Beach. It’s fame enhanced by the fly on the wall docu Bondi Rescue. There are far better beaches in Australia but there’s no denying that Bondi is in a great setting with more surfer dudes and chicks per square metre than anywhere else! If you’re not in the water there’s a great walk around the back of the beach, about 1km length in total and all on the flat. Further back are an array of shops, cafes and restaurants. It’s a great spot to come to and spend a few hours if not all day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach but I couldn't see anything special. Plenty to do for kids with the skate park Like most beaches nice to walk along.Heaps of dogs everywhereHappy to see it but will not rush back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful again today!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was certainly great to be back here and we got the first nice day in ages. It's still winter so this was a walking tour rather than a swimathon. But it was great to be reunited with my son and his new Australian family ahain and enjoying the primo location of Bondi Beach once more! Separated by the Pandemic but finally reunited.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Australia's most famous city beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Backpackers from around the world gather at Bondi Beach to celebrate Christmas Day every year. This pristine strip of white sand, 1 km long, is 7km from the Sydney CBD, It's around half an hour travelling time. Bondi Beach is Australia's most famous urban beach. "Bondi" is Aboriginal for "water breaking over rocks."

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited in june-july so it was winters in Australia. The beach wasn't as crowded (that was a saving for people who want peace and solitude 😋

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must go
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately I went there when the weather was at its worst! Torrential rain! However, that didn’t stop me from seeing the amazing view and despite the nsw gov warning to avoid water sports, there were still lots of surfers. Definitely will visit there again when the weather is better but A MUST VISIT. Take the train to Bondi Junction and catch bus 333 or 380 (u will see the beach and you can stop at any bus stop along the beach). First time in Sydney and the people and place is just beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blue water and clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is well connected from the city using Bus and Rail.The views on the way are amazing. The walkway has beautiful laid back feel with all kinds of restaurants and activity wear shops dominating the streets.The beach was very clean, people were minding their own business. As it was the cold season so not many people were in water and we observed that helicopters hovering to monitor the people in waters inciting them to return to the sand.The water was clear blue but the waves were high. Probably that is the reason this place is famous for surfing. It would be necessary to look over young children here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worlds most overrated beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the most over rated beach on the planet. Crowded full of arrogant people and feels like everyone is in a bad mood.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit to Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well what can I say about Bondi Beach you seen reports & reviews this place does not let you down. The Beach was clean the sea was nice its all you could wish for. Its a dream to come here from the UK.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful long wide popular clean beach with an ocean pool. It is patrolled so a good place for a dip.Easy to get to from the city by bus or train. Thanks for the vote if you found this review helpful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Undeniably the best beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful location, beautiful people around, you dont need to check weather to come to this beach, whether you are getting into the water or not, this is the best place to be when you feel like hanging out. Bustling cafe scene and great night lifee to around this area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place for a walk eventho its cloudy and windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Extremely cloudy and windy but that doesn’t stop people from having walks here at Bondi Beach like my partner and I. We love the sound and the calmness of the waves, what a beautiful place to catch up with you love ones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Beach of Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach: a name, a warranty. If you think about a beach in Sydney, surely Bondi will be the first name which will pop up to your mind. It’s very big and you can take breathtaking photos, the water is quite cold but at least you can take a bath.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney’s iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Along with Surfers Paradise, Australia’s most famous and iconic beach. Best way to get here is via a bus or train to Bondi Junction, then take any of the buses to the beach. Although it’s picturesque and has excellent views, it gets very crowded so you may want to visit one of the other beaches in the area if you want some privacy.Lots of cafes and shops around if you don’t wish to visit the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Australia's most famous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is 100% Aussie, even though every backpacker  in the country seems to turn up for Christmas. The water is clear and normally the surf isn't threatening, and the sand is golden.  Life Savers patrol the beach, but please, if you can't swim, restrict yourself  to paddling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach Visit - public lockers available?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hey Everyone I attempted to go to Bondi beach & hire a surfboard & a public locker After asking lots of people ( life guards, ticket inspectors, ice cream vendors etc ) and no one knew ! Their pavilion is under construction where they used to be & Bondi looks like it needs some much needed attention! Considering the wealth around you’d assume it’s happening soon After an hour of walking around  I found lockers for hire @ icebergs ocean pool I could not just pay for the locker only but had to pay for admission as well, so $12 aud in total Note to council * maybe some signs to let travellers know where they are ( lockers ) or an information booth with a phone support central to the beach The Bondi people are soo friendly and the beach is amazing itself & we had a great time once settled

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sublime again last year!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had such a varied travel diet last year before everything closed, including time spent in Australia and then the United Kingdom on the other side of the world. Bondi had been fabulous with limpid blue waters lapping at the edge of the golden sands. It was amazing to come on an uncharacteristically swell free day last summer. The waters ere quite calm and still for its being Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One best beaches in Australia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach with its vast stretch of beach and families, nippers, and surfers are amazingly beautiful. There’s real difference between north and south shore of beach. At present one side sits iconic restaurants and cafes, others have North Bondi surf club. An easy way to spend time together, bring your chair, beach towel, and please watch out surfers and stingrays, or else Bondi patrol will come to rescue. A breathtaking and beautiful place, Bondi Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to spend New Year’s Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I highly recommend visiting Bondi Beach when exploring Sydney, it’s a great place to spend the day if you’re looking to relax and have a beach day and for us there’s no better place to start the year than on the world famous Bondi Beach!The beach is very well protected by lifeguards, even though the sea was a little rough I felt safe at all times, I don’t think I’ve ever visited a beach so thoroughly patrolled as Bondi is.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a great beach, with gorgeous white sand. It’s got a public pool at one end and Icebergs at the other which there’s a fee to enter. There’s lots of cafes along the main road and Esplanade. There’s the Bondi to Coogee Walk. It’s easy to get the 380 bus from Watson’s Bay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An iconic Australian landmark!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sydney has an abundance of iconic landmarks  which most visitors to the city put on their sightseeing schedule.  And Bondi Beach is certainly one of them.  It’s probably true to say that  the 1km stretch of  that picturesque and sweeping white-sand crescent of Bondi is one of Australia’s most iconic beaches. Bondi Beach is definitely worth a visit, for some surfing, or swimming, or sunbathing, or walking along the sand, the beach promenade, and the lovely  coastal cliff walk that heads south from the beach to Coogee Beach.Whatever you do at Bondi Beach,  do it sensibly.  If you intending to swim or surf, use sunscreen as the harsh Australian sun can be cruel on your skin.  There are lifeguards on duty, and clear rules for swimming and surfing are in place for your safety.   Take care of your belongings; most beach-goers keep their belongings close to them, though I believe there are lockers in one of the pavilions.  There’s ample changing and showering facilities.Even if you don’t want to swim, surf or sunbathe, at least go to Bondi Beach to get a feel for  the beach and surfing culture which  is a part of the Australian lifestyle. The beach itself is attractive, but it becomes extremely crowded in the warmer months.  There’s also lots of other stuff you can do when you get to this beach.  Walk along the fine sand, or the beach promenade,  or rest awhile, and simply take it all in.  There’s some fine street murals to check out on some of the concrete walls by the beach. There’s cafes and shops right in front of the beach, but they do  get crowded.  Step behind the beach onto Campbell Parade for a plethora of shops (many with a recurring ‘beach theme’), cafes, restaurants and bars.  It’s a great stretch for browsing, and for sitting outside watching the passing parade.  One of my favourite activities is the Bondi to Coogee cliff top walk.  It takes a couple of hours at a leisurely pace; you may even find the smaller Coogee Beach less crowded for beach activities. Even if you are just going to say you’ve been to Bondi Beach and to get the obligatory selfie, do go to Bondi Beach.  The beach is around 7km east of the centre of Sydney; I usually take the 380 bus from Circular Quay; it takes about 45 minutes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is one of the most iconic places in Australia. It is famous for its waves and its sand. It's a beautiful place. Great for a swim and great for just a walk. We have been there many times. We love to just stroll around. There many cafes and eateries as well as other types of shops. It gets quite busy during warmer months.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It should be called SHARK BEACH!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and me went there and went swimming. I have to say that although the water is nice, the beach is terribly sandy. It was really white. Be warned, if you go onto the beach wearing socks and sandals like we did, be prepared to get sand all over your socks. Also, make sure you take sunscreen or you will end up really burned all over. I wish someone had told me that as well. We couldn't move for the next 4 days and stayed in our hotel on the bed. At least the room service had plenty of good food in our hotel which was great. The other thing that I wish I had known about were the SHARKS! I never knew that Australia had sharks in the water. It's crazy! Worst of all is that they JUMP OUT OF THE WATER!!The whole place is full of sharks. One guy told us that because we are from the USA they like to eat Americans more than Australians. I saw one jump out of the water that was huge but he said that was just a baby. I got a photo of it to proof it. The people down there are crazy, no way would I ever swim in their sea water if I had known it was infested with sharks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always a good day out at Bondi.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Certainly the best known of the Sydney beaches - it is always a pleasant day out ta Bondi. Although I would try to avoid public holidays when it can get very busy. Nowadays (with COVID) I would suggest Bronte as the more enjoyable alternative. .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Out of season
reviewsWithKeywords.text: August is not a good time for the beaches in Sydney. It was cold and windy, with some rain, deserted but one can imagine what it looks like when it's in full use. Definitely a must when you visit Sydney. A good way to see it is to take the blue line on the Big Bus hop on - hop off tour and get off at the beach, takea stroll to the next stop and catch the next bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect place to sunbathing, try to surf, skate, practice yoga and do shopping.. I love watching waves and surfers ! I recommend to walk on coastal walk from bondi beach to coffee beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An Icon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its Bondi, you've got to go.But dont expect the cafes to be value for money... they are expensive! but some of the food is pretty good, even if the staff are unfriendly, snooty gorgeous people !!!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great place to visit, swim, or workout first thing in the morning or early evening. It can get packed at other hours. Seasonal of course.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just as good as it looks on telly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Another iconic location, the beach was clean and full of people. Lots of pubs and restaurants around. Sat and watched the life savers for a while and soaked up the sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very popular place with the locals since Australians loved the sun, sand and sea. Other than the beach, there are lots of restaurants and shops in the area. A great place to rest and relax.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited here recently on a visit from ireland. I've always watched Bondi rescue and was dying to get to bondi beach. When I got there I was kinda shocked at how small it is in real life. Lol the t.v show kinda makes it seem alot bigger. Anyways it was a nice beach. The waves and currents are very strong. It's a nice beach to sun bathe but a bit too strong for me to swim in lol. I was in for about 10 minutes and I had enough of being bashed by the waves. You do need to be a strong swimmer to take on Bondi. It's a nice beach just to chill and people watch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great to have seen it over summer!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is always an iconic place to visit and it was great to have caught it just before the huge shutdown. It was packed at that point with wall to wall acreages of displayed flesh.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spend The Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great beach to explore and enjoy the sea life. There are bars, restaurants, and local shops. It was winter so it was slow and we didn't swim. I can only imagine how crazy it would be in the summer. Good times.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped here for a quick visit with our tour group.  The beach is very nice and was empty when we visited, which was during the week.  Another couple on our tour stopped at the beach a couple weeks prior when the weather was extremely hot and they mentioned that there were so many people that you could not even see the sand.  Our tour guide also provided information regarding the Bondi Beach Lifesaving Program, which we found very interesting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not that impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were unimpressed with Bondi, we were not there for all that long, but it was nothing outstanding, just a beach and the day we were there the waves were nothing to shout about - did expect something more spectacular - have been to many better beaches - we were not in the water - just had a walk along the prom - the murals were quite interesting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi!!
