reviewsWithKeywords.text: Finally made it to the famous Bondi Beach. I’m not one for the sand and beaches, however this was a must. I loved taking the cliff walks around Bondi, and don’t feel like you have to walk the entire thing. We just did a short 15 minute walk around and saw some great cliffs and rock formations along with good views of Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were disappointed with Bondi beach as it was extremely crowded on the day that we went. Most people seem to go for a quick dip and to pose for selfies etc. Nothing wrong with that but we expected a cooler beach than the one populated by people taking pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wanted to visit the famous bondi beach when in Sydney hopped on a bus which took us right into the centre it is a marvellous beach but to be honest less than I expected it was very busy with plenty to see in the surrounding area so having seen it I can write it off my bucket list !!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic & Worth a Visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always wanted to visit Bondi Beach, high on the "bucket list" so really happy to have done it.I realise there are better beaches locally, Manly, etc. but this is Bondi.Loads of people around, all nationalities, so great for people watching.Great bars & restaurants, cafes, etc. everywhere, lots of shops selling the usual surf & beachwear, so bring your credit card.A great few hours visiting, was a bit rushed, but well worth it & recommend a visit if in Sydney.Chose the nearest cafe for a snack & drinks, service, food, drinks all amazing, loved it.A great few hours at Bondi, the beach was as advertised, just fabulous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous beach with lots to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Expansive beach with lots of shops and restaurants about. Visited 20 years ago, the place has cleaned up quite a bit ...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Infamous for a reason
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have visited this beach in both the winter and summer. When we visited in the winter we were the only ones there, and for good reason as it was very cold, but it was still nice to sit down and chill out. In the summer it was relatively packed but there was still ample space to lye down. The transport links to the beach are okay, although you have to get a train and then switch to a bus at Bondi Junction which is a pain, and despite the buses being frequent, they are very full in the summer months. As this is a world renowned beach, there is no shortage of shops and eateries lining the back of the beach so there is no need to worry about food etc. and the beach itself is well maintained and extremely safe with an amazing lifeguard service. Keeping to shallow water it is safe, however rip currents are common and the waves, further out, are massive. The iceberg pool is also situated on the southern end of the beach and is a nice place to visit if it is not too busy! If you're visiting Sydney then I definitely reccomend a day trip to Bondi if you are there between the spring and autumn months.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and iconic beach, crescent shaped, sandy, nice surf and ambiance
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the best beach in Sydney, favorite of surfers and the young crowd, with lots of sand, sun and fun things to do, with lots of restaurants nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a driver show us Sydney and ended up here. Had lunch at Iceburgs, amazing views, great views and reasonably priced. The beach was loaded with young folks, must be a college somewhere near. Good shopping across from beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its Good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved Bondi beach and the vibe but thought it to be overrated. Probably the sea waves are perfect for beginners to learn surfing and that's how it garnered so much attention. The town maybe tiny but has some amazing cafes, restaurants and has the most happening (lively) crowd The walk from Coogee to Bondi is a must though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always wanted to come here and it really didn’t disappoint.. Beautiful golden sand, clear water and manned by lifeguards who are professional and always seen so you feel safe.. Close to cafés and shops so always easy to get a drink.. I love it here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfing with Lets go surfing Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best thing about Bondi beach -learn surfing. The waves are little and not something a real surfer would write home about, but for beginners it was ideal. The instructors were patient and friendly too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous crescent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Simply a stunning location!  The beach is enormous with beautiful wave action for surfers and swimmers.  Stroll along the cliff walk and take in the fabulous views!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunrise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Staple beach for early morning visits. Plenty of leisure spaces for stroll and picnic. Excellent beach patrol always felt safe to swim

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Sydney beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the Big Bus out to Bondi and were not disappointed. It’s quite a large beach, with clean soft sand and the big breakers. Lots of surfers to watch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking in more ways than one.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Four of us spent a wonderful afternoon and evening enjoying the beach,surf and evening dining around Bondi and all of us were in full agreement that Bondi lives up to its reputation and some!The beach itself is vast and it seemed to accommodate the many enjoying the weather quite easily,we managed to throw down towels to the rear of the beach wall so to offer at lest some shade and spent an exhilarating time in the water being dragged here there and everywhere.The currents are really strong and the rip tides too,so do be careful,although the Lifeguards were constantly warning people and are obviously very diligent.After a few hours on the beach we called into the North Bondi RSL for drinks to meet up with family and were highly impressed with the silent tribute observed at the designated time,something we did not know of so total respect to this tradition.From the RSL we strolled along the promenade to the South end of the beach for dinner and an enjoyable evening relaxing and catching up.So a wonderful day spent amongst an incredible and iconic beach,we loved it and can't believe how people now seem to recommend Manly over Bondi,no chance,Bondi everytime for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Understandable reputation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A wide expanse of fine white sand, which gently slopes into the sea, which reliably delivers a decent surf. All this and only 4 miles from the centre of Sydney. I went there expecting to be underwhelmed but I wasn't. One sad note. Someone was washed out to sea and drowned on the day we went so I would keep away from the rocky extremes of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach Walk and beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was a can't miss site when in Sydney. The beach, surfers, water and views were outstanding. The beach walk / coastline trails had amazing views of cliffs and ocean views. The path is not the place for those with balance issues or mobility impairment. The stone steps very in size, angle, height and make this rather dangerous for those with any walking issues. There were not always great handrails either. The walk was worth it if you are  mobile and in decent shape. Be careful if you guy. Folks have died on this walk. The views are worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's a beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you're into surfing and a surfer, then I can see the appeal. We went to say that we had been. A stretch of retail outlets mixed within eateries and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Guess I just didn't see the excitement about this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was part of a local tour.  It just was not as exciting as they make it to believe, but then we are not surfing people.  It looks like it was more exciting in years past.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was at Bondi Beach late afternoon and it was great not crowded enough room where your not sitting on top of each other, highly recommend visiting the beach later in the day in summer. The was was really warm and clean. With a dinner on the grass area viewing Bondi turning into evening was breath taking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice little beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Crowded but a nice beach to swim ,surf, and walk in the water.  Worth the trip to see while visiting sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Smaller than the reputation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Biggest reputation for a beach in Australia.  It may have a great surf reputation and swimming is fine but it is a relatively small beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty cool beach! There’s a cool graffiti wall and the beach is clean. I went when it was still chilly (I went last May) so we didn’t go in the water, although that didn’t stop the locals. I would definitely recommend going and walking around even if it’s too cold to swim. It’s a short drive away from downtown Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Iconic! Clean and fresh which was very pleasant refreshing. Great walk on the sand and lovely climb on the rocks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun Sea Sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sydney is surrounded by beaches but Bondi is the main one and located in the city. This beach is paradise for surfers & they create a magnificent view on the sea. The beach is really vast & Bondi to Coogee coastal walk is really sprawling & scenic. One can spend a whole day in the beach. People are always busy with different activities like volleyball, surfing n all. Not only human even dogs also come for a coastal walk.People do picnic at the beach side & it's really well connected with the other sides of the city.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golden Sands
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to Bondi Beach yesterday at the end of the Coogee to Bondi Coastal Walk.It is an Australian Icon, so therefore very busy. A tourist Mecca even now with the Covid-19 virus threatening.Too busy for me, but if it is your scene you should check it out!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We live in Florida,USA and found Bondi Beach stunning. We found it clean, the locals pleasant and the cliff walk awesome. We also rode the hop on hop off bus which was very slow to pick us up BUT it was Friday rush hour so we just took it to the last stop and walked to our hotel through one of the parks. Wonderful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking Views!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband, son and I took the Coogee to Bondi walk for the first time in many years and it was just as gorgeous as we remembered! Walking along the sea cliffs, through several lovely beaches, and ending at Bondi is a terrific way to experience the best of Sydney. We went on a Saturday but there was smoke that likely kept some of the crowds away. Still, there was a steady flow of people, mostly tourists. Next time we might go on a weekday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but didnt really live up to my high expectations.  We took the Hop on Hop Off Bus just to take pictures of it.  We didn't get in the water.  It was really too hot for us to be there without doing so.  I think that may have prevented me from enjoying it as much as I thought I would.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See
reviewsWithKeywords.text: World famous ad certainly worth a visit. Awesome to see the rocks where the pool juts out into the sea. We did a walk from Coogee to Bondi Beach and found some of the other beaches nicer! Bondi beach is quite busy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not my favourite destination
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately, Bondi Beach and surrounds are overcrowded, poorly maintained by Waverley Council and there's litter everywhere !!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You must visit this beach. The water is beautiful and the sand is clean. You can walk near the cliffs and see spectacular views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach nothing special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand was beautiful, white, soft and nice to walk on, the sea was warm very salty though! There were sun loungers and deck chairs to hire for $10 for 3 hours, worth getting though. Little shops dotted around, showers and toilet facilities. The beach is good for water sports. Nothing too special but is a nice beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is easy to reach by bus from Sydney CBD. It is a beautiful 1000 meters of golden sand and warm gentle waves. The water is clear and refreshing, but the sun is intense. There is no natural shade, however umbrellas and cabanas are available for rent. Plenty of restaurants and shops line the street. Public washrooms and changing facilities are available. Take a walk south for some smaller, less touristy beaches like Bronte Beach. The coastal walk is incredible and keep going further all the way to Coogee Beach if you have the time and energy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Icon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach always a beautiful site. Easy to get there by walking from Bondi junction or directly but bus. Water is always cool but enticing. The boulevard is tired so you can imagine the era and who has enjoyed this icon. Beautiful memories

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Yep, it’s ‘The’ Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great to visit this iconic beach, just to see what all the fuss is about (we’ve all seen at least one episode of Bondi Rescue!)Overcast when we were there so the 20,000 plus visitors they can get per day was down to about 150!It’s a lovely clean beach and we enjoyed a good swim.The beach isn’t as big as I was expecting and don’t think I’d like to be here when it’s packed.Enjoyed our time here, but there are (in my opinion) better beaches around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Packed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent some time here on New Year’s Day.  Naturally, the beach was packed. It was a very lovely day. The temperature was just right and everyone were having a great time. Got a chance to walk around and explore the area. Very nice beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No Cigars!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: During our Sydney stay we decided to visit the iconic Bondi Beach.The beach is a great place to visit a stroll along the shoreline We started off at the Icebergs swimming pool with the fantastic view across the bay

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wear your sunscreen.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the public bus from Sydney, they get packed tightly to the beach. The beach is quite beautiful, such white lustrous sandy beaches and some kick arse scorching sun, like you have never experienced ever before.My friends and I were out hanging out watching peeps and by the water for about 45 minutes and I had blisters on the back of my legs from that short time out. We didn’t have any sunscreen on since we really didn’t intend on sunbathing and were hanging out at the cafes and restaurants nearby. The sun is intense and the claim is that even the SPF from home has zero efficacy against the Australian sun at all. Buy it there. I think Australia has the highest rate of skin cancer and I get why. Wear a strong SPF even if you are out briefly here walking. The sun blister was painful for days and kept us hotel bound for several days.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach , clean , water was beautiful, easy to catch bus there  from city , met a couple of the lifeguards! Great walk from Brontes pools ! Lots of food choices across the street!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always a popular location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here for a wander after getting off the Big Bus tour and found some lovely shops, bars and restaurants. Also had a stroll along the lovely beach. Well worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun beach but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is the iconic Sydney beach, and it’s a lot of fun. The retaining walls have wonderfully colorful art painted by local artists, there are plenty of concessions, showers, and changing rooms, it’s easily reached by public transportation, and you can surf, swim, sunbathe, or sit in the shade of a rental umbrella as you like. And, if you like crowds of nearly naked folks sitting, surfing and sunbathing within inches of you, it’s the place to go. I prefer secluded, pristine beaches, so Bondi’s charms were limited for me. It’s a scene, fun to watch, not a place I’d want to stay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Obligatory Check-in
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's part of the must do experience when you hit Sydney however if I am honest I was a little disappointed.  So many more beautiful beaches along the coast. It was really busy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Rocks !!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Though it was too cold to swim during my visit I loved the beach itself and the massive waves! We also loved the rocks and got some great photos! Recommend a visit to Bondi!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good facilities but not as picturesque as hoped
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked to bondi beach from potts point. Great walk and bondi was nice. Good restaurants and good changing/shower/beach facilities. We hired an umbrella and 2 x loungers for $35 for 4 hours which was a lot but worth it. Was expecting a more picturesque beach but it was pretty standard. It was a nice day but wouldn't rush back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BONDI Beach Sydney is Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Date of experience: 26 December 2019Bondi is one of Australia’s most iconic beaches because of its sweeping white-sand curved shape. Bondi gas its own dramatic scenery. Bondi is attractive to walkers and joggers. Reliable waves draw surfers while, nearby, hardy locals swim in the Icebergs ocean pool year-round.Bondi Beach has been used and is still used as a location for numerous films, television series, music videos, and a video game. The tour manager of Thomas Cook said that numerous festivals and events such as the annual “Miss Bondi beauty pageant” have made Bondi Beach a popular destination among travellers. The beach has long captured the attention of poets including legendary Les Murray, Joanne Burns and Brook Emery.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were recommended to trade Bondi for Manly Beach but were keen to say we’d been to Bondi. We loved it! For someone who hates sand, I loved the feel of the sand at Bondi. So much in the way of people watching and the water was gorgeous. We laid on the beach, went for a swim and a stroll and enjoyed coffee at one of the little shops along the foreshore. Keen to check out Sydney’s other beaches next time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rain!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went here twice in January- once rainy, once sunny and very different experiences. Loved needing the Bondi lifeguards when they were filming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Right out of the TV series
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An absolute “do not miss” when you are in Sydney! Together with Copacabana and Waikiki Beach probably one out of three of the most famous beaches in the world. And dramatic with the strong currants and high waves!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the lovely place in Australia.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach. People look very happy. Very clean and safe. Beautiful wave. We spent few hours in here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everything is awesome. The beach, the mood, the people. We had a wonderful time. People from all over the world are there. We made the walk trough the beaches and the landscape is breathtaking. I recomend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just an overall Greek beach town with an amazing nightlife and food scene
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So I stayed and bond I beach for four days I hate the trails north to Manley and south to Cordia Beach what an amazing experience to walk those trails. The beach itself is utterly amazing and you have so many people at the beach at all times the water was clean and clear cool refreshing and if you serve early morning had some of the best surfing I so I stayed in Bondi Beach for four days I hate the trails north manly and south to corgi beach what an amazing experience to walk those trails. The beach itself is utterly amazing and you have so many people at the beach at all times the water was clean and clear cool refreshing and if you surf early morning had some of the best surfing.I stayed at the week up hostile right in the heart of bond I beach which I recommend pretty much anyone because of how nice facilities are. Are you sure if you were there on a Sunday to go to the Bondi market great experience if you like flea markets and small vendor foods

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a a beautiful clean beach the sand was soft and the sea clear if a little cold, we had our 3 year old so we didn't venture to far into the sea, there is a small seawater pool next to the beach which was perfect for us it has a seating area. There are lifeguards and set areas to swim and surf. The waves are big and the current strong. We had to walk a fair bit to find a restaurant that had space as it was busy. We took a taxi to the beach which I was glad of as the parking seemed full. There are beach showers available which are handy. This is a lovely beach and a must if your visiting the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy to access from Hop on bus stop.Clean sand with Lifeguards on duty.Surf beach so large waves with undertow so swim only between the flags. Lovely walk to Iceburg pool then local shops for great priced souvenirs such as good quality tshirts at $40.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our favorite beach...the very fine sand feels great beneath your feet.  Many places to eat nearby completes the experience.  Getting train away from beach is a challenge because of big crowds so we took a taxi back to Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surf paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Soft white sand and big surf waves!! What a great experience other than the parking fee $25 for 3 hours😩The lifeguards set up a good stretch of beach for safe swimming.The cliff walk from Bondi to Coogee Beach is an amazing way to see the different rock formations and beaches along the way Just under 7 km hike Lots of joggers and training parks along the way if you’re inclined to do it as a workout

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A short stretch of paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have visited many of the famous beaches in the world, but few as lively as Bondi ! The sandy stretch is relatively very short, as compared to Copacabana Ipanema but it's the cleanest and well maintained. The beachside restaurants offer some of the best food and drink in Sydney! One can relax with a chilled beer and watch the waves surge ashore over the thousands of young beach enthusiasts sunning themselves!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Typical Sydney stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but definitely highly touristed. Still a needed sight to see while in Sydney a cant miss

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If your a tourist it’s a few restaurants and pubs around , a lot of people walking around and at the beach was a good vibe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful.....crowded!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful but also very very crowded. we were there on a Saturday and there was little place to move. We still spent several hours there and had a great time. Please keep an eye on your tweens and teens as it is easy to get lost. Take a lot of water, umbrellas and maybe your boards. Also sign up for surf boarding lessons early as the time is determined by the waves. Options are limited.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even thought the beach was really busy as it was New Year's Day,there was still plenty of space to spread you towel and catch the rays, take a dip or watch the surfers. The iconic life guards were in abundance,  Being a smoking free beach it was nice to find a cigarette free beach, in fact there was next to no rubbish on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, be smart about public transit options
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So the beach itself is great, lots of space even on a hot summer day.  When we were there, the part of the beach closest to the ocean was obviously the most packed however the back half of the beach still had plenty of real estate to go around (and we were there on a summer Saturday).  Lots of kids but can easily be avoided due to the ample space.If you intend to take public transit, do yourself a favor and begin at locations where most don’t or you’ll be standing for a 20-40 minute ride depending on where you get on.  To ensure you get a seat going there, get on the bus at circular quay.  Coming back, walk to the far north end of the beach first, and then get on the bus.  Going there, if you take the train and then get on the bus at Bondi junction, it’s standing room only.  Similarly going back, if you get on the bus at the south end of the beach, all the seats will already be taken.An option if you don’t want to sit on the actual beach is the iceberg pool located on the southernmost end of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: New Year’s Day visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It seemed such an iconic way to spend New Year’s Day at Bondi beach - oh my goodness so crowded  !Unbelievable numbers and I truly think it’s not even the best beach !Just the most famous - haha Fabulous people watching and still a must do if you come to Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First time to Bondi Beach. Cold sea water and fine beautiful sand. Spending half day morning at the beach with nice cool weather. Suited for surfing than swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had to go to Bondi you couldn't come to Sydney and not visit Bondi. The sand was beautiful, the sea more suited for surfing than swimming but the lifeguards were definitely on the ball at all times keeping you fully informed as to safe swimming areas etc. We spent a lovely day there soaking up the sun,  beach beds umbrellas etc in abundance - cost for three beds and one umbrella for 65 dollars (approx £30). Lovely restaurants and a good amount of shops. All in all a lovely day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach but be prepared for how cold the water is.  Lots of cafes and shops makes for a great day out

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the place for new years.It's a good beach, saw plenty families there. The water was apparently cold because, it was getting cloudy when I reached there.It's one of the must go places in Australia.I enjoyed the white sand. I'm sure you'll enjoy.  And yes, there are lifeguards at the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach itself is pretty but right by a noisy road. There is no shade anywhere. On the day we visited the surf was dangerous and water was freezing. Maybe we just picked a bad day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very busy!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is nice, but there are far too many people there, luckily I hadn't arrived just to see Bondi!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top 10 beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having beautiful beaches at my country home and visiting the most beautiful beaches in the world I can say that bondi is almost perfect. The sand is soft and white as you can get, the sea is a beautiful blue BUT the water is freezing cold. That is the reason I don’t give it a 10 but an 7. Despite that, the vibe, sand sea and restaurants around makes it great. Be aware, if you go with kids, that there are ton of topless all around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On our first trip to Sydney we wanted to make sure we made it ti the famous Bondi Beach. We were not disappointed. We enjoyed a lovely lunch at a beachside cafe and watched those brave enough to go into the water. Although it was December and summer it was still pretty cold out there.Still there were lots of people on the beach and in the shops and cafes. Wish we had more time to spend out there as it beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most happening beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There a few beaches along the coast but this is probably by far the most crowded and most happening. Despite being crowded, you can still find a spot to lie down to get a tan.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Different
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were here for a short visit but this place was packed. It provides lots of options for food and shops. Although it wasn’t a very hot day the beach was packed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk from Coogee to Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: End the coastal walk at Bondi for a cool beer but holiday crowds everywhere and weekends make areas like Bronte full. Enjoy lunch or dinner at the Coogee Pavilion though!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Over rated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful and popular beach, but there are others, just as and more scenic around Sydney that eclipse this one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was dirty and not enough toilets and the toilets where dirty and smells plus no toilet paper would never go again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family Friendly Must-See
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We packed our stroller full of beach gear and took the bus out here from downtown.  Worth the visit.  Very clean and something for everyone.  Our 2yr old splashed in the little pools at the north end.Be advised it is very busy and the change rooms are kind of gross.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's just the name Bondi which brings people over here. Found this place to be an average beach. The cafes and bars over here a little expensive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and walking track
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked from Elizabeth Bay to Bondi Beach, which is a beautiful 3 hour walk, and then carried on along the Coast on the South side of Bondi Beach before coming back to the beach itself for some sun bathing. A great day in a beautiful area. People from Sydney are lucky to have such a beautiful beach at their door step.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful long stretch of beach.  Good for boogie boarding, light surfing and sunning.  Even some shade under trees by parking lot

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful  beach of Sydney. A must visit place. Spent few hours there with my teenager daughter who loves beach and difficult to drag her out from there as it’s quiet amazing beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Place for Having fun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Diving with the Waves will take a lot of fun. You feal Save under the eyes of the lifegarde team. The Beach is clean and you have the opportunities for restrooms, shower facilities and changing Rooms. They are many possibilitys for having Drinks and Snacks .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded, dirty, and with polluted air.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This grossly overused beach is most time extremely crowded, dirty with litter, oil slicks, and ash.  The overheated crowds are also known to be rather hostile.  Polluted air from the city and the nearby burning national parks tops off the experience most people would prefer to miss.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very easy to get there, bus 333 from downtown Sydney, goes really often. The beach was just a perfection for the a day of. Very soft and sad and nice waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Clean Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just love this place - it’s the perfect spot for some time out of the hussle of the City Parking can be a bit challenging so take the puck transport into Bondi - very walkable too

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach & Art Work alongside!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is the iconic Sydney beach and well worth the visit. It has cafes and restaurants upstairs along the beach (mostly expensive). Right next to the beach, there is a pathway, where you walk along and can see the art work of different artists and is worth a visit. The beach is hot fav among the locals/surfers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach,  heaps to look at, well paroled,great eateries and coffee shop within walking distance

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, beautiful, beautiful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the bus from Taylor Sq. to bondi beach a journey of around 25minutes and arrived at this beautiful site. Pristine sand and a vibrant ocean combined. It wasn’t the busiest of days but it was truly lovely. Well cared for, no rubbish in sight, lifeguards on station, it was great.  There’s a walkway at road level if you don’t want to get sand in your toes. But you’re at bondi, get stuck in! Plenty of souvenirs and eateries of all description to choose from.  If you choose the right time this would be heaven.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It has to be seen and it has to be visited.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Iconic yet a beach for everyone. In Italy it would be covered in beach umbrellas and roped off into sections by the beach mafia. Not in egalitarian Australia. Here it is open for all comers and it is a joy to look at and to admire. Sun bathe - no one seems to pay any attention to the Cancer Council mantra of “slip, slap, slop, slide” though perhaps more “slide” on the designer sunnies than the rest. At least they have got rid off the oil dispensers that used to be available to ensure skin cancers got a good chance to develop. Or surf or just play in the surf. All tastes and all styles are welcome. But why does the council allow cars to park on prime space overlooking this stunning bay and beach? The bus service into the city is frequent. The beachfront businesses cater to most tastes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its a beach.  Dont put more into it than you should.  If you really wanted beaches you wouldn't be in Sydney.  It has good atmosphere and is overhyped but it has an amazing trail system to walk and free toilets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Soft sand, clean, & clear blue water!  Great place to relax. Great location within walking distance of food/drinks and shopping.  It can get crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome waves, great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came with kids and they immediately started swimming by the surf area. A local let us know that there's some bad rip-currents on the beach so we should stay "between the flags to swim." The waves were large as far as I was concerned and the kids (age 10) had an absolute blast playing in the surf. There was metered parking and the day we went, we were able to get a spot without any problem but it might be a hassle on busy days? There's lots of shops and restaurants right next to the beach and surf shops and people giving lessons and stuff. Great beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Be prepared that it is VERY busy on a Sunday. From casual holiday makers, older people doing their best, to rude runners trying to do a PB. If you are a tourist from overseas, last can be a bad reflection. It will be a good idea to limit running at certain times of the day/week. Take water and wear flats. Not ideal, but not impossible, to go with a pram

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in the world?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach proves its one of the best in the world. The sand is clean and deep. The girls are gorgeous and many are topless. You want food and drink? You’ve got fifty choices with a ten minute walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not bad
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I suppose this is a must visit place. Areas could do with an upgrade but the beach  is wonderful and clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well not as big as I expected. Didn’t look too safe for swimming with young children. Very big waves. A good place to hang out with friends though and the life guards were plentiful. Good bars and restaurants also

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach.  Lots of people swimming and surfing.  Be aware that if you do want to swimming in the water, there are flags marked on the beach.  That is the safest area where there is no riptide.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really cool beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really cool beach. It’s famous, iconic and touristy. Very beautiful views. A bit overpriced on everything. But still must visit when in Sydney!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best part of Sydney!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were told by many to avoid Bondi beach that it’s too touristy and there are better beaches. I’m very happy we ignored that. We actually did not care for the city of Sydney and felt that Bondi was one of it’s redeeming factors!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing walk if you like beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the 6km walk from Bondi to Congee beach and took us about 3 hours at a leisurely pace. Could see people fishing, surfing and swimming along the way. It was very windy and even though it was summer, we hardly sweated! Would recommend using sunblock :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I just had to visit Bondi whilst in Sydney and was so glad I did. Lovely clean beach and when we visited it was pretty quiet due to the weather not being the greatest. However stepping foot on the iconic beach was a great moment and one I will never forget.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach - tourists everywhere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see, very touristy but iconic. Glad we came but still prefer Manly beach worth a breakfast or lunch visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must see lovely and clean just what I thought it would be like after watching it on tv didn’t see the life guards lol lots of places to eat and drink enjoy a lovely glass of wine looking out at the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach to go to.  Has a lovely expanse.  Is a good beach to look at - either from close up or from "high" up nearby.  Am sure it is also a good beach for swimming.  I've seen it a few times when I visit Sculptures by the Sea from year to year.  There are good cafes nearby from which to view the beach while eating/drinking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect sand, clean and friendly.  This is one of the best beaches and water in the world...see for yourself.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great day on this iconic beach , not as amazing as I thought but clean white sand and a good day out Mike uk

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very impressive beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Obviously the most famous and iconic of all the Sydney beaches. A beautiful and long stretch of coastline boasting beautiful spots for surfing and swimming.One has to be conscious travelling alone with valuables - as it is more crowded and has more tourists. I had no issues but if you want to lock away your possessions you can only do so until 1630 at beachside facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi's up!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is an Aboriginal word for surf, and there's plenty of it on this beach. While the northern end is gentle, the southern end has a rip current known as Backpackers' Rip. We chose to forego swimming or sunning and just viewed the beach from overlooks near Notts Avenue and looking back from the Bondi to Coogee Beach Coastal Walk (see my review, "Put Bondi Beach in your rearview mirror").One of Australia's most visited tourist sites, Bondi Beach hosted the beach volleyball events at the 2000 Summer Olympics. Near the center of the beach, Bondi Pavilion hosts major festivals. There's a fascinating oceanside swimming pool at the southern end (see my review of Bondi Icebergs Swimming Club, "Wave pool -- literally!").TIPS:* Consider taking a city bus from the Central Business District. It's easy, though it can be crowded with other beachgoers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEST BEACH IN SYDNEY
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our party of 6 adults and 2 kids from Singapore selected Bondi Beach in Sydney to get a feel of the sun,sand and sea available in Sydney. We were very happy with our day trip to Bondi. The beach was popular with swimmers and surfers. There were good food options. We were lucky to catch performers near the Heritage Pavilion .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Average
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I found Bondi to be very average - it was probably a great beach before, but now it's just too full of tourists. The shops were overpriced, and I didn't find the beach itself to be particularly beautiful. It is really the type of the place where you go to be seen and to say that you've been - if I go back to Sydney, I would probably go to Manly instead.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic and beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the worlds most iconic beaches and it certainly doesn’t disappoint. You can get there via the 333 bus from the city or T4 train to Bondi Junction and then either the 333 bus or 380 from the bus station just outside the train station.The waters are unbelievably clear and so blue. I’ve never seen anything like it. The sand was beautiful and the beach incredibly clean. There are lockers, changing rooms and even a place to hire things like towels, chairs and buy sun cream. There are also some great places to eat.We went on a warm week day and it wasn’t very busy which was fantastic. A must when visiting Australia!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fine
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great sand now with umbrellas and loungers for rent.Excellent lifeguard beach coverage.All in all looks great, but can be windy, as today.Crowds are large, be warned if you are catching the bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I didn't go swimming because I didn't have time, but the area is super cute and had tons of places to shop and eat. I walked around and took pictures. I wish I had the time to go swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit beach in New South Wales
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went there for Sculpture by the Sea and it was amazing! The sun was shining and everything perfect. You should visit this place if you come to NSW

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While on Sydney worth the trip to see the beach! Stunning panorama , good shops and restaurants. Recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Superb ocean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a superb ocean beach.  Big, wide and handsome and so close to the centre of Sydney.  A great beach to visit, whether you’re planning a swim or a sightsee.  If you’re doing the latter, make sure you take the paths up to the headlands.  The view back to the beach or out to the pacific ocean is superb.  It’s also a short walk to the more compact but also very beautiful Tamarama beach.  Don’t miss this fantastic experience folks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An icon of Australian culture.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is not a lot else to add about Bondi Beach. A large sandy beach, surrounded by coastal footpaths, parks and suburban streets. Very popular on a warm sunny day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see Sydney beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dont miss out on Bondi - easy to reach Bondi Junction by train, and then a quick bus ride right to the beach. The surrounding area is beautiful, the beach is huge and clean, and there are many costal walks you can take to surrounding beaches. It's famous for a reason!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hot and sunny with an great range of amenities, shopping and eateries within a 2 minute walk from the beach. Easy to get to on the train or bus from Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MUST SEE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to see the Sculptures by the Sea and walked from Tamarama to Bondi past all the sculptures, we caught bus 381 from Bondi Junction to Tamarama and it was an easy walk along the beautiful coastline to Bondi Beach, we had lunch at the Bondi Icebergs which has a magnificent view of Bondi Beach and the food and drinks were delicious, we then walked past all the Murals on a wall right opposite the Beach which are great to see, if you swim here make sure to swim between the flags, Bondi Beach itself is stunning and a must to see if in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach with Chill sea breeze
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Bondi beach is picturesque with different colors and lovely surf. In September the sea breeze was real cold. Nice place to surf for the surf lovers. Really refreshing to sit there. Lot of eateries around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Aussie beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see if visiting Australia and whilst in Sydney. The beach has good facilities and cafe. The sand and surf can be really busy, and A lot to view, boobs out is legal. Good skate park and parking, does fill up easy on nice weather days.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My Daughter & I loved Bondi Beach & we are due to go back soon. We went by train & then took a bus. There is also some great shopping to be done in Bondi Junction.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed Bondi Beach even though it was windy and a bit cool (Spring in Sydney).  The Bucket List cafe was OK - beer selection fair compared to California.  All in all we thoroughly enjoyed Bondi.  We did have trouble getting the parking meter to work; however, Urs left a note on the windshield and 4 1/2 hours later - No ticket‼️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dissapointment at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were so excited, but when we arrived there was no where to park at all.  All carparks where full, and many of them you could only park for 30 mins.  the beach and dining looked amazing, but it was absolutely packed.  we were so stressed driving around looking for a spot we ended up leaving and got too see nothing.If you go, go super early as going mid morning like we did is a nightmare

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excitement, fun, security
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beach for all ages and tastes. It even has a seawater swimming pool. For those who do not want to swimm there's a beautiful lawn to lay down and apreciate the view and the sun. Many restaurants, stores and cafés will make your stay much better. The lifeguard team is the best in Australia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this iconic beach went by train from central station to Bondi junction and  then bus 333 very easy to do , just get an opal card to tap on and off not expensive . You also get to see the surrounding area . Spent a beautiful morning sat on the beach watching to surfers and even ventured in the see my self a bit on the cold but with the experience. I suspect it can get very busy at a weekend . There are lockers, changing room and showers (free to use ) at the Bondi beach bath building in the center of the promenade. I think lockers were 4 dollars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First visit, not much surf happening but enjoyed the walk along the track of the Sea sculptures there for a period of time. Breach is beautiful white sand, we tool a walk along to Tamarama and Bronte beaches and overall I think Bronte was nicer. Bondi just has the name

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After hearing about Bondi Beach for many years, it was great to finally see it.  The beach is wide and sandy, perfect for sun bathing.  It also is famous as being one of the best places to surf in Australia.  When we were there in the late afternoon, there were lots of surfers catching long, slow waves.  Bondi is easy to reach from Sydney via bus, Uber or taxi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day trip from Stdney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took transport for Sydney for those who are maybe planning to do the same!We took a train from Martin Place to Bondi Junction - cost $2ish and took around 15 minutes on an Opal card (which we purchased in the train station at a kiosk for €10). We then took a 333 bus from stance A in the bus station and it was another €2ish and 20 minutes bus journey. We were dropped right beside the beach. The actual beach is as expected; super busy!!! The only facilities we used were the toilets before leaving. The ladies toilets needed a good clean! I would not have put my bag down for love nor money - but they do the job and no charge is applied so can’t complain TOO much!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney's most famous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not a lot has changed over the years.  This is still one of the most popular beaches to see and be seen.  It has nice sand, surfing, a salt water pool at one end (8aud per person) and the typical tourist stores/bars you find at every popular beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great brach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow what a great place, pure white sand, blue sea what more could you want.   Just as appears clean and locals appear proud of it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is one of the most famous beaches in the world for a reason! From the environment surrounding the beach to the culture around the beach, everything adds to the vibe. Just grab a drink from one of the surrounding cafes and watch the waves hit the icebergs pool, take a walk along the beach or just be there. It's wonderful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Smaller than I thought
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After all the hype I heard of Bondi Beach, it was disappointing.  Smaller than I thought and not a lot to do.  A few restaurants and bars, but nothing else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach filled with locals and tourists.  Wonderful white sand, lots of surfers.  Also lots to do around the area.  Different places for food, drinks and shopping. A fun place to go for the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice to see it again after many years
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fifty years ago as a young fellow I spent a fair bit of time here so it was great to visit again,This time though we just came on the hop on hop off bus with friends from Canada.It was a lovely sunny day with a slight breeze, perfect weather to show off one of Australia’s iconic beaches to overseas visitors.For a Tuesday there were quite a few people about and as usual there were plenty of surfers out there doing there stuff..The beach and water still looked inviting, still a nice place to enjoy, where have all the years gone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is the beach with the reputation. It's really nice, clean and protected by life guards. Popular with the surfing set but there it's not a great deal going on. That's not to say that there is anything wrong with Bondi, but if you want a bigger beach with a bit of life going on around it Manly is the place to be.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful View for 5 Minutes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you’re a surfer, I’m assume you will rate this 5+ stars. If you’re a tourist in October, it’s a beautiful walk that you can enjoy for a bit if you don’t mind the very strong wind (bring a sweater/jacket with a hood) and the time/effort it takes to come from the more central parts of Sydney. The shops along the beach front rip you off, even saying that a small bottle of water costs $2 then take $3.5 when you pay. The view is definitely worth it for a few minutes it but keep your expectations low for this famous beach and you’ll enjoy it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just as I would have Expected.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a day in Sydney and wanted to take in Bondi Beach.It was all that I expected except the day we went it was very windy.Great beach with lovely lawn areas.Plenty of eating houses and shops on one side of the road.Took the 333 bus from the city which took us all the way Always wanted to visit and put on my bucket list and now done.Well worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun and surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best beach in Sydney :PFinding parking can be a bit tricky during peak season but it is worth it. Clean and pretty beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I travel frequently and Austrailia was NOT on my bucket list. It is NOW! Bondi Beach was so beautiful, the water is the prettiest blue/green, the scenery around it was amazing, I couldn't get enough. The city itself is not as clean as Manly Beach, but the ocean is just breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice views,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very nice & clean ..Has long trail for walking around the Beach with gorgeous views,  clean bathrooms, restaurants and life guards

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its free and as Sydney as you get.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great stop for a beach day out, watching the people trot by or exercise with the best of them.  Bondi has always had a free and easy life style approach and nothing much has changed throughout the ages.  Great Cafe, Restaurants and Pubs along the front with some of the best cake shops I have ever tried.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold but pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went yesterday and it was really windy and cold, but some were still simming and even surfing! Nice sand beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holidays
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not as impressive as we thought, worth going though. Lots of cafes, shops and bars.Easy to get too as local buses very regular and not expensive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely way to spend an evening ,eyeing the sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A short journey from Circular quay, its a lovely way to spend the evening and enjoy the sunset. Vast expanse of clean sand and clean water with chilly wind blowing across. Not crowded, with cafes nearby. The wall art along the beach is worth the visit , just walk along and enjoy the beauty of the painted walls; the messages  conveyed ,or merely the beauty of the scene.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really nothing special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After visiting Camps  Bay in Cape Town I keep thinking that not much happens on Bondi BeachRelatively dirty, kids, dogs, food, drinks on a small beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy popular beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was crazy busy.. and it's not even summer. Soft white sand with shops and eateries surrounding the beach. Train from CBD was busy and trying to catch 333 bus was worse. Buses got filled up in no time, so queued built up very quickly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picture perfect beach. Not.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Terrible parking situation, beach is always packed, too many backpackers and tourists, way overrated.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beauty!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Coming from a country without beautiful beaches , i really enjoyed the stroll down bondi beach, peaceful n calm ( mayb bcause it wasnt d peak period..). The best part is that me n wife had a chance to see a whale flippin in a distance.. it was just.. wow! Theres also a fitness corner to mingle, n lots of pictures to take along the way..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: To See and Be Seen
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Talk about fine granulated sand, talk about a beautiful ocean with strong surf, talk about surfers, the wind and the sun. Talk about a famous beach and when you talk about Sydney, one place definitely comes to mind: Bondi beach. And from it, everyone will think of all the adjectives that could properly define the place. From people who have the chance to go Down Under, it is not only a must place to see but in a proper perspective, it is a must place to be seen. Not much can be said about Bondi Beach that haven’t been written yet. It is so famous that even sharks, if allowed, would like to frequent the waters of Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Exactly how it is seen on ‘Bondi beach rescue’ show.Great opportunity to see popular lifeguards off show. It was clean and has green park area to sit and small cafe on beachside.All kind of shops across the road.Paid parking expensive but very close to everything and still worth it.so close to get too, its a must see if visiting Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too Crowed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to the beach to see what all the hoopla was about. Well I saw for myself. The beach was overly crowded for me. Trash cans were overflowing. The bar on the beach was packed. Life guards were doing an excellent job of pulling people out of the ocean. Groups of people taped off areas for their people so that area did not become public. Come early if you want to get a good parking spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous beach of Australia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No visit to Sydney would be complete without a visit to the famous Bondi beach. Even though it  was cold and raining, it didnt deter our enthusiasm. Car drive was around 7-8 km from Sydney and was comfortable. Beach was empty because of the weather. However surfers were there surfing inspite the cold. The curved beach itself is beautiful and we walked quite a distance. Lining the beach are boutique shops, cafes and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful coastline - easy walk along cliff tops from Tamarama Beach to Bondi. Stop into Icebergs for a drink and enjoy the view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better than I expected
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have to say that I thought this would be a commercial type beach and it was not !!!! Stunning beach great surf loads to do great restaurants. Awesome

What a beautiful beach. Golden sands and plenty of room. I’d imagine during the summer season you’d not get moved on the beach. Plenty of places to eat and buy supplies from one of the many businesses down the shop front.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach brilliant
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited bondi beach on a Sunday morning the beach is really clean water inviting spent all day there then we wanted something to eat at teatime we found ourselves in the bondi RSL  we where made to feel really welcome great.food and some really nice Austrailian ex service personnel  thankyou from a pomm ex forces

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see when in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach/coast line, popular with surfers! Plenty of cafes along the front. Lots of sitting areas for picnics too. A really easy bus ride from Sydney. A worth while a trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Obligatory tourist stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came to Bondi specifically because of the show Bondi rescue. Littlest son is a massive fan. So took the 333 bus from Sydney central to Bondi, took about 40 min. There was a few souvenir shops and general clothing and food shops. Bondi beach itself was average. I’m from Perth and our beaches are a lot cleaner and bigger with clearer water so I wasn’t awed by the beach itself.Son was happy to take pics at the lifeguard tower but didn’t get the chance to meet any of the boys from the show. Oh well. I also stopped at the bondi beach gym for some photos on the fanous Bondi pole. That was really good.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The nicest thing in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was blown away when i was hereExpected it to be just a beach but more than thatBondi Beach is extremely big with lots of pple, surfing, picnic, jogging, walking their dogs, etcProbably cuz from where im from, beaches are much less activeSpent quite a while there and took the walk to coogee (though i gave up less than halfway uz its too far)Love the view, also at the iceberg club, the swimming pool is fantastic with ocean wavesc itting against itThe walk to coogee, started past the iceberg club and with amazing view of the ocean, mountain walks along the coast with its up and down slopes. Can be tiring and the wind is strong hereThe place feels very chill, like a beach town but clean and nice waters and sandBeen to several beach towns like phuket or krabi in thailand, this place is much betterWent to a cafhe(the famous Trio) for a ch ilax coffee breakHighly recommend this place if you are in Sydney, this is the place that makes me like Sydney over Melbourne Too gorgeousOh and if you think my expectations might be too low, I went to Hyams Beach (the famous beach for its white sands), i prefer this much MUCH moreeeeHope my review is helpful for you, like if it doesl

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mr. Adrian Lee
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love the Mother Nature of this beach, the sensational movement of the waves makes soothing and a sense of serenity to your ears. It gives a sense of peace and tranquility both mind, body and soul. However, we were not able to take a proper picture near the beach as it was heavily down pour with stormy windy temperature. Hence, we are grateful and thankful for the opportunity to be here ☺️☺️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Mind-blowing experience, very beautiful beach, lots of options for food and sports. One should definitely go for surfing if visiting Bondi Beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach & Boardwalk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped at Bondi Beach on a tour. Beautiful beach & water. Nice stroll along the beach boardwalk, a few stores & restaurants. If not doing beach or water activites, you won't need more than one hour to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kite festival
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The day visited was the day of kite festival on September 8th. A lot of people and traffic jam. Hundreds of kite flying along the beach.It was fun to watch.  Bondi Beach is beautiful. Worth visit and spend half day here while you are in Sydney. Buss 333 from city center (across Sheraton Grande) takes you here without transferring. You need to buy Opal Card in advance to get this bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Do it! Dare the walk from Bondi Beach to Coogee Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you enjoy ocean breeze, pounding waves and a hearty 2.5-3 h walk then you'll be in heaven.Great coves and beaches at every turn, lean surfers& beach bodies and amazing views.It is a bit strenuous, while always on a cement foot path you do end up "pounding the pavement ". But there's a beer once you enter Coogee! (Check out the Coogee pavilion!)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to swim and relax
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love to go swimming in the ocean almost every morning in summer. Bondi Beach is an excellent place for that. It is quite safe, there are lifeguards. It was great to see them practicing. There is also a number of good eateries and gift and other shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach surrounded in coffee shops and restaurants with some phenomenal street art! Must visit in Sydney!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice place to for beach walk and for a swim, during summer it so crowded,  views and the ambiance it's a good experience, beachin the city

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Festival of the Winds - Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This fantastic festival is sadly only one Sunday a year at Australia’s iconic Bondi Beach Sydney. This year it was Sunday 8th September from 11am till 4pm . Amazing day with hundred of balloons circling and gliding in the near perfect conditions above the stunning surf and sand that is always beautiful Bondi. Kites are for sale and kit making classes are also offered on the day. A huge stay of food stalls with outstanding food of all varieties on offer . The event is free to attend and live music and entertainment is on all day. People are welcome to bring their own kites to fly however you can only fly kites on the grass area above the beach as the sand is for the professional displays only. Parking of course is always difficult and is metered in most areas but there are lots of buses available for transport from the city and various outer suburbs. Highly recommend this fabulous outdoor activity.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beach, plenty to see and do, walk along the beach or just sit on the grass and have a picnic, there is tables there if you wish. Plenty of food outlets to choose from right across the road, there is also a Woolworths near by if you wish to purchase food there, and if you forget your sunscreen Chemist warehouse is just across the road. It’s a day for all ages, but you have to pay for parking, so I recommend public transport which takes you right to the beach, regardless what direction your coming from. Swim between the flags for your safety.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Bondi in August. it was a beautiful and serene visit. the view was breathtaking and despite the cold weather. i am very happy to have visited. clear blue sea, beautiful beach and great atmosphere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Staying in the CBD, we took a bus to Bondi as the trains were not working, but it was easy, an overcast day we had a lovely time walking around and had a beautiful breakfast at the Bondi Bathers overlooking the ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, famous, touristy beach, very crowded with tanners/swimmers/surfers/strollers; a great place to start off a walk along the ocean with plenty of photo ops, people watching, volleyballers, incredible views, rock formations, different beaches/neighborhoods, an oceanside cemetery, etc. Sugarcane, in Coogee is a great restaurant for lunch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Baecation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had an amazing time at Bondi beach with my lover. Victor was quite friendly and ensured we enjoyed our stay

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Many people come here to surf, the view here is beautiful and can walk from bondi beach to bronte beach, and you can see the bondi icebergs pool on the way, it's nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazing place to have a swim or just relax and bake in the sun. There is also a trail that close by that you can follow if you are interested in going on a calming walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach and Place to Learn Surfing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While not as big as Manly, it has a casual feel with an amazing beach. It is a great place to surf because the waves have a nice break between the shallow and deeper water, and are very consistent with wind patterns. The water is also calm enough to swim in, which I personally enjoyed.There is also a Pavillion that you can store your stuff in if you want to take a sudden dip. There are also numerous shops, parks, and restaurants to explore. It has a San Fransico feel but more laid back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was able to experience both sides of the Pacific Ocean within a span of 24 hours. The waves were beautiful. I was able to see the pool that gets its water from the ocean. I've wanted to see that for years. There were some restaurants and little shops close to the beach. The street art was beautiful as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most famous beach of Sydney!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is best known for its waves, which make it one of the top surfing destinations in the world. Bondi is also nice for strolling, sunbathing and swimming. Despite its popularity (and its plentiful souvenir shops and surf and fashion boutiques), Bondi maintains an alternative, edgy feel. Topless sunbathing is allowed here as well, though it's mostly limited to areas without children.Almost universally, it is said the 6-mile trek to Bondi is a must and that the beach is one of the most beautiful in the world (to claim a prime spot on the sand, it is suggested to arrive early). Many former visitors also recommend setting aside time for one of the region's coastal walks. Both the Bondi to Coogee walk and the Bondi to Bronte walk offer superb water views and relaxing spots for picnics.TRANSPORTS: the best way to get to Bondi Beach, is by train or bus. From Central Station, you can take a train bound for Bondi Junction and then catch the 333 bus to reach the beach. You can also pick up the 380 bus from Circular Quay. Limited parking is available, though driving here is not encouraged. A visit to Bondi is free, but expect to pay for area amenities like food and souvenirs. Public bathrooms and outdoor showers, which are located throughout the beachfront area, are also free to use.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice-to-see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our family took us here and we were told it was a pretty iconic tourist destination so we certainly were intrigued.  It is a lovely crescent-shaped beach with quite strong waves.  Nice to see the outdoor gym where the men were soaking in the rays while working out.  A nice-to-see on my list.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Suprising small
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As one of the most famous, at least outwardly, beaches in australia i was expecting to be blown away; and while it was a very nice beach, clean and with lots of people for a fall day, i was also really smaill i walked the entire strech, including the lookout cliffs in 40 mins

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking around
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach to walk around, a lot of tourist though but still worth to go. Wonderful restaurants along the corner. Must see

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It may be overrated to some. But trust me you'll be in awe when u see the clear turquoise blue sea and the fine smooth sands. Cos its winter the beach wasn't crowded. U could do picnic at the grass patch watch surfers do their stunts. Besides spending your day at the beach. Trek a little to the top to have a spectacular view of the beach and sea! Its absolutely amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, views and restaurants, be careful of the water!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Coming from Adelaide, South Australia, this was my first time to Bondi Beach and was happy to find it was actually quite peaceful during August. There were plenty of cafes with a variety of food available, not so much on the esplanade but still worth visiting. As a fairly experienced open-water swimmer (no surf-life saving experience however), I was surprised at how strong and powerful the waves and currents were and I got dumped heavily on my head while body surfing the waves, this happened between the red and yellow flags! So if you are not a competent swimmer I would recommend to be VERY careful in the water and DEFINITELY swim between the flags!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but as per locals.. GO TO MANLY BEACH
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went looking to experience the hype... well thats where it fell flat. Great beach ummm but thats all it really is. Maybe because where we come from we blessed with many great beaches. Found it overcrowded and really not.that.great. Shouldve listened to the MANY locals that tried to convince us to go to Manly Beach. Sadly we already booked a few things we couldnt cancel. Should've listened...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a nice , clean beach, easily accessible by public transport, however we had driven down in our rented car.It has some nice cafes nearby. It’s a great place to spend some time. It wasn’t very crowded in August. But I have seen better beaches, and after all the hype, was a tad disappointed

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing half day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach deserves all the accolades showered on it ever since I can remember. Great surfs, fine sands, good restaurants nearby. When I was there in August, it was not crowded. Sydney’s mild winter makes it a lovely time to visit and chill, in my opinion. We did not swim, but could play in the water.To get to Bondi, we chose to take a ferry from Circular Quay, Pier 2, to Watson’s Bay (explored the Gap when we were there) and from there took bus 380 to Bondi. For the return trip to the city, we took bus 333, a 40-minute bus ride. All the trips were paid using the Opal card. It was a great half-day trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty but very crowded!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was great to go to Bondi Beach and experience this beach, but there are much better beaches that don’t have as many people. It was so so crowded when we went.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfer’s Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Bondi and this is indeed a good place to enjoy sun and beach, especially to surfers. Lots of cafe’s and food options in the area. A good view can be witnessed on the rocky part of north bondi. Must visit if you are in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good transport links
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the bus from the city suburbs to Bondi beach. It's a very commercial main street with all the fast food chains like McDonalds and beach stores selling clothes and sun cream etc. The area is a crescent shape around the bay and the shops and main road follow that shape.   Lots and lots of young people  fill the area for the beach scene and surfing.   It's quite a meeting point for young people.There were no waves the day we were there.It reminds me of Newquay in the UK ...... very similar indeed.Great to visit and tuck off the bucket list.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surf Beach, street art and pavilion
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I came early morning - on my way to get coffee. The people here right now would be die hard Bondi Beach goers. It’s in the middle of winter here, sunny, but cold. More than 50 surfers on the water, and many others walking on the beach. This is an iconic place - beyond the hype there is a serene tranquility to this place. From the surfers, to the dog walkers, to this who are just walking, relaxing, and talking. Morning rituals. Afternoon excitement. Evening spectacle. Bondi beach is a must-see attraction when visiting SYDNEY.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful, and please go to see the infinity pool at the south side. But its clear this is the place where most tourists and backpackers go to, as the bars/restaurants along the boulevard are a bit on the lower segment, with lots of home- or pennyless people hanging around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best beach at all! Do not miss!!!! We arrive by bus 374. Nice walk on the rocks. A little bit windy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great waves, clean air, nice sand, but if you are going to swimm take every warning seriously, because waves are very strong. Lufe guards are very effective in warning people to be safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is great, albeit crowded. The town surrounding it is dirty and rowdy, and selling chep touristy merch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a fantastic day, walking round the area, great fish and chips in the traditional chip shop , would recommend to anyone visiting the beach to stop by for great food, the beach was incredible and clean

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing as ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great walks  scenery and places to eat.  However  would say it can get busy. The beach is amazing with beautiful  views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good, but ...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Firstly, beware the naming of 'Bondi Junction' station. It really is a good 40mins walk from the station to the beach and the station itself is below a shopping centre (what everyone would go to Bondi for, right?). That said, you can still use the Sydney city bus tickets in the area and some of the buses will take you back to Circular Quay.As for Bondi itself, it's a lovely beach with good amenities, lots of people and a friendly atmosphere. I wasn't there at the height of summer, so I may have seen it when it was a bit less packed than normal ... yet, it was still busy!But ... it is only a beach. Once you have got over standing on the famous Bondi beach, that really is about it. There are great walks to be had, especially to the south, which make you realise that there are better beaches close by. Worth going to, but once you've been there, you've been there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach and surrounding coastal walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's famous for a reason, because it's beautiful!  Even in the winter time you can catch some hits of warm sun so definitely visit!  Surfers are out every day, and the surrounding coastal walk, restaurants, park, and town are a GREAT way to spend a few hours (or more) in Sydney.  I came from Circular Quay, took the train (for the first time) and it was pretty easy.  Just buy an OPAL card, the trip is like $3 all told.  You have to switch one time, then get off at Bondi Junction.  From there grab a cab to the beach (too far to walk).  Have lunch, watch the surfers, do the coastal walk (another must do), watch kids in the skate park, walk on the beach, check out the waves crashing into the Iceberg swim club (to the right of the beach), and have an awesome time at this spectacular beach. Place must be insane in the summer.  Will definitely come back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful day at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always a great place to visit so long as there isn’t too many tourists around. Stunning beach and water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of those places you just have to go!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi was WONDERFUL! There are tons of people laying out, surfing, walking, running, playing games, you name it and it's here!Our favorite part was the murals where we had a miniature photoshoot, so awesome!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited on a rather cold & windy day, so accept we didn’t see Bondi Beach at its beast – although I have visited in the summer (39 years ago) – the sand is beautiful, golden & soft and importantly clean & litter free. As out of season visitor numbers understandably low but still a good number of surfers braving the cold – as was the odd intrepid swimmer or two – far braver than us! Definitely a place to visit to tick off the “Bucket List”, I’m sure in the height of the season there will be quieter less busy beaches & coves to be found for those in the know. However, I would definitely recommend a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfer's paradise perhaps
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our visit was during winter time in July, not much people but can feel if during summer it should be crowded. Easily to travel by taking 333 bus from circular quay.
