reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful well known beach 8km from Sydney. The beach and views are beautiful. Definitely worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, plenty to see and do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are probably many more beautiful beaches in Australia but to step onto Bondi Beach and soak in the atmosphere has to be a highlight of a trip to Sydney. Take some photos, have a snack or drink in one of the many cafes/bars to suit all tastes and budgets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfer’s beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not a place to swim properly, as you can in other different beaches. Good to surf and enjoy it from the sand and the surroundings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went there in winter but it was sunny nice day. The beach is beautiful white sandy. There are lots of resraurants. Also can easily change in the bathroom and provides lockers. Along the beach, tgere are lots of beautiful street arts

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Exhilarating
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After lunch nearby, we decided to spin by Bondi Beach as the weather was nice. As it was winter time, there weren't too many people swimming but there were still lots of people at Bondi- walking, sipping coffee, enjoying the breeze. Still a great way to cap an afternoon . And it's free!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place to spend some time!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful scenic view: checkGo surfing: checkFood options for meals: checkSecluded spots for romantic times: checkClothing optional: checkSpacious lawn to lay down: checkAll in all a great spot to visit and spend some quality time in Sydney. Well connected with public transport.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go for the Coastal Walk, otherwise Manly is Better
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is great, and it’s the beginning of the coastal walk that travels through Tamarama, Bronte, and Coogee beaches. If you go to do the walk it’s totally worth it. There are small surf shops and plenty of lunch/dinner joints with great beach views. If you’re planing a full day at the beach, I prefer Manly beach. It has more shops/restaurants and it’s just bigger so you can spread out more. Plus the ferries take you straight to Manly where as you have to connect into Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A wonder down under
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The world renowned Bondi Beach is a truly iconic.  The sand is fine, and silky.  Swimmers, and surfers share waves.  I recommend public transportation, as parking is limited.  Restaurants and coffee shops are within walking distance.  People from near and far visit the numerous public events held year round.  A playground area for kids, a public pool, and community room are within the beach confines. There are a number of shops nearby to purchase a souvenir or two.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, clean, and I could sit all day, people watching, there are all the services from buses,taxis, plus shops, restaurants etc. The beach it self was lovely and clean, and well look after with the life guards on patrol 24/7. Great for families.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Winter @ Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I thought visiting in winter will be fewer people and I am wrong. There are still a lot of beachgoers and surfers while the Sun is up. Parking is always full, be prepared to park a few streets away. I will always try to drive along the beach to look for parking.They are smart by organising activities during wintertime. They have ice skating, and ferry wheels cater tourist like us who don't want to swim in winter. The view of Bondi beach/sea is fantastic and multimillions dollars property seat along the horizon. There are shopping and restaurants across the road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Popular beach for people watching
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We made a quick photo stop and had a quick stroll along the beach. The beach seemed to be clean and was not too crowded on a weekday. There is no shade on the beach, a sun umbrella will be needed for an extended stay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 1st Visit to Bondi Beach, Australia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Train and bus guides thru the internet were of great help.  Brought my  rubber slippers, which I eventually tossed in my bag, because walking barefoot on the white sand beach is relaxing.  Skating rink was just for merry-go-skiing due to limited space. Grumpy resto, just a few steps away from the shore, offering a glass of wine per pizza or pasta was a good deal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of many beaches in Australia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of many beaches in Australia. It's a little crowded there, especially during summer. Manly beach is much more quiet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped here on a tour for about an hour and ended up deciding we needed to come back the next day.  We came back by bus the following day, which was surprisingly easy from our hotel.  We rented a towels, chairs and an umbrella from a stand on the beach. The rays are STRONG here so wear extra SPF and re-apply way more often than you normally would.  The beach wasn't too crowded, but it was windy.  It was a great relaxed day at the beach and would definitely recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I finally got the chance to visit this beach after seeing it on TV and shows all the time. Love the unique street art they display on the walls - adds a hip vibe to this iconic beach. I went during winter and it was still nice enough to take a leisurely stroll.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a beautiful beach even in winter. Lots of people walking around enjoying life. Lots of things to see and do around Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach is lovely and well worth a visit. It is not as big as I thought it would be. There are a few shops and cafes too. The beach was lovely and clean and there are plenty of benches you can sit on to enjoy the views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great attraction! We took the underground to Bondi Junction and the bus from there! It’s beautiful if you just want to eat and walk around or if you really want to surf! Amazing environment great place!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Small But Beautifully Formed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a lot smaller than I thought, both ends blocked off by outcrops as opposed to the miles of golden sand I expected. Still very nice though. I was only there for a couple of hours (a stop on the hop-on hop-off bus which is a convenient way to see it) in "winter" (about 22 degrees) but there was a nice vibe to the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach is famous and it sure has reasons. Crystal clear waters and a magnificent view. A must visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My Favourite Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I absolutely loved the time I spent at Bondi Beach. The beach is so beautiful with pristine water. I was lucky that I went on a weekday so it wasn't as busy. Perfect place to sit and relax. When I came back a second time I spent time exploring the parks and view points to the north and south of the beach. Definitely recommend a trip to the Icebergs Club to have a drink on the terrace!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Second time better than the first.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My initial visit to the Bondi Beach was underwhelming and disappointing, as it was with a bus tour in the cold rain.I decided to give it another try on my last day in Sydney.  It was the Queen's Birthday Holiday and the weather was beautiful(for the beginning of Winter) , giving me an opportunity to experience all of the hype that I've heard about Bondi Beach.  There were picnics, barbecue and music on the grassy knolls, skaters, volleyball and street art in another section, surfers at sea and sunbathers sprinkled all over the place.  The water was warm,  the sand/beach was clean and the vibe was super chill. Plenty of restaurants and shops surrounding the area.  It was a great way to spend my last evening in Sydney.  Can't wait to return.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, especially at sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a really great beach. Perfect for us kids, tho waves are really big so parents, always keep watch. Other than that, it’s really great. Unfortunately, I didn’t get to take photos as I was having too much fun. Also, there are murals there that are really nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beachgoers delight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you do nothing else, jump on the Hop on-Hop off bus and make a stop here.  Even if you don't plan to go on the beach it is a very large park area and although quite busy it does not detract from the ambiance of the area.  Many small shops and dining establishments (both local and large franchises) are located on the walkway along with a variety of clothing and other shopping options.  Even if you don't dip in the ocean, it is a great place to people-watch and view the beach and surrounding area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach But Busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Bondi Beach as part of a day trip to see the Sunday markets and then walk the coastal walk. The markets were nice- crafty and we then walked past the shops lining  the main road before walking along the grassy promenade and up past the pool. Nice views of the sweeping beach and lots of room despite it being busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved it. Wish we could surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved our visit to Bondi Beach. The sand and surrounding area was spotless and there were more than adequate places to eat drink or just watch the waves roll in with surfers on top.We took the bus from Circular Quay and 45 minutes later we were at Bondi. The beach was not as long as we imagined but we loved our visit there and wished that we could surf to take full advantage.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t have too high of expectations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a great place for sunset and viewing the iceberg pools, but wasn’t amazing. It’s a nice beach..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Christmas Day on Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely a tradition for many to go to Bondi Beach on Christmas Day. The beach was crowded with locals and visitors alike, but we expected it to be. Lots of people in red Santa hats. No surf rentals today and many shops were closed, as well. But, overall still a great day to enjoy the sun, sand, and sea! We took the city bus from our hotel in Sydney CBD. Make sure you buy an "Opal" bus card for visitors at a convenience store because they don't sell tickets on the bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I never expect a park and beach that is so well maintained, clean and well facilited for visitors. Love the grass field and seating area, everyone enjoying the sea view and hang out at the park, so relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pristine sand!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a half day tour of Sydney and its suburbs leading to the Bondi beach. The beach was pristine with the white soft sand totally taking the cake. There are a lot of shops along the beach for eating and shopping. We had not packed shorts for the boys so wanted to buy some there but nothing was available for the older one (9 years). There were some for the younger one (6 yrs) but they were super expensive. We ended up just having ice cream and leaving. All in all a buzzing place with lots of people surfing and generally sitting or walking etc..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Place to Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you’ve watched the show Bondi Rescue, you may as well check out the place the show is filmed! Beautiful beach, plenty to check out around it including some awesome artwork and not too hard to get to. But seriously, if you can’t swim, stay out of the water, it’s easy to see how people get themselves into trouble so easily when you visit the beach and ignore the lifeguards signage and warnings. Stay safe and enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Looks like a great area to living right next to the beach. Have a lot of restaurants and cafes nearby  but they can Be expensive

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Use as a start point for coastal walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a nice beach but there are many better beaches to spend a day at in Sydney. Use Bondi as a starting point for the coastal walk to Coogee beach. Transport tip: Try and get the bus from the city to Bondi, this will be the easiest way. Avoid the train to Bondi Junction- this is a lot further away from the beach than you would expect, you’ll still have to get another bus which you’ll have to queue for ages for and will be packed before it picks you up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for tourist
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Be prepared for the high volumes of people visiting the beach. It is a pretty large beach with a good number of bars and restaurants around for good drinks and eats. This is a good beach to visit when it comes to outsiders not familiar with Australian beaches. There are other beaches to go to however if you want something simple and easy Bondi beach is the place to be. There's even a skatepark for advanced and amateur skaters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very nice and beautiful sandy beach.  There are plenty of shops and places to eat and get ice cream.   They also have a place to clean off from the wonderful beach activities with toilets and showers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t Miss
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was in Sydney and on my last day went to Bondi. At first I was hesitant because people had told me it was trashy. Glad I did not listen. I did the Coastal Walk which was breathtaking. Please don’t miss this. On the walk which is about 2 miles are cliffs, beaches and surfers. On the way back I ate in.Bondi Iceberg.It is right on the water overlooking an infinity pool, cliffs and the beach. What a perfect way to end my trip to down under.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I found Bondi Beach to be what I expected—a beautiful beach with lots of surfers. I saw one or two surf schools along with solo surfers and groups of surfers. They were fun to watch. I got a coffee and sat near the sand to people-watch, and it was a beautiful way to spend a morning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach Boardwalk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The boardwalk on Bondi Beach is very dog friendly. Dogs cannot go on the beach but a lot of shops and restaurants have food and water dishes out for dogs. It was great.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sweet beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved it here! It's very friendly, good amount of people, loads of cafe, ice cream, restaurants, dogs. Direct bus in to the city to the beach. Half way from Westfield shopping centre. Lovely area, clean beach :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Bondi Beach on a warm day and it slowly began to flow with people. The beach is beautiful and is manned by professional lifeguards. The strip of shops near the beach offer local shopping and opportunities to eat. Toilets and lockers are also available. The Bondi Icebergs Club to the side of the beach is also great for swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular day, clean beach, lifeguards and a busy beach. A typical Bondi beach day. We wondered the esplanade and took in the sights.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I spent just part of an afternoon at this iconic Australian beach. It was May, so the beach was hardly bustling with activity but there was enough going on to pique our interest, mostly surfing activity.The beach is remarkably clean. We had a quick fish and chips and beer at Lush on Bondi. The food was great but the ‘music’ was too loud and inappropriate for family dining. We actually walked past and checked out the other options because of the noise but decided Lush was the best choice in spite of it. We certainly could have enjoyed a whole day at the beach. Had I brought the appropriate gear and had the time, I would have taken a dip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is a very good place to hangout and chill. Loved it. There are plenty of place to eat as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach in the suburbs of Sydney. Prestine and beautiful, nice for a stroll even along the shore and taking in the breathtaking views from Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach and town. Plenty to see, eat, and do. Make sure you make it to the market if it is open while you are visiting. The iceberg pool is also a must see and great place for a drink overlooking the pool and ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi to Coogee Beach Coastal Walk - A walk well worth taking!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful walk and well worth taking if you are able to do so. Bondi Beach itself is amazing. No wonder it is a world-famous beach. We watched many young people learning to surf the waves while children played in the water. The walk from the main beach to the lookout point (going past the Icebergs Ocean Pool where there is also a dining room & bar), also has many photo opportunities along the way. This walking trail seems to end just past the lookout point. However, go online to get the complete circular trail that takes you back to your starting point. Time well spent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It was a good day to visit this beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were thankful that it was sunny enough to visit Bondi Beach. It was warm enough. Upon arriving, my Better Half and I marvelled at the smoothness of the sand, the strong winds, and the people enjoying the surfing. This is a good place to be when it is hot and sunny and you’d like to go for a swim. This is our first visit to Bondi Beach and we were thankful to take lots of pictures and videos of such a gorgeous place!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manly Beach > Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We used our Opal cards to get the bus to Bondi Beach. This was very easy. Once arriving at Bondi Beach there are plenty of shops around the town, you can visit the swimming pool or the beach. If I’m honest Bondi Beach is a bit of a tourist trap. I preferred visiting Manly as there were less crowds and I thought the town and beach was nicer. There is also more to do in Manly e.g walks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So beautiful, easy to get to from city center and getting there by Big Bus was 30 mins. Enjoyed strolling the beach on a beautiful Saturday and grabbing lunch before heading back. A fantastic place to relax and unwind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must place to visit!!  Ps don’t forget your swim suit!  We planed on staying on the beach just a short time but it was sooo cool we spent several hrs.  The beach was awesome the water amazing.  Truly cool shopping cool stores right off the beach.  Please if you visit in AUSTRALIA please go to Bondi you will always remember this beach...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cooler beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its autumn, if you prepare ur thongs and thinking lying on hot sunny beach for tanning then u r coming in a wrong time. Its freezing n windy....dont get me wrong....the beach is beautiful n clean....its just we came in wrong season...i guess

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better than expected!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach with so much to do and great places to stay. We rented an apartment just a block from the beach, but there are plenty of hostels and other places to stay as well. Tons of shopping, restaurants, and other amenities to meet anyone’s needs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beach worth visiting!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach itself is amazing but more then that there are amazing walks that are stunning. I would recommend the walk bondi to bronte but if you are looking for something lower key and less tourists you can try coogie beach which is about a 5 min drive away also really nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Big waves💕
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Thrilled to walk on this fabulous white sandy beach and watch the waves.  Clean change rooms and gift shops very close by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's a Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nothing much to shout about. No Pamela Anderson. In fact nothing really here at all. Some surf for the surfer. But not much else. Water was ok, but not really suited for families with young children. Disappointing. Restaurants, not great either. Maybe just out of season. But generally area looked dated.Coogee beach on the other hand. Much nicer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A good place to relax and eat
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you enjoy the busy beach then this is the place for you! It seems pretty safe, the sand very soft! Heaps of places for you to buy souvenirs, eat or drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Plenty food and sun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place for a sunny day. A lot of sun, water and little shops to buy your lunch. Nice boardwalk along the beach. Gorgeous place - a must visit while in Sydney. Use hop on-off bus, blue line to take you there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: lives up to the hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this was part of our bus tour. coming down the hill into bondi and you can see how pretty it is. of course it was crowded but it doesnt take away from the beauty of the area. lots of cafes everywhere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic Anzac Day spent laying on beach and swimming. Great cafes around, lots of lifeguards around including the boys on Bondi Rescue. Unfortunately Icebergs pool was closed maybe for maintenance ? Deck lounges and umbrellas available for hire on beach. Worth a visit !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Yes it is with Manly the nearest beach from Sydney but it is crowded.Manly is mich bigger but you will have to go by ferry so.... Bonny is reachable by bus.Nice and regular surfing waves. Good surfing schools and junk food. But the city has no interest and the parking is dreadfully expensive. You will feel secured with the life saving guards. Nice hôtel and salted swimming pool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a must do for everyone visiting Sydney. Such an iconic beach and also take a dip in icebergs pool a short walk along the beach. The eateries across the road are amazing as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfing.....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I don't know how to put it there is something between me and surfing. It's a beautiful place to go to. Look at.and wonderful place to surf.surrounded by good number of surfing shop,souvenirs shops,clothes,food,wine what not.We had a great time because it just drizzled for a while and the skies cleared just before we started swimming....I hate to say this it would be injustice if I don't give a honest option  so here hear... the beach is well maintained,space for working out, very active life guarded very safe but the trash cans gave an awful stench for quite a distance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited on a quiet afternoon.  The beach is lovely but can get busy with surfers. It's a nice walk along the sand and had a promenade where you can sit and have a drink/food.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had to tread foot in the world famous Bondi Beach 🏖 on our visit the wind was crazy so we ere unable to stay on the beach for long, the waves we’re great though, a wonderful bay worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do for an undying experinence of Sydney.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Vast stretches of sand and sea with perfect views of the wave catching surfboarders can never be explained but with Bondi. The rock pool is so exciting and the cliff around is fabulous during sunrise and sunset. The surrounding parade is perfect for shopping and the restaurants are classy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great surfing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is wide and despite a lot of people it never seemed too crowded. It’s such a fun and laid back beach community. Food is closes by and you can spend the day chilling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a spectacular place, pictures don’t do it justice, sit by the water have someFish and chips or walk along the beach front, either way you’ll love it. Parking is very expensive right on the water so I suggest finding somewhere close by if you don’t mind a little walking

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Way better than expected
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came out to Bondi on the Big Bus trip, and it was well worth it. Gorgeous sand, idyllic setting, loads of shops (not sure what they all sell as we didn't go in) and some great places to eat. Very much an unexpected highlight

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No bondi lifeguards but still great scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Arrived on a beauty winters day.  Was windy but very sunny and just beautiful.  Walked round the headland  to Bronte beech and what a great walk.  Saw dolphins in the distance.  A great walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crazy busy, bustling beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So spectacular beach, Sandy, great swimming, unbelievable views.  Not a 5 for me because it is so busy... it is truly crazy.  If you are in your late teens, early twenties this is the place to be.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most touristic and crowded beach of Sydney East and one of the most beautiful when there is no one around. Surfing is awesome in winter or with dangerous conditions and horrible in summer. There are probably as many surfers on the wave as towels on the beach. Anyway, everybody loves Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEACH
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a MUST to visit when visiting Sydney. You just need to feel the waves and ride them. Very nice surroundings with nice restaurants and surf shops....a place to relax and just enjoy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 40 minutes from city center
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You will find the iconic beach of Bondi.  Enjoy a swim between the flags or view the ocean club pool on the waters edge.  Good restaurants and shopping along the main road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Beach that is a must to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great Beach that is smaller than I imagined and in the height of the season could be very crowded. A great selection of bars and restaurants and an atmosphere one would expect in this Iconic place. Close to Sydney so worth a bus ride.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach Food Markets on Saturday mornings
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Do not miss out on this amazing food experience.  Saturday mornings at Bondi Beach Public School there are many food stalls, fresh vegetables, butchers, flowers etc.  My favourite breakfast is the corn fritter stall who pile up your plate with the most delicious food.  2nd choice is the falafel stall.  Everyone then sits on the oval enjoying their feasts and contributing to the amazing community feel of the event.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach yes, but slightly overhyped, expansive and crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Yes, it is a nice beach, it is a "must see" in Sydney, is located "in" the city, which is pretty cool. But from my point of view and compared to what i had heard before this beach was a bit of a let down as it was not as iconic as it is advertised. The shops / restaurants around the area are way overpriced (Sydney is an expansive place anyway, but here i paid +30$ for 4 soft drinks - in a supermarket) and the tourists are more than willing to pay. Crowds of selfie-tourists spoil the scene, i didn´t feel the desire to stay longer than a few minutes here. Instead I highly recommend the smaller and less visited beaches along the Bondi-Coogee walk, like my favourites Tamarama and Coogee Beach, and Bronte Beach as well. If you are more into privacy, great swims, natural / scenic landscapes and nature, then take an extra walk of only a few minutes south of Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place for a sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walk down to the beach or down on to the rocks, beautiful place, lots of parking, public toilets available, bars and restaurants near by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The  water is chilly out of season but a great place to  walk and unwind.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This iconic beach has 2 very different faces – teeming with people on the sand and in the water during Australian summer but virtually abandoned in winter and only a few walkers and surfers to be seen. The  water is chilly out of season but a great place to  walk or relax. No problem finding places serving food or coffee – many restaurants, takeaway places, and shops at Bondi. The Bondi-Coogee coastal walk is refreshing in the cooler weather and there is a swimming pool located to the side where you can swim there for reduced price. For us Bondi Beach (what a great name) was a must see but we found it was a bit smaller than imagined - also glad it is close to Sydney and its attractions.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there in late April and very few people were swimming (I guess the place is overcrowded in summer time). The whole area is clean and a beer in the Pavilion is very refreshing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the blue route on Big Bus Tour and hopped off at Bondi for a few hours - the beach is fab., clean and water quality great. Walked the Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk and what spectacular views of the many beaches along the walk - something you have to do if in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I was disappointed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After all the hype about Bondi beach I was expecting something quite spectacular. It was quite small and virtually no one was surfing. There was an art display at Bondi pavilion but nothing much happening.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not that Special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Made the trip via public transport from City, fairly straight forward but involves train trip then jumping on buses to get to Bondi. Nothing quite like being packed on a bus like a sardine. As for the beach, well yes it's pretty. But wow, tourists outnumber the locals it appears. All eateries were packed and had considerable cues & naturally argumentative customers were prolific. To be honest we we're glad to get out of there and back to the City. To be honest, much nicer beaches to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Went on a nice hot day and enjoyed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beach with great views. Definitely lived up to the hype. It was only a half hour from where I stayed. Excellent food along the beach area with places to shop too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Maybe we just caught it on an off-day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well, the rain most certainly did not help.  But it was still possible to see the sand, ocean, waves, and amenities that Bondi Beach had to offer.  And a really big pool.  And sharks.  Australia has its share, and them some, of our finned friends.It's human nature to make the best with what you have and this beach is pretty much just about the best (or nearly so) that Sydney has.  The Beach does have shark nets and, that all by itself, would keep my feet firmly planted on the sand.  We lived in California and we go to Maui, so we have been to many beaches where they also have sharks.  But just not so many and there aren't shark nets.  And just how effective are they anyway?  The skippers on the tour boats say they don't swim in the ocean.  These are the guys in the know; who is going to argue with the voice of experience?  But it is a popular draw, this Bondi Beach.  Make good use of the resources you have and enjoy them as best you can.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t Bother
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach with fine sand, where families seem to gather on the weekend to sun and surf. It’s like any famous beach and coming from California, U.S.A, I would pick something else to do.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After all the hype we wanted to see what this famous beach had to offer, when we arrived we were so disappointed, it's appears to be right next to a housing estate, the beach isn't that big and it was crowded. We turned around and went back to Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach - unmissable.  While you're there, do take a surfing lesson from Let's Go Surfing - they do a really good job of getting you up on your feet but also teach you about rip tides and how to carry your board without being hit in the face on the way in to the sea! For a great view of the beach with a drink or a meal, go to the RSL (Returned Servicemen's League) at  the North end of the beach (upstairs - downstairs is a different establishment).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfers Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most iconic beaches not only in Australia but in the world.. from surfers to hardy swimmers tackle the waves while sun seekers enjoy the sweeping sands.If the waves prove to be powerful or looks daunting then stick to the Icebergs outdoor pool which is stunning and is surrounded by the sea..The beach is also part of a coastal walk with stunning views and crashing waves on the mountains. With plenty of pubs, bars and restaurants to choose from. The beach itself is a 10 minute bus ride from Bondi Junction station. All good for families, backpackers to couples.Thanks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good for a relaxing stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was here during the Australian winter, so the usual crowds were gone - and it turned out to be perfect. The hour-long stroll was quiet and relaxing, and the view was not bad as well. Public facilities abound, and there's great coffee a few steps away!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite surf beach in Sydney because it is easily accessible and safe
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi o my fav surf beach in Sydney.  We know we’re tomalways get a free park a 10 minute walk to the beach.  Living I. Surry Hills, I sometimes jump on the 333 Express bus to Bondi.  It only take a about 20 minutes.  I prefer North Bondi where the crowd is a bit more manageable.  There are places to get sandwiches and drinks not too far from the beach.  It is always clean and people seem quite respectful of the beach at a Roth Bondi.  My favorite bay beach is Shelly Beach at Manly.  It is beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Been here many times, but there's no better view on a sunny day , so much to see lots of cafes , restaurants , shops to explore ,markets on weekends , walk along costs you nothing to enjoy the view,  have a dip or just watch  the surf and admire plenty of buses from city, start the walk along the coast from here, which goes from right of beach, call into ice bergs for a drink or meal lovely views from there.just come you wont be disappointed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand and Surfers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A sunny day to visit Bondi Beach.  Even with a chill in the air there were plenty of people out enjoying the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vibrant and lively beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved bondi beach! The vibe is definitely friendly and stylish, it attracts the most beautiful people and provides glorious waves for surfers. Lots of shops. Restaurants and bars around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy access by local bus service. Clean beach with soft sand! There are many shops to visit along the beach too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No seaweed. No sea shells. No rocks. Lots of fun waves. Beautiful sand. Chill atmosphere. Lots of local shopping and cuisine. Just a beautiful beach, clean and lovely!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely day when in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Got there on the tourist bus, which gave a great overview of the area on the trip and stopped every hour. It was super hot, did some beach time but also some better than expected shopping

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very picturesque beach with the nice clean sand and beautiful color water. Lifeguards on duty every day plus lifesavers on weekends. Nice beach to hang out and enjoy the view and day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach to be if you live here or are here for a holiday. Clean n visitors help to keep it up to it's mark. Great place to swim, to tan, to surf, to eat drink n party

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach to sit down on the sand and watch the ocean and people walking by. The ocean breeze is very nice and warm. Also, nice to walk on the beach as well. There are public washrooms and change rooms but really high traffic area. No shade. Really enjoyed just sitting at the beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nothing spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For 30 years, I've been wanting to be on Bondi Beach since a family member used to live in ydney and had always talked about this Beach.  I went with friends and we got there using the Hop On/Hop Off bus.  We went early December so it was not that hot yet. A bit disappointed as I expected so much more of this famous beach. We're from California so maybe ...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great visit to Bondi beach had a paddle in the sea and fish and chips in the picnic area with a cool drink great to say you’ve been.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must visit and see. Bondi is a place to be seen and to see. The beach has life guards and watch for rips in backpackers corner near Bondi icebergs. Bondi is super popular in summet and parking limit, is pay per park.  Has all the amenities and food outlet close by. Visit the guards on duty and may be filmed for Bondi rescue tv show if not get a photo. Beach apparel is very skimpy and leave not much for the imagination. Has excellent skate park and exercise area. Take a walk along the beach foreshore after a swim and look back and enjoy the views. Check out the graf wall Totally recommend a visit.😆

reviewsWithKeywords.title: At last I have seen it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I always wanted  to visit Bondi Beach, and at last made it but oh dear the weather was foul.    It was cold, windy and occasional rain, not what you see on tv at all.  There was hardly anyone on the beach which meant for us easy walking round, we saw the lifeguard station on Bondi rescue and took the obligatory photos.       But it was worth it and definitely a place to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful people, amazing beach. Wide beach and not too crowded. Changing rooms and bathrooms available. Many restaurants and bars. Great walk to Coogee.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Another iconic Sydney landmark that is well worth a visit is Bondi beach.. Clean plenty to do.. Place to eat and drink.. even a couple of markets on the day we visited.. Highly recommended for all the family..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not my cup-of-tea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for people who like crowded chaotic beaches and are going to one more from the crowd than the sand. The place is packed on a good day. Difficult to find parking. There are so many other, quieter, more secluded beaches available for the taker on the Australian coast that I don't understand why people just flock to Bondi. I had really wanted to do the Bondi-to-Bronte walk but turned away when I saw the crowds. Tamarama beach, a mile or so down South, is smaller, more picturesque, but also gets very crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice and sandy beach, crowds ok for a Monday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here on a Monday for taking a sunbath, cool down in the ocean and enjoy the view on the surfers. Is it crowded? Most likely on the weekends, for us on Monday it was fine. Public transport is available, parking limited. Facilities (toilets, showers)  are available, but frankly, these could be cleaner, but given these are public and free it might be acceptable. Also, lockers are available. The beach does not offer any trees or similar for a cooling shadow. Besides, the spot is nice for surfing. We enjoyed the half day and would come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic, but not a great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everyone's heard of it, and if you're in Sydney, you're bound to try it. Plenty of people, nice sand and gentle, sloping beach. No particularly beautiful sights but it's OK.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A “Must See” visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great seafront to visit with easy walking along the esplanade and an inviting beach to walk along or laze about on. Places to sit  and watch the world. Bars, shops and public changing/ toilet/ shower conveniences. A real buzz and something for everyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fifty Years Later
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband visited Bondi Beach 50 years ago as a young serviceman.  The beach is the same but all the high rises one block from the beach are new as well as some homes on the right side of the beach facing the ocean.  I found it to be very crowded, busy, very touristy, & expensive.  It was a walk down memory lane for him.  I’m sure there are other beaches just as nice but without the crowds in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy but a must do place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I arrived in Sydney for the first time 3.5 years ago and yesterday was the first time I visited Bondi Beach. I quite often enjoy watching Bondi Rescue haha so it felt a little surreal actually being there! It was very busy, which I expected, but it was still a nice chilled beach to visit and check out the amazing surfers! I went on a Sunday to make use of the cheap travel (got a train from Central Station to Bondi Junction then a bus to Bondi Beach) and the overall travel time was about 20/25 minutes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On our way to Australia we had to spend one night  in Sydney and for sure there was no better place to stay than Bondi. Strolling on the beach , watching the surfers , sipping a glass of wine while watching the colorful crowd goes by was a treat..... and the next morning after an early breakfast, taking a walk on the boardwalk , sharing the beach with the early surfers, the private gym trainers and there clients, the joggers was a sure way to get to see how people here adapt there lifestyle to the environment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach - meh
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super crowded, no white sands here. Shops had outrageous prices, restaurants were just okay; for the best food in town, I recommend the Sydney Fish Market (Head there instead). Skip Bondi, in my opinion.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: NIce beach but busy.....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a beautiful day and the place was packed.  However it is a beautiful beach and worth the ride out from Sydney to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Underwhelming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Heard about Bondi all my life, seen the TV program re Life guards etc. The reality is that it's quite small. The sand is lovely and yes there is good surfing but the town is a bit dated and not the beach front cafés , bars and restaurants I was expecting. Seen way better beaches, better beach resorts.  Just underwhelmed really. Don't get me wrong it's not bad , it's just not the experience I had thought it would be. Chatting to Australian friends they say it's a common reaction. Especially when it's absolutely rammed with people. Enjoy but don't expect nirvana.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the most iconic beach in Australia.  We spent a little time here and visited the sculpture by the sea exhibit that was going on.  There is plenty of sand on the beach so you will have no problems finding a spot to catch some sun.  The water gets crowded at times but its a good spot to relax and watch some surfers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a great time at Bondi. We really enjoyed the spectacle of the surfing, the beautiful people and the scenic views. The water was perfect for a swim.A must visit when in Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Two trains and a bus from Million's Point Station. Easy and inexpensive transit to visit this beautiful beach. Clean, lots of shopping and dining available. We had lunch at Lush on the beach. We watched the lifeguards in action and enjoyed the coastal walk. Beware the power of the surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: World Class Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see for any beach lover including those who enjoy tanning naturally. Reminds me of the California beaches out from LA. Great surf and plenty of wonderful restaurants and shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the nicest beaches in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach is the most iconic of all the beaches in Sydney, and rightfully so. It has a ton of different bars and restaurants along the water that you can sit at and grab a drink or food and they often have specials. It’s not usually too packed except on weekends, and is well worth a visit for the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, cool water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited for only an hour. Had a chance to walk the shoreline getting our feet wet. A lot of families and sun worshippers. The beach was clean and safe. Many surfers trying to catch a wave which were not very big this afternoon. Restaurants in the area but we didn't visit any.Would love to have stayed longer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk and a beer
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Felt I had to go to Bondi Beach why we was there had a walk along the beach to beach is not the best beach in the world is a little bit of height there was some swimmers out far we was waiting to get eaten by sharks but we didn't see any of that which was a shameWe did manage to find a nice bar across the roads where we had some beer and what still I do people pose in their cars

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi to Coogee good walk!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic views, great exercise (3 1/2 miles) 2 1/2 hour walk. Absolutely beautiful. Bondi to Coogee Beach is a very enjoyable walk ( taking bus back). Having reward at the Coogee Pavilion on Rooftop Bar!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach and Walk to Bronte
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the second time we’ve been to Bondi Beach and did the walk to Bronte and back, the last time was 11 years ago and this time we didn’t forget our camera.The walk is still fantastic with fab views of Bondi, Tamarama & Bronte beaches.The beaches all have parks adjacent to them with full facilities that’s required for a day at the beach.Tamarama and Bronte parks have free public electric grills which are just great, we cooked our lunch on the grill at Tamarama Park.The walk has some steep steps to negotiate.There are some wonderful eroded rocks along the walk that are great for a photo opportunity.Bondi Beach is great for people watching as there’s always something going on.We took the 333 bus to Bondi which runs from Young Street near Circular Quay, a single ticket costs $3.66 each way- you can’t use cash or contactless card on this bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a bit of hike to get there from central Sydney. It is worth the visit but the area is overated and a bit run down. The beach is very clean but crowded during the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most spectacular each I have ever seen. No hotels rising up over it. Absolutely beautiful. So much more amazing and less touristy than Waikiki. Pull up some sand and enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Rock Pools Make It.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The rock swimming pools built out into the sea are incredible and must be amazing to swim in with big waves crashing.There are some lovely boutiques one road back from the main hub and the best ice cream in the world at Anita’s.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I made the mistake of trying to go to Bondi Beach late in the morning on a Saturday. The place was packed and unsuccessfully looked for a parking spot for over an hour. I decided to re-visit early on Monday morning. This was much better. The sunrise was gorgeous, the water was blue, and the current was strong.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a quick trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach.  I scored a 4 because I needed to leave better marks for several Hawaii and Caribbean beaches I’ve seen. Large, beautiful, famous (if that’s your thing), with a bit calmer side toward the north end and surfing waves on the south side of the beach.  Amenities weren’t as convenient to the beach as I’d thought and souvenirs were very thin.  But if you venture off the beach to the boardwalk type area, there are a few restaurants and facilities.  Parking is every bit as bad as other reviews say.....be aware.  Pls let me know if this is helpful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Golden beach Down Under
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ah, the great beach for Sydneysiders, any tourists - local or foreign alike who would want to experience the best of Sydney. Though of course i'm biased for our own beautiful beaches back home, this one makes for a wonderful day out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go to Manly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi has the brand but Manly is 10 times the beach. We only saw and walked the beach for a bit as we hopped off the Hop on bus to eat, but this beach is a huge disappointment. Not great looking beach and surprisingly few services on the beach walk. I think we must have missed something. Manly is amazing, with three beaches and miles of restaurants and shops, everything you expect in a tacky beach town!Skip Bondi and go to Manly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Thoroughly enjoyed this beautiful beach. We took the “Hop on Hop off bus” from downtown Sydney to Bondi and that just added to the day. Beach is beautiful, clean, and filled with friendly people. We rented an umbrella and 2 chairs and settled in for a nice day. We ate at 1of the 3 restaurants there and had a nice lunch. Strongly recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited on a weekday so no crowds. The sand is a soft powder. Surprised at how cold the water was. Fun to watch children have their surfing lessons. Beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Urban beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful urban beach setting. The sand on this beach is just fabulous.  Like fine ground sugar/salt. There are concessions aplenty and it is easy to spend time here

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good On Ya!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: LUV Bondi Beach.  Pretty much amazing surfing daily.  Waves are awesome.  Gotta watch the kiddies when the waves break,  of course.  But it's a true beauty and treasure! Very large beach with incredible views,  so there's room to catch lots of rays of you're not into catching waves.  This spot if flippin gorgeous! Great shopping and all sorts of coffee,  ice cream shops,  etc., all around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bustling beach, big waves, great walking opportunity
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a bustling hustling beach. The day we were there, the waves were slamming and the sea was pretty rough. Lots of yelling and scolding by the lifeguards. I mean we almost jumped out of our skin when one drove up behind us and started barking out orders to swim between the flags. Absolutely gorgeous place. The walk from Bondi to Coogee is a must do! Each cone, lookout and beach is stunning or charming. Bring walking shoes and money to stop in some of the yummy restaurants along the way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney's Iconic Beach - Don't Miss It!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach, uncrowded on a warm summer day. We spent the day watching the swimmers, sun bathers and those with boogie boards. It sits surrounded by beautiful, ancient rock formations like nothing you have ever seen. Highly recommended for a day trip or an hour walk. Don't miss it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a must visit when you come to Sydney. Great place to go for a walk and have a beautiful breakfast while watching the surf. Take the coastal walk past the Icebergers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach worth visiting with private club entrance honoring fallen soldiers.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is a private club at end of Beach I think the initials are RSW(something like that) that you can enter as a guest with a foreign passport. It has a beautiful beach and is a restaurant and bar overlooking the area. The club is for fallen Australian soldiers with plaques and other items honoring their service from all the wars that Australia has been involved in. The food looked good. We settled for a quick dark beer from a local brewery.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfers paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although this is a lovely beach, close to Sydney, with sandy beaches and excellent surfing, it gets very crowded, as it is not that big, and it is very popular. The surfing is amazing, and it is a lovely place to visit, however if you want to spend time on the beach, be prepared to have very close neighbours on the sand with you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always warm and inviting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All welcomecat yhis grest beach.No matter where you go eveyone knows BONDI. Whether you are a babe or jyst a looker get the sand between your toes at thid beach icon

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Spectacular Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is not a large beach but it is beautiful with white sand, crystal clear water that has great surf breaks and several fun restaurants fyom which to enjoy the view. Lots to look at so go and enjoy for several hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: classic beauty, and lots of Aussie surfing activity
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The quintessential Australian beach, with sand, swimming areas and perfect conditions for surfers. Sometimes the surf is too wild for swimmers, though, as it was the day we were there. We watched the activity from the veranda of the Bondi Beach club, open to everyone, with good food and a wondeful birdseye view of the beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, many beachfront restaurants to dine in
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach.  Many people on the beach, very pleasant.  We were able to rent an umbrella to sit under as the sun was very hot, although the water was still very cold, even in December which is summer in Sydney.  We walked through the stretch of restaurants fronting the beach, and enjoyed lunch at Lamrock Cafe.  From there, we took a 30-minute scenic coastal walk across the beach side path to Bronte beach.  Beautiful views of the bay as we took an easy stroll along the stone path.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach offer spectacular view of the Pacific Ocean. Lots of restaurants available for beer and snacks. Music band plays music at night time l. Ample amount of parking available. Must visit place while visiting Sydney

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Stay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is what it is cracked up to be, beautiful sandy beach with massive waves to play in. The beach is well patrolled by the lifeguards and if you swim within the flags you will be safe and have a great time! If you would rather surf then there is an area designated for that, and you will not be disappointed either.I went in January which is there summer and the temperature was around 45 deg but they were having a heatwave at that time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too crowded and overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the big bus blue line here while in Sydney. It is a nice beach, but super crowded and you are only allowed to swim in a small area. Shops nearby are expensive and full of junk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: New Years Day !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited on New Years Day (for those of us from the northern Hemisphere, visiting a beach on new year's day is fun).  Biggest surprise was the VERY cold water.Relatively easy to get to via Sydney Rail/bus.Area around the beach is somewhat of a tourist trap, but that is to be expected.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lives up to its name
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came to Sydney on holiday and of course had to visit the iconic Bondi Beach. Being from California, I love my beaches.Bondi reminded me of home, and some of my favorite beaches. It has a fun, vibrant, easiness about it. Sure it touristy around the edges but down on the beach and in the water it’s pure joy. Surfers, sun soakers, people jumping in the waves, friends hanging out, white sandy beaches, that’s what it’s all about!Lifeguards on duty in all wheel vehicles cruise the beach to keep the less avid water folks close to shore. Safety is a priority here. Bathing tops, not so much. You can also rent umbrellas, chairs, boogie boards and wetsuits for reasonable fees. Lots of shops and eateries close by. We had great fresh seafood and chips at Bondi Surf Seafood Market. Well worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a tourist trap but is still a must visit while in Sydney. Beautiful coastal walks start here and it’s a nice way to start the he day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OMG
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s amazing. Lovely beach with amazing views. Had lunch at Iceberg which I would highly recommend. Took the hop on off bus from Sydney Central Train station. Do not miss a trip here if you are in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit the world famous Bondi Bech and bring your bathing suit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has golden sands and blue waters and safe to swim but stay between the flags. Great restaurants to suit all budgets and bring the camera. Shopping is great too and you may like to buy a new bikini or board shorts & or fabulous jewellery.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach near Sydney central
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can take bus no 333 from Sydney central directly to Bondi beachHave a good.restaurant in the promedane On weekend is vwry crowded

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Family Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our extended family of 7 stayed at Bondi post cruise as the teenagers wanted to experience "the vibe". We stayed for 3 nights and thoroughly enjoyed every minute. Our unit was situated only 100 metres from the beach. Walking everywhere was a breeze. Besides to have the ultimate Bondi experience you need to get amongst the crowds and walk around. An abundance of shops, eateries and drinking holes in easy reach. The summer markets on Sat and Sun at Bondi Primary School were a great distraction, with plenty of yummy offerings. The teenagers thoroughly enjoyed the beach experience, and they left feeling happy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach is the bomb!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is gargantuan in size and has beautiful sand and water. It also has a variety of places to eat, have ice cream, and shop. For a day of fun in the sun, Bondi Beach is a great choice. You will also have fun watching the surfers as they go about their business in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tourist beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is pretty nice but it is very crowded. Yes, it is a tourist beach. The beach is really big and there are many of cafes, restaurants, shops, and bars along the walk. It is really easy to get to the beach from the city of Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not impressed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have lived in Sydney all my life and can't understand what all the hype is about Bondi Beach. Trying to get there by public transport is not easy and if you drive parking is a nightmare! There are SO many other gorgeous beaches either in the area or in the north that are easier to get to and park. Seein them out unless your young and want to be seen.......

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy territorial beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Massive city beach,  a lot of different places to lay your towel, the toilets are not real Close so be ready. It’s gets. Very busy on a weekend so get your spot around 10 am. Swim between the flags is my suggestion especially if your not familiar with the surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Views, Lovely Powder Sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful cove-like beach with gorgeous powder-like sand. There is a grassy area where people lounged and enjoyed the scenery. Sunbathers were engaged in volleyball, sun bathing and swimming. There is a nice wide promenade for those who  prefer a non-sand visual experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A bit over rated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is iconic, we give it that. But the traffic is insane, there is people everywhere snd therefore not the cleanest beach ever.It is a surf beach so if you are not a proficient swimmer stay away from the water and only swim between the flags. With so many beautiful  beaches in Sydney I really think you can get a better experience elsewhere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach Clean Sea is beautiful Strong undercurrent so best to swim between the flags An iconic have to see beach Very busy in summer

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Bondi beach on the big bus tour. Well worth a visit but can be rather busy especially with surfers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved a day on bondi beach whilst travelling through Sydney. The beach was relaxing and entertaining with plenty local amenities in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surprised!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I must say I was very surprised when I visited Bondi Beach.  Because it has such an iconic status, I think I expected more!  It’s not very big and fortunately as we visited on a weekday, not too busy.  I wouldn’t like to go at the weekend.  Having said that I enjoyed the visit.   We also managed to find the best cafe we’ve been in since we arrived in Sydney 10 days ago - Trio.  Excellent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dinner on the beach at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Brilliant spot - not just cause family have lived here for many years - but it's got that small-town vibe, yet there's designer stores as well. A must is the gelato icecream store it's brilliant. They let you try various flavours and its a delectable treat. Loads of spots to have dinner including fish and chips with a cold beverage and a view of the beach... or any number of take-away stores.  So much action and swimming of course too, plus loads of surfers... so funny to see the surfers on the bus and trains with their boards (but only cause we walk to our beach round the corner in NZ) it's just their way of life. Easy to access by train and bus from the CBD or bus...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everything I Dreamed Of
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I’ve wanted to go to Bondi since I was a little girl and it did not disappoint. We took the bus from Circular Quay and upon arrival, it was a short walk down to the sand.The beach was busy the first time we were there but not to the point you were tripping over one another.It is imperative that you only swim in the designated areas to avoid dangers such as rips and surfers.The second day we were there, they were having some event with a bunch of tiny kids who appeared to be training to be lifeguards. It was amazing to watch these (in some cases toddlers), being put through drills.The water was much colder than I expected and very rough. You need to keep you eyes on the ocean and be aware of potentially crushing shore break.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Try to find a grain of sand at the place to be seen Bondi Beach especially on a long weekend.  Did the tourist thing and saw some of the Bondi Rescue boys, had a swim, people watched but not sure why the hype? . Australia is truly blessed with its beautiful beaches and coastlines.  Enjoy them all not just Bondi

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It is Sydney Iconic beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see for all visitors to Sydney.   There are plenty of places to eat and drink.  Finding a spot on the sand maybe a different story.  If driving you can always find a place to park you may have to walk a bit but the walk is pleasant and you are here to see Bondi and walking is the best way to see Bondi at its best. People watching at bondi is a great way to past time.... All the beaches along our wonderful coast are worth going to. It is a patrolled beach so swim between the flags you should be fine. Its not the cheapest area to buy food in but most of the places are with a sea view.(Beach View.)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See when in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a 20 dollar away With uber This nuce City and Beach us a must With many Nice restaurants and grea surfing If you Are into that, and great Big Beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun but crowded and expensive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As a famous beach that draws massive flocks of tourists, you can imagine that there isn’t much space. Good luck finding enough open sand for your gaggle of friends to each pitch a lawn chair. But the beach itself is quite beautiful, and if you go on the off season, it’s actually not too bad.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, you can hire beach umbrellas and chairs. Shops across thed road, Woolworths sell great freshly made sushi. Happy hour at bondi hotel good valu also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Special Beach in Australia  but very ordinary
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Australians have a love affair with Bondi Beach. Do not blame them because this is among the best beaches they have for safe swimming, A semi circle beach between residential or commercial areas on both sides, this beach does get very crowded on a summer day but provides an opportunity to swimmers and surfers to enjoy the ocean.This beach cannot compare to many white sand beaches in Africa in places like Seychelles, Mauritius, Tanzania and Kenya where swimming can be done with no risk from predators.Munir D.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean pretty beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We actually liked the vibe of manly beach a lot better. The day we went unfortunately the weather wasnt great, cloudy, cold and extremely windy so it wasnt crowded at all. We did a very long walk and walked down to Bronte beach along the coast. Not a bad walk but it was so windy when we went was blowing me over. Walk took about 45 min to an hour one way. The beach itself is very clean. There is a place with a changing room and restrooms. Lots of shops and restaurants. There are lifeguards and a station if you get injured.  There is a place to rent chairs, surfboards etc but they RIP you off if you go at the end of the day. It is $10 per chair for 3 hours so we rented 2 chairs and then they said oh we are closing early at 4 so you only have an hour 1/2 but they charged us full price! Wasnt happy about that.  The bus ride from circular quay takes a very long time due to all the stops. We went back to manly for a 2nd visit instead of coming back here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not as good as you think it'll be...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is iconic and billed as a must see attraction when visiting Sydney but sadly for me it didn't live up to the hype. Yes there's golden sands, amazing surf and beautiful weather but there is also massive overcrowding (to the point you can't find a space to sit on the beach), litter and loads of obnoxious gap year backpackers. I'm glad to have ticked it off my bucket list but would recommend Manly for a much better beach experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyed walking aling the boardwalk and the clean sand. Many stores on Bondi Road for drinks food and miscellaneous. Lots of drinking water taps and bins to put garbage. All in all very enjoyable and free!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most famous beach in Sydney. Huge and crowded but definitely worth visiting. It's nice even to take a walk or have a drink in nearby caffes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What’s not to love
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Recently enjoyed a few days at Bondi Beach.Great safe beach, thanks to all the lovely lifeguards.Lovely area to walk, swim & have a meal.My son got to meet quite a few of the lifeguards ( Bondi Rescue fan) which he loved.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEST BEACH EVER
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a must when visiting NSW the people are so friendly restaurants are amazing and something for everyone taste and budget water was surprisingly very cold  was very surprised that everything closed at 9pm even on NEW YEARS EVE

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just what we expected.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent three nights in an Airbnb. Walked everywhere. Beach was great. Felt very safe. Would be great if the locals put some time into their neighbourhood (cleaning up bins, rubbish on side of roads,mowed nature strips).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice and fashion beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible views!!!! You can take hundreds of photos!!! Too many people almost every day in summer. Difficult to find a place in the sand A lot of surfers ... Take the Coastal Walk: it is amazing!!!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Iconic beach, cool scenery. Sea was had a fair amount of weed in places. Lots of shops and bus stops nearby so easy to get to. Worth a visit if you’re a tourist but lots of other beaches that are nicer near by such as Manly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi busy...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably not the best day to go, New Year's Day... it was busy but also beautiful and the weather was hot, hot, hot. Make sure you wear something sensible on your feet and take a hat. You can rent umbrellas and sunloungers as well as lockers but the later it is the higher the likelihood they will be sold out. The water was cool, but good fun, and there are always a good mix of people. Worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great beach with a wide range interesting people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having always wanted to visit it was surreal to finally be on the famous Bondi Beach. It is a nice place with a great vibe and a wide mix of characters on show. The lifeguards are all very friendly and have a tough job on a busy day. i'd highly recommend a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overcrowded . . . and not that clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The famous Bondi Beach - used to be the hang-out for sun-lovers, surfers and families to have their picnic.Now it is simply an overcrowded piece of sand with the smell of sewerage gently wafting up from the waves

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The epicentre of Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not the best beach for surfing, but definetely a top spot for everything else. Even the 333 work really good. The vibe is so unique that I'll be difficult to find a similar place in the world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really nice beach near Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this beach is really nice and full of life. It's definitely worth visiting and spending some time there. some great restaurants and cafes nearby where you can experience local stuff

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Evening stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We decided to do the mandatory visit down to Bondi late in the arvo to avoid most of the heat and crowds, which paid off. Nice peaceful afternoon just watching to world go buy on the steps and from one of the restaurants as sun set. Will be back for a swim one day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice enough beach but nothing out of the ordinary
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don’t go here with any high expectations of anything particularly special - at end of day it’s just a very busy beach. That said it’s a nice beach and very popular. Water was warm and lots of people were swimming and surfing. Also lots of life guards on the beach so you feel safe when in the water.The town of Bondi offers lots of shops and restaurants/cafes!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great spot to visit. Recommendations below!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went in mid January which is the tourist time of the year. Watch out for the weather since that will make or break your experience. The beach has male and female changing rooms, showers, and restrooms as well as stores to purchase Bondi merchandise as well as food.The beach does have topless tanning, so that’s just something to be aware of. Most of the ladies that do are appropriate about it and often do it far from the water.To get the the beach using public transportation, recommend using an Opal card and putting at a minimum of $10 AUD. Take the rail on T4 to Bondi Junction Station. From there, take the bus to Bondi Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The beach to go to
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A trip to Sydney would not be complete without a trip to this beach.   Some touristy stops and great people watching.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see if you visit Sydney. Such a beautiful beach. It is a Great place to have a swim under the watchful eyes of yhe famous Bondi Rescue people. There are so many options for  food at Bondi, it is hard to make a choice, but all were very busy. A good sign of quality. There are a few nice places to walk with great views and some great spots to sit under a tree and take ot all in. Make it if you can

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Sydney beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Outstanding beach in Sydney, easily reachable by train to Bondi junction + bus connection. Beautiful public art displays of murals on the walls. Very clean beach and great eco-awareness. Swimming in lifeguarded areas only. Lots of restaurants/cafes--recommend "The Bucket List" for a lunch stop (burgers, fish tacos). Highly recommend the Bondi-Coogee coastal walk--it's breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came on a 30 degree summer day. Very impressed. Beautiful views, soft sand, lovely waves, nice place for the boys to catch some waves on their bodyboards. We rented an umbrella and 2 deck chairs. Lunch was at Campbell Parade. Everyone left feeling happy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect beach, very clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Somebody else said that I walked onto the beach and forgot I was in Australia. This is a great beach very busy yet plenty of room, well protected with life guards and good facilities around. Loads of room to play ball games, run around have fun, we hired an umbrella and lounges which were pretty well priced and boards for the kids, the waves rolled in , then the wind dropped, it was perfect, everyone had a great day. Thanks Bondi , we will return

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great escape
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After going for 3 days no stop at Sydney we took a couple of days to enjoy our vacation and run to the beach is only 30 minutes away from downtown Sydney the blue line of double decker stop but if you ready want to enjoy the beach stay at least a couple of days is beautiful taxi cost less than $40 Australian dollars from Sydney Beach is beautiful but the water is super cold even in December

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi bliss
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First time visiting, and I forgot that I was still in Australia!  It was s amazing, right down to the magnificent water and beach, to the inviting green grass sitting area. The ambiance is perfect summer tunes. Parking is the only down fall, but still won’t stop me from visiting again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderfull campus beach.High waves. Close to the strip and nice atmosphere. Busy with a lot of people but very nice

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fun day at the beach, so easy to access with the bus. Getting to a surf beach in 3O min with an express bus is just so convenient. Can hire umbrellas and chairs, heaps of shops around, therefore no need to pre pack food.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Evening at beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Near perfect conditions be at beach.No waves for the surfer's.Had desert across the road. Great day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not My Favourite Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Now, to be up front, I am not a fan of sand. I don't like it. I'm on Anakin Skywalker's side when it comes to sand. It's rough and it's coarse and it gets everywhere.Having said, the sand on Bondi beach is the most amazingly fine sand I've seen, I had to walk around in it and paddle in the water a bit.I don't think Bondi seems like a very safe beach, in terms of the pull of the tide. The fine sand just seems to go out to see with every wave, meaning the beach takes a massive slope once you get to the water and the water can become deep very fast. That's probably great for surfing, but I think with little ones, and we had a child with us, you would need to be careful and very watchful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t bag the people who put there own lives on the line to save others every day they work
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I got caught in a rip at Bondi while trying to teach myself how to surf (bad idea!). Fortunately I’m a strong swimmer so managed to get back to the beach eventually.  I had absolutely no strength left in my body and I was 150 metres down from the point where I entered the water. During this ordeal I was watched by a a lifesaver who instantly recognised I might be in trouble and I new that if I lifted my hand he would save me...awesome!   Now as a father of four kids and nurse I would like to point out that it’s not the he job of these guys to look after our children,.  It’s the job of we parents. If they get stung by jelly fish it’s our fault for taking them in.  Go to the beach with stingoes and don’t blame these outstanding human beings for your own mistake!   Legends every one.   Andy the Scotsman.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a hot vacation week in Sydney so the beach was very crowded.  Fun to shop and watch the scene. Other nearby beaches were quieter.  There are places to rent beach gear and surf boards.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful tourist beach full of people
