reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a big area that you can do a lot of beach activities.  Full of people when we visit in December.  It seems a safe place to stroll and watch people. It worths a visit but the place is kind of overrated.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great day trip.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here from the UK to see the lifeguards from the famous tv programme. Unfortunately no one was around, didn’t like to knock on the door, the beach is beautiful and the buildings around it are very nice. Lush white sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Syd
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I can say that Bondi is the best beach in Sydney. Good wave to surf, and there is parking very near to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying in Sydney and got a Light Rail to the Bondi Junction and caught a bus to the Beach. It was a chilly slightly windy day for the time of year so few people were actually on the beach. It was quite impressive as beaches go but coming from South Africa its difficult to impress when held up to Cape Town and its beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous beach worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rather crowded but wort a visit anyway, and a great start for the southbond coastal walk. Fun to watch all the surfers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My Favorite
reviewsWithKeywords.text: between Bondi and Coogee, this is my favorite beach. Both have unique offerings, but I loved the artwork along the walls and being able to get away from the crowd to explore further away. Beach was also crowded during my visit, but there are ways to still have fun. Lots to do and would visit again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but touristy!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is pretty nice but it is very crowded. Definitely a tourist beach. But the beach is really big and there are tons of restaurants, shops, and bars along the walk. It is really easy to get to this beach from the center of Sydney, which is really nice!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: calm waves, clean and busy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: it was christmas day and everything was shut. there was nothing other than bondi beach to go to. it was so busy as everyone had the same idea we missed 3 full buses before we could get there. but the ride was worth it. we stopped at the far end of the beach and not the middle where there were shops and restaurants as i felt that place was more full. the far end was little less populated but it had no food. sobif u want food please get off in the middle area. the day was well spent the beach is super safe with calm waves and u can go pretty far from shore and still feel pretty safe no strong undercurrents. we had a great time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What's the hype about this beach?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the most boring beach as there hardly any shading during the heatwave time. Park area is tiny and dirty. Garbage bins were full and most garbage thrown all around. This beach is nothing compared to Manly. Restaurant choices are limited too

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited as part of a tour and got to walk around and have lunch while watching the surfers. Several of our group plan to go back tomorrow to actually surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic and beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Depending on the time of year, this beach will have a different impact on visitors. We were blessed with beautiful weather which allowed us to drive with the windows down all the way to the beach and enjoy an afternoon on the beach. It can get a bit crowded on hotter days but nonetheless the beach is huge and be advised to follow the instructions by the lifeguards and make your trip a safe one and their job easier. If you drive to Bondi like we did (we're not from Sydney) the roads can be very steep and narrow like the rest of Sydney. Better to take public transport :).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Swimming at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach is a must see when visiting Sydney.  We visited on 29 Dec 2018.   The beach clean but crowded as can be expected.  What was not expected was how dirty the bathrooms were.  Coming from Africa I though I was use to dirty bathrooms, but this was on another level.  The ladies bathrooms was very unhygienic, with used sanitary ware lying on the floor.  If you do visit Bondi beach brace yourself for the bathrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go Early
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Being really the nearest beach around Sydney apart from Manley it gets busy purchase your opal card and use it on the blue line from st James or kings cross 2 stops from kings cross then head to the bus all within the same complex no 338 or 333 will take you directly to the beach. Remember to tap in and out with your opal cards. You’ll get the hang of it quite a cool system they have.I’d say get there for around 9am you’ll be ready to leave by 12 as it becomes extremely busy if your a die hard and don’t mind the crowds you’ll be fine

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A social beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Me and my family visited the beach and it was a good day out. There is plenty to do with water activities, such as swimming and surfing. Lots if places to eat but also free use if the BBQs to cook your own food. There is plenty of grass for those that don’t like the sand. The beach is very busy so a very social location.Overall a fun day out. Not tranquil so don’t go if you want peace and quiet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: cool seas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went there with my family and friends. The beach was clean in fact one of the cleanest seen. The parking was ample and very near to the beach. Though it was quite windy at that time and the winds were chilling the view was fabulous with people exercising and jogging on the beach. The overall experience was very good.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its why you visit Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you come to Australia the first thing you want to do is go to Bondi Beach. It's one of the most iconic beaches in the world and once you get there you know why. It has an amazing atmosphere and the Lifesavers are always on the lookout. Don't get me wrong there are other beaches that are better but Bondi Beach is where it's at. You can spend the entire day there relaxing, swimming and eating at the lovely cafes. The biggest problem is parking! If you can find a good parking spot you will be paying up to $20 for the entire day. Public transport is not bad you can catch the bus from Bondi Junction. The only thing I will warn everyone about is the surf is dangerous for people that aren't used to swimming in Australian waters. So don't be a bloody idiot and swim between the flags. There is no smoking or drinking alcohol on the beach sorry you Europeans I know this upsets you. Make sure you pack plenty of sunscreen, water and sunglasses. If you're feeling energetic you can always do the coastal walk but make sure you take your stuff because it could get stolen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A place to go and relax. Nice beach surrounded by restarurantes and bars. Ideal fo those who like surf. You can visit the beachfront promenade, enjoy a coffee or cool drink and the best panoramic view at Dover Heights.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great fun for everyone, in the water and on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Grab a lounger and an umbrella (easy to rent) and enjoy the best people watching west of Waikiki. The whole world comes to Bondi and the life guard club and the local police dona terrific job of keeping it safe.  The surf and tides are not for the novice swimmer so be warned.....know your limitations and stay between the flags. It seems the guards were pulling people out of the surf all day long.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like any other beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I used to come here a lot but find myself not coming here as often as I used too. While the beach is lovely and beautiful, I don’t see why the big hype and fuss is over it. There are plenty of other beaches close to Bondi which are just as nice and less crowded. There are too many tourists that come here and leave their rubbish behind. On a weekend and on a hot day, this beach is full of people and you really have to try and find a spot to set up. There is very minimal shade at Bondi, so make sure you pack an umbrella or tent with you if it is a hot day. The waves can be pretty big and the current can be strong, so please make sure you swim between the flags. The good thing about Bondi is that across the road, you have a variety of food options to choose from. I would not recommend you drive to Bondi Beach as the parking is very limited and is terrible. I would suggest you catch the train to Bondi Junction and then catch the bus to Bondi Beach. There are frequent trains and buses that run to Bondi Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Looks like a nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was in town for one day and went to Bondi Beach. The beach looks fantastic.  Unfortunately, the weather did not cooperate. It was cool and dreary - much too cool to consider swimming or lying on the beach. We walked on the beach with a few other die hards, then walked across the street to one of the bars for draft beers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sardine style
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Too crowded with people everywhere. Hardly any parking and also very expensive parking. The worst beach EVER!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots of people and high waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is nice, the sand is very nice and contrary to popular belief (mine and my fam’s) you could actually walk on it barefoot! Even though there were a lot of people (probably not as much as there could be) it was easy to find a spot for the entire family close to the water! The waves are pretty high, but if you’re not that good of a swimmer or if you have kids, stay close to the shore as there are some pretty scary currents!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a windy day when we got there, but it was worth it. We took the bus to Bondi Junction with Opal card (must have when you travel with public transportations). From Bondi beach you can take a long walk to other beaches with nice view. Absolutely worth a trip with kids or for couples. After a nice walk can you have a nice meal in Bondi Junction square. There were a lot of food you can choose from and with a lot goodie stands.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Almost brilliant bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My first time to bondi and pleasantly surprised. The quality of the sand and sea are actually quite good. Gets crowded but people watching is part of the fun. Lots of shops around to get your sunblock, snacks and water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited here on a Sunday morning, what a great beach. It's very well patrolled. It's buzzing with people but plenty of space. One of the most busiest beaches I've seen. Can certainly spend a few days here. Plenty of bars on the harbour to grab food or a drink. A must if you're in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So Australian Bondi is such a vibrant, lively place full of people walking & exercising. What a great place to be

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun and lively even during winter
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Likes: Just the right amount of quietness and liveliness. There was an event when I came here but even so, a walk by the beach was relaxing. Maybe because it's winter that is why the breeze was refreshing. I also liked the wall arts/murals. Made me wanna take a picture on each art. Watched the sunset here and it's lovely.Dislikes: Because there were a lot of people, it was hard to find a place where I can just sit and relax. But that's not much of a big deal actually

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s an iconic beach which is buckling under the weight of its overwhelming popularity. The public transport is trying but is hampered by those taking cars. Private cars should be banned.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach and surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went for an afternoon to Bondi Beach to take our teenage son surfing and we had a great time. Facilities throughout were good. Surf board hire for $25 at Ripcurl shop opposite was excellent and they were so friendly.  Plenty of places to shop for souvenirs and sit for a coffee.  Best way to get there is T4 from city to Bondi Jnct and then bus to beach which is very regular and easy to find

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Christmas day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Crazy waves! Excellent life guards, good access to facilities. Soft sand, plenty of space, keep little ones close and listen to the lifeguards for your safety.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold summer at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s summer time but still rather cold in December. Strong wind with plenty of surfers and swimmers. There were more tourists than local.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love this beach! Absolutely beautiful and definitely worthwhile to go. Lots of great shopping and excellent food nearby

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Global meeting spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most famous beaches in the world. There is everything and more. Just walking down the beach you will hear accents from all over the world. Cafes and bars with magnificent views. There are surely beaches in nicer surroundings, but this is one of a kind when it comes to meeting up with other nationalities. Prices are pretty steep, parking and drinks/food included so if you’re on a budget bring your own and arrive by public transport.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Has to be done !!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice Beach - there are many better, but it’s iconic and has to be done.  Parking is very expensive though

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to Bondi Beach on a Saturday and it was packed with people. A lot of twenty-somethings having a good time. Just walking along the boardwalk is great. No shortage of places to eats as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Musst see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is probably the most known beach in Sydney. It's good for swimming, getting tanned and for surfing. Also the Icebergs are next to it, if you are interested in new photos on social media 😉

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is an iconic spot to visit. The beach is soft and clean, the waves are good for a surf, and because it’s 1 km long there’s a lot of space. The views are stunning, especially from the north end of the beach by Ben Buckler. The pavilion is right there for restrooms, food, and trinkets. For a tourist beach, it is very nice for a visit with easy access to the main shops, buses, and food.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow wow wow!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The travel book said that we would not be impressed!  Boy, were they wrong.  We used public transit to travel from centre town Sydney and the bus dropped us right in front of the beach.  What a sight to behold!  This is a huge beach with acres and acres of white sand and turquoise blue water.  On a Sunday, the beach was peppered with locals and tourists alike trying to catch some rays and swim the dangerous waves.  We did stick our feet in the water and found it extremely cold!!!  The beach has a few nice eateries and we did have lunch there and found the food at par as far as prices goes with venues elsewhere and the food was quite good.  There are change rooms and toilets and stalls with lots of tourism information.The beach is well managed with lifeguards and surfing guards on site.  Be sure to do the Bondi to Coogee walk - it's so well worth the hike!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great place to sit and people watch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is really beautiful and while crowded, everyone there is friendly and there to do the same thing as you, swim, sunbake or relax. If interested, walk to the right side and around the cliffs. The view is simply stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I had been told of mixed views on this beach before I got there so was not sure what to expect.I was surprised and in a good way.We were ther at a weekend so it was busy. That said, it was well set up with very good facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: very large and still crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The size of this beach is large compared with the neighbouring beaches. Public transport to Sidney is frequent, but at the end of the day you can best walk to the north side because at the south side you may not be able to get a place in the bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Clear Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is very busy, lots of people watching & that is part of its charm. It has incredible surf and clear water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views but amazing surf!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its the most famous beach in Sydney and probably in Australia. Its really beautiful and lots of green space if all the sandy area is taken with families, backpackers and students. If you're not a good swimmer its better to go to another beach as here the surf could be very dangerous as the waves are usually very big!Plenty of restaurants and cafes as well as a very scenic coast walk!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After so, the hype associated with this world known beach we were disappointed. It's a nice beach and good for surfing but the area is tacky and overrated. It was packed on day we went but it is quite a nice beach itself but surroundings let it down. My advice is take ferry to Manly beach instead where you can surf too but in much nicer surroundings and area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent view with clear water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hi Visited this place for Adidas Parley Event to promote the banning of plastic material being used and thrown into the oceans. we had 4km walk around the beach for this event. It was in the evening time and was amazed to see so many people having fun surfing, doing water rides ,etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everything and more
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went there to have a quick swim and body board.  I was amazed at how big it really is.  Found the hire places on the beach very easily to hire my body board.  Water is crystal clear and had a lot of fun in the surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach was a very last minute decision to go to for me. It’s quite far away from the city but the Uber ride was totally worth it. The beach was the prettiest beach I’ve ever seen. The sand was so soft. The water was crystal clear. Although a bit chilly it didn’t stop others from going out and surfing. I was there at sunset and the view was amazing. I highly recommend this beach as a must see spot while you’re in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk & Talk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want a full day with your spouse then we highly recommend Bondi. My new wife and I started our day at the rock swimming pool and ended at the opposite end on top of the cliffs. We spent the whole day walking and talking ..Great Day Out

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach is one of the most famous beaches, not only in Sydney, but also in entire Australia. It is close to Sydney CBD, can go by bus or train. From Bondi junction bus station, buses are available to Bondi beach. Food shop are available there. Getting a parking is hard.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bathing and surfing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sun tanning people have the luxury to choose to be on either nice sand or perfectly cut grass. There are outdoor gyms and also a small pool area with sea water for the young. So this beach is great for both families and others.The water is clear and I like the colour and the beach is pretty clean and the sand is nice.On the other side of the road you have the possibility to shop more or less whatever and eat and drink.This is of course one of the most popular beaches and the most well known beach outside Australia. So it can be pretty crowded. If you are ok with the crowd this is the beach for you!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent the day at Bondi beach lovely clean beach, easy to travel to via train and bus from Sydney. Plenty of eateries close by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach in the City
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is undoubtedly the best beach in sydney. As soon as one arrives on the beach the sound of water and waves taken onto ears and when one thinks that it's so good the eye rests on the graffiti art done on the wall and every single art is so pleasing to watch. At the end one could not stop himself from approaching the water and getting feet wet. Seagulls are also good to see there and apartments on the cliffs look so satisfying with people who can be seen over the cliffs. Over all a good place to be with friends and family.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overcrowded and underrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is all the hype and show but it’s like having a bath with your entire family and a dozen strangers. It’s packed on any normal day and should be regulated with a fence line and tickets so it’s not like cramming sardines into a can. My advice, don’t bother wasting your time. You can’t sit anywhere, swim without your body rubbing against a stranger or eat across the road without queuing. The city of Bondi has failed its community in a quest of greed here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: "noise of water breaking over rocks"
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Closing my eyes, listen to the nature. Listing to the Rollin waves as they try to survive on the steady rocks. Look at the waves, try to flush away the most beautiful sand of my beach. The most beautiful beach on earth

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sprawling Sandy Beach - Surfer's Galore!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a mecca for surfers and is close to Paradise!  The variety of sports is endless here: surfing, paddle boarding, kayaking, swimming, volleyball, snorkelling, scuba, you name it.  Lots of young people and families have a blast!  The beach is surrounded with shopping, restaurants and bars to complete the day.  The trails along the coastline will give you a birds-eve view of dolphins and migrating whales too.  Also a good place for birding. Always a favourite for locals, tourists and residents of Sydney who wish to enjoy a first-rate beach experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must visit if going to Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Caught a bus from the city and spent the day on Bondi beach. Great day out. Including shops and restaurants/cafes, there was everything for everyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic  beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is the iconic beach associated with Sydney. Despite the high expectations, it is a very enjoyable spot.Amazing view, friendly atmosphere. Many spots to swim, tan, eat and drink!Hard to miss

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Got to do it just to say you've been there!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the bus from central Sydney. I suggest  you buy a bus card (a bit like oyster card) from a local shop for $10 and used it for there and back, a couple of $ left on the card. It is a good way of seeing all the different neighbourhoods too.Bondi is large and busy and pretty. It has very good changing rooms, showers etc free for the public. There are some boutiques if you want to spend money and lots of cafes and restaurants. We didn't swim but lots of people were in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sydney 18
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a few miles drive from Sydney central. Had to go and see the world famous Bondi Beach. It’s a great tourist attraction and the locals use it for fitness and obviously surfing. Great clean beach with lovely views. It was a bit cloudy on my visit but with high temperatures I would definitely visit again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beginning of Spring and already Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a city tour that included Bondi beach. Though it is late spring in early December the beach was already crowded. There were nice shops along the beachfront and clean change/bathrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Typical Beach Town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice beach town, shops and restaurants and a very nice beach for swimming & surfingNothing unique unless they have a special event going on ....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach + nearby food and drink
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An easy beach to relax and enjoy the sun & surf. A few restaurants are within very easy walking distance and more are a few blocks away. It's clean and there's lots of room (at least on a weekday!)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but there are others in close proximity that are just as nice but not as famous.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful large cove with soft white sands. Big waves so popular with surfers. Plenty of facilities. Does get super busy in summer- up to 35000 people! There are other smaller but equally nice beaches further along the coast that get a bit less busy. Some you can walk to and others require a short drive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved it! Beautiful sand and rolling waves! You can watch the 🏄🏼‍♀️ surfers or just chill and people watch! Lovely walks too along the waterfront, bars and cafes. Buses are regular and you can get the train from Sydney, very straight forward.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lives up to its reputation!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a fantastic beach, white soft sand and very clean environment, safe for families (and everyone else!), lots of shops and restaurants nearby. Lifeguards on duty and you must swim between the flags, but lots of surfing going on riding the waves as it was quite windy whilst we were there

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Got there on the hop on hop off bus.Lovely sand beach. Stood in water.Lots of shops and cafes too.Must do on any tour

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold breeze in November
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went there late October and you can feel the cold breeze coming from the ocean.  If youre from tropical country, visiting Bondi beach this time of the year is so cold especially in the afternoon. Though during mid day the sun will literally burn your skin.  But despite all these, the beauty of Bondi beach still stands out.  Great place to hang out and just chill.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Poor weather spoils view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Picked a bad day as it was overcast- lovely sandy beach and a good number of swimmers mainly outside Australia.Great murals - pick a warm clear day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were holidaying in Sydney and thought we must see Bondi Beach. It was as beautiful s we imagined. Huge surf waves, fine sand that you just have to walk on. Beautifully clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love this beautiful beach in Australia!!it my first time there and simply love the sand, big waves and the sun.Parking can be a little tricky when it comes to weekend a peak season.But if you are a beach goer, this is one beach you just gotta visit.Love the beach but don't wanna get dark? apart from putting on those sun block, there are small umbrella renting station around the beach.just about 15 dollars you can rent the beach umbrella for as long as you stay in the beach (not overnight though).Shower and toilet facilities also locate conveniently along the road near the beach.foods and some fashion stores can be found easily too if you want to get some souvenir such at t-shirt.As the it facing the pacific ocean thus the big strong waves, young children need to be strictly watch by the parents or guardian.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, lots people and parking tight and $
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spoiler I am from Western Australia so hard to impress with a beach. This was just ok, homeless people about, surfer dudes, lots of tourists from overseas. The beach was busy but not packed, surf was up and looked good. Sand very yellow and nothing that cool about it - underwhelmed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have traveled a lot and this is one of the most beautiful beaches very have ever seen.  It is a fun place to hang out if the weather bus good.  Definitely worth a stop if just to take pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What has Blackpool and Bondi got in common?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well its not the weather !!! But it is that they have a main busy road separating and a big beach . They also have a bit of a tacky strip and that is how I found Bondi . Its also not on the ferry or rail network so was not a great journey to get there . I did not find great cafes and food so sadly it did not live up to the hype .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderfuk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful with fine white sand. Between the beach and road there is a field of green which is great for picnics. Take bus 333 from Bondi Junction train station. There are shops along the main road with good food and beach stuff. Not suitable for swimming and beware if you are with children. If you are having a meal don’t feed the birds or they will swarm you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ok
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went as to see what all the hipe was about,but when we got there.it wasn't as big as I thought it looked good surf and good for swimming as well life guarded,but otherwise just another beach plenty of eateries and cafes,so ok if that's what you want 😎👍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful town by the seashore with a very lively bubbly atmosphere, the cleanliness was amazing of both beach and footpaths. The choice of places to eat and shop was also great an absolute visit again 4 days wasn't enough.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach highly recommend ! Did the Bronte to Bondi walk. The people here are so friendly and the beach is nice and clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just a Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is clean with nice sand, however it's just another beach. I don't find it any more spectacular than any other nice beach. Don't quite understand why it is so popular. I would say the beach is fairly small as well. Can easily walk from one side to the other under 30 minutes. I wouldn't bother going twice. It doesn't stand out to me in any way. If there wasn't so much hype about this place then I wouldn't judge so harshly. There is nice art work painted on the walls, which we spent more time looking at than the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Of course a MUST SEE !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For me it was a bit disappointing. I like Brontë and Tamarama beach much more. But of course this beach is so famous you definitely must go there and see it yourself. Behind the beach many nice restaurants. Busy place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not a bad way to spend New Year's eve.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just another place to tick off the list, would have liked a bit more sun but was still warm and busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wohoo....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beach we enjoyed in the life. Clean, full of world tourist, exciting, memorable. Best, Best, Best.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just go!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not too much to say. It's iconic. It's busy. There's a big beach to share. It's close to Sydney city and accessible by bus.Swim between the flags are risk getting into difficulties. The currents can be extremely strong here. Listen to the lifesavers/lifeguards.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous Local Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was fortunate enough to stay here for four nights on my first visit to Sydney. It was actually fairly quiet due to not the best weather. The shops along the beach are okay, nothing special or unique. A nice place for a morning or sunset stroll. Fun to watch the surfers and a few brave swimmers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach and Aussie icon.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to Sculptures by the Sea on a beautiful sunny day and the experience was lovely. The beach and surrounding area is clean with plenty of cafe’s, bars and lunch time spots to visit. Will be back for many years to come.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Went to see sculpture by the see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a great view from the cliffs, dropped my phone on the concrete wouldn’t recommend doing that as phone broke from the contact but otherwise the beautiful sceneries are stunning and make up for my broken phone. 😂

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always wanted to visit Bondi Beach so while in Sydney it was obviously a must! The beach is gorgeous, clean and bustling with people! Great watching everyone out surfing aswell! I loved it I’d definitely return in the future!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach’s Sculpture by the Sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Every couple of years I visit this exhibition which is uniquely perched along the cliff walk between Bondi Beach through Bronte to Tamarama Beach. The sculptures were nice but the real beauty were the eroded rock faces, bright colored flowers growing alongside and the sea. I would advise visiting on weekdays (for the lesser crowds and better beachside parking).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEAUTIFUL BEACH - Sculptures By The Sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to see Sculptures By the Sea at Bondi, we walked from Tamarama Beach along the Coastal walk past all the Amazing Sculptures To Bondi Beach we walked past the Bondi Icebergs Club & were going to have lunch there but it was really busy, on a quieter day this is a beautiful spot to eat & they have really good food, so we walked along the walkway alongside the Beach past a huge wall of Amazing Murals which are really worth seeing, crossed the road & had lunch at ‘The Bucket List’ the food was great, we sat outside overlooking Bondi  Beach, great day out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Icebergs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place, beautiful people, beautiful food. Service a little erratic. Food was excellent. Probably need to book a few months in advance for the restaurant but the bar is more relaxed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun at the Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The first attempted swim of the year is always fun,  hopped into the family mobile and off we set down to Bondi beach arrived at 8:45, parking was already hard to find by 9;15 we finally found one. The council make the whole outing so enjoyable when the metered parking is about $3,50 for 30 minutes. By the time you walk from the car to the red and yellow flags you end up with about 15 minutes of actual time in the water so no time to build sand castles.Nothing says beach fun with the Council's greedy hand I  your back pocket.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Photo opportunities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a bit cool and windy the day we were there. We would have gone swimming otherwise We walked the beach cliff trail instead. The walk was very nice with a lot of gorgeous Pacific Ocean views. We took some wonderful photos and enjoyed a nice cup of coffee at the end. There's a nice fish market in town with delicious shrimp, oysters and lobster.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brilliant Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is a very popular beach packed with vibrant buzzing people - and that is the brilliant thing about it. My family really enjoyed the day, here. We really enjoyed using the pool and looking at the sea view. The waves were huge and were beautifully coloured with blue. Both the restaurant and bar had excellent service. I would really reccomend going to this wellknown renowned beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must in Sydney, if for nothing else then its legendary name as a must see place.We had hot chocolate at one of the cafes close to Bondi, hot chocolate on a nice cool day, another must when at Bondi. Paid parking available in the lots right near the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing day at Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great places to eat and watch the world go by good open spaces if you don’t like the sand but love the sea views . Nice and flat to stroll around the promenade

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing timing with the art exhibition on
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unreal beach with fantastic walk round the coast was lucky enough to see the art exhibition on the walk round and was lucky enough to have the sun shinning up there with one of the best beaches I’ve been to

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just like TV
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did the walk from bronte to bondi and the coastal views were nothing to sneeze at. Bondi was a nice Australian white ssand beach and was closed due to dangerous currents the day we went. Still nice to wet the feet on a stroll. Besides we love Bondi rescue!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun and nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I know the locals aren't a huge fan of this place, much like the Oahu residents and Waikiki in Hawaii. However, this is a beautiful beach with plenty of people on the sand and in the water. There is the iconic pool off to the side that seems part of the ocean and you can seemingly swim there for under $10 in the pool. There are plenty of eateries, restaurants, and shops at Bondi and is the starting or ending point of the Bondi-Coogee coastal walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great even in cooler weather
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a fabulous beach, its definitely a surfers beach. So many younger kids taking advantage of the great waves to learn how to surf. The area is full of shops and places to grab a bite to eat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Stretch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately we didn’t stay as long as we’d like. But the sand and surf were fantastic. October is a little off-season, we’re told, which accounted for the sparse crowd—perfect for relaxed sightseeing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Late night beach stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Arrived later than anticipated to wake from Bondi to Coogee,  but still took a stroll on the beach. Very nice beach,  lovely sand and surf - surfer favorite.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Another great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of Sydneys great beaches. offering a great walk along the coast, great cafe and restaurants and great markets and shopping. Makes for a good day out

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful beach so close to main st for shopping across the road for Sunday markets. This beach has lifeguards in spring and summer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want to spend a day in a beach and see beautiful people, you may want to visit Bondi beach. The sunset is lovely as the coast turns golden.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is perhaps one of the best beach in Sydney please do visit with your friends and family and I assure you are going to have a great time

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We hear so much about world famous Bondi Beach. Seeing it is not the same! It’s beautiful, wild and exhilarating! When we were there, there weren’t any surfers in the water. It was still worth walking around. The whole area is fascinating. Well worth the detour!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most Beautiful white sand beach a surfer's paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took a walk through sandy ,partially paved rocky beach upto cliff top. An excellent view from the top .Also surrounded by various eateries and enjoyed Coogee coastal walk.Also can enjoy swimming at an elevated swimming pool. People flock to what is known grassy knoll- tiny grass field .In September every year there is kite festival in the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Had to see Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Using the hop on hop off bus tour we stopped off at the beach. Good weather, fun to watch surfing and lots of places to eat and shop at.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Who doesn't love a great beach? And when it's one of the most iconic beaches in the world, even better!Bondi is one of those places everyone should visit if they can, and once you've been once you'll want to keep coming back. The beach is great and so is the surfing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is the best beach you can go to in Sydney. Lots of people, beautiful beach, amazing weather, I would go back to Bondi any given day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach though we weren’t lucky with weather!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited in the first week of October and were hoping for warm weather, unfortunately it wasn’t that warm or even sunny.Nevertheless the area, the shops, the beach stroll and even watching the committed surfers in the early morning was worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the great and famous Sydney beaches.beatifil sands and water unfortunately we could not swim because it was cold for me but we enjoyed the walk and watching people

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful beach. It truly is postcard perfect.Life guards are everywhere which is great (however please always swimming in between the red and yellow flags) Its  clean and so lovely to swim at. Lots of cafes/ shopping close by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I spent the day at Bondi Beach. It was chilly so we did a lot of walking around and had lunch. I definitely recommend the walk from Bondi to Bronte Beach. Breathtaking views and a great way to get some exercise and see the area. I also loved the murals at Bondi Beach. Great place for photo and selfies!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If there is one beach you must go to in Sydney, Bondi Beach is it! Beautiful ocean views and sounds. One can easily spend an afternoon there relaxing and walking the coastal trail. Sounds of waves breaking is very therapeutic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No visit to Sydney is complete without a trip to Bondi beach. Chilled vibe and lots of restaurants just around if you want to take a break from the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A huge disappointment
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was very disappointed with Bondi Beach. Having heard all about it I was expecting fantastic views and a fabulous long beach. However, the reality is a small beach surrounded by shops - not at all pretty or appealing. If you want to see some stunning beaches in Australia head for the south instead.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow what a beautiful dangerous beach! You would be crazy to swim outside of the flags due to the undertow and rips. It is a fabulous setting with plenty of beach space to spread out. Lots of cafes and shops to investigate just behind the beach and accommodation everywhere. A really great place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tourist Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is Sydney’s number #1 tourist beach.The beach is clean, beautiful and a lovely compliment to Australian beaches.The beach is under the care of some of the worlds most skilled, educated, trained and experienced life guards you’ll ever come across.If you’re coming here, please please swim between the flags. The currents at Australian beaches can be deadly and often you can’t see the danger from outside the water. If you come into trouble put your hand up for help.This beach doesn’t have many locals visiting, it is 99% tourist only. That is not a criticism, this is definitely a beautiful beach.Like any public place around the world that attracts a lot of tourist... don’t take valuables to the beach to simply leave them unattended as you swim. Theft is a reality we face anywhere in the world. Parking is not great and generally reserved for disabled spaces or timed parking for locals running errands. Definitely take a bus from the city or from Bondi Junction which is linked to the train system.There is a nearby walk to Coogee which is great for all ages, fitness levels and mobility levels including wheelchairs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nature at its best.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A gorgeous beach on the Australian coastline. Lots of beautiful clean sand to sit and relax. Life guard patrol, swim between the flags.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the detour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you have time, it is worth going to see the famous Bondi beach, especially on a nice day. Even if it's too cold to go swimming,  it is fun to watch the surfers. Lots of bars and restaurants near the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Check the weather before heading out at this time of year!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We made a 1.5 hour commute on the train to come here without checking temperatures and wind, and were in for a chilly and very windy time. While it was beautiful watching the sunset along the uninterrupted horizon, I was freezing. Was however pleased to see many food options and bathrooms for a comfortable and delicious evening dinner afterwards. Both affordable and higher range options available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach! Just remember your sun cream!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is the jewel of Sydney. It's really just massive. Full of holiday goers and the locals surfing and just catching a tan! The water is very powerful though so just take your time in the water if you're not a strong swimmer. Also remember your sun cream I burnt terribly and it was cloudy. Brilliant beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Birthday holiday visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well you can’t come to Sydney and not visit the infamous Bondi beach can you, if you have time to fit it in the do so. Wouldn’t say that it is a must though, at the end of the day it is a nice sandy beach, could be anywhere. We visited on an unusually hot day and the place was rammed! Plenty of souvenir shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great place even on a cold windy day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So, my group and I decided to see the famous Bondi Beach that everyone told us to see. I will say, the beach did not disappoint. If you’re from the states it’s got a feel of Huntington Beach to it, but the views and the bar scene around the area just doesn’t compete. The food options and souvenir shops right before the beach vary and can give even the group of 10 I went with plenty of options to check out.The only thing that I would say is a downside right now on the beach is the minor construction they have going on, on the beach it isn’t a large area that’s being torn down or renovated but it is noticeable. Other than that, the place is just generally a fun place to be around regardless.I will definitely make a return again when it’s warmer it was a crisp 65F when we went with winds blowing in from the ocean. Needless to say. It. Was. Cold.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful landscape very clean and easy to access with lot of cozy bars.it is ideal for swimming and surfing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took my family of 8 here for a week getaway. Monday- friday there were a few people around , but once it was sat & Sunday there were a lot of people there . Beautiful beach. Rough water though . Clean sand & beach. Lots of tourists everywhere . Heaps of grass to sit if you don’t want to sit on sand. Shops, cafe’s & restaurants across the road . Some parking available but full on weekends . Heaps of street art on the walls, and great to see the Bondi life guards there patrolling the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great day visit close to Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great way to spend the day just a short drive from Sydney. Took a swim at the famous Bondi pool. COLD but has a great sauna with glass door and windows overlooking the bay. A definite must.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Somewhat Over-rated Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is large beach and known the world around and has great waves and good sand but it is a somewhat over-rated beach and the street cafe's along the beach are fairly tacky. There are better beaches along the coast but a great place to start the walk to Coogee which is up there with the best in views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to go to!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect for locals, surfers, and tourists alike! This is hands down the best beach in Sydney and is a great place to visit any time of year. Surfers will love the waves off of the ocean, tanners will love the sands, tourists will love the views. There really is something for everyone. There is also a public pool located off the beach which is perfect for days when you don't feel like going into the ocean. There are cafes and other various dining options as well. A must do while in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow Factor
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful, iconic beach centrally located and easy to get to. Not as picturesque as many other Sydney beaches but still has a wow factor - surrounded by  beautiful sandstone rocky outcrops, great sand and lovely surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: More than a beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is famous for the world class beach. Even you are not swimmer, you will have to come to visit this beach in Sydney. Quite often, tourists are seen here with their lugguage pulling around the boardwalk before their flight.The beach is also popular for festival, gathering, sports event and family activity. The one day Festival of the Winds held there and it brought so much fun to the area even it's still a bit cold for swimming.The only setback of the beach is there is no train station so traffic jam is quite often going in if not out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Marketing exec is a genius
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Whoever did marketing for Bondi Beach is an absolute genius. The beach is crowded most of the year, overcrowded in summer with a limited number of reasonably priced places to have a drink or dine after. The nightlife in Bondi is non existent - the beach, although beautiful is flushed with so many people and travel too and from is an absolute nightmare.  There are better beaches to go to - Coogee Bronte Tamarama Maroubra Northern Beaches to name a very few. Well done Marketing team however! Job very well done. Photo taken early morning 8am pre-rush.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful! Wish we had come at a different time of year when it’s hot and sunny. Still enjoyed our visit and the walk to Coogee beach. Enjoyable watching the surfers 🏄🏻‍♂️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Touristy but beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are lots of tourist and backpackers in the area. Beautiful beach that live up to its hype but can get very crowded in the summer. Parking is a nightmare during public holidays and the summer. You're better off taking the train from the city to Bondi Junction and then taking the bus to Bondi beach instead. There is a Bondi to Coogee coastal walk that passes by several more beaches starting from the Bondi Icebergs end of the beach. Despite the obvious tourist trap and crowd, you will not be disappointed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One the Best Beaches in the World "Bondi Beach"
reviewsWithKeywords.text: "Bondi Beach" located at Eastern part of Sydney is one of the best beach in the world. An absolute must walk when visit Sydney. The walk features 5-6 famous Sydney beaches, stunning views, parks, cliffs, bays and rock pools. I came to know this is also known as Coastal Walk. Good part is, this beach is frequented by locals, tourists, backpackers and the Sydney high society people. It’s not just about the beaches and the views, the path that connected this string of beaches is also flanked by native bush and beautiful flowers that are now in the summer months in full bloom. Lot of eateries around one can enjoy the & relish on food too. Bondi Pavillion is an excellent gallery to visit if you are an art lover. Superb experience and recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: it's a legend
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice spot to enjoy a day in the sun.  Nice if you enjoy a day at the beach and a legend if you're a surfer.  If you're not a surfer,(like me), t's still fun to watch the waves come in and the surfers catch a ride.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: There is a reason Bondi is world-renowned
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been to Bondi probably fifty times over ten years and to swim only about five of those times. I have been to Icebergs at least twenty of those times which overlooks Bondi on the south side. The rest of the times it was to walk along the beach, breakfast at one of the many seaside restaurants, visit Sculpture By the Sea, even to baptise a close friend. Whatever the reason there is something to love about Bondi. Just go there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful relaxed but trendy place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach. Some great eateries. V relaxed feeling about the place. Worth a visit ... specially if u r a surfer . Apparently the surf worshippers get in a quick surf before and after work ... 530am they descend on the beach after  the clocks change!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a couple of hours here at the beach while visiting Sydney. Just a short train ride and we were there. Had a meal and a few drinks. Walked along the beach even had a chat with guys from Bondi Rescue. A nice day out

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Historic • Relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s winter when I came here so didn’t go to the water. However just by being here, feel the breeze you’ll feel relax and recharge.Just sit on the bench and bring a book it’s good enough. There are plenty of shops, hotels built in early 1900’s and cafés.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful city beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was over there after the City2surf and it was really excited to see this beach in winter... small waves and no one in water...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This was exactly what we expected - we had a brilliant day!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We really enjoyed our time on Bondi Beach. It was just as depicted on a TV programme in the UK called Bondi Rescue.The sand was lovely and soft and I was surprised when I waded into the water, very close to the shore, how quickly I sank into the sand and almost lost my balance when a wave came in and can now imagine how easily and quickly someone can get into trouble at Bondi. My short trousers got a soaking but I was rewarded by having a picture taken with one of the Lady Life Guards! Thank you.The entire Bondi area is full of character and life with plenty of cafes and restaurants etc and we were sad when we had to leave to catch our HoHo bus back to Sydney.It was a great day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was incredible getting to surf with the locals was incredible . The blue water and the white sand are exactly why this is one of the most iconic beaches on the planet .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and just great. Amazing way to chill and enjoy a lovely view for relaxing mind and soul Really good for workout !!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the trip!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy to get to the beach on the bus from the Circular Quay or CBD. Good place to people watch-suspect it isn't as pleasant when everyone and their brother (and sister) are there in the summer. Good cafes/restaurants overlooking the beach. Worth going just so you can say you were there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the more fun beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Talk about people watching!  This is the place for it!  It ranks up there with some of the beaches in Mykonos that I've visited.  Large, clean, relatively safe (from sharks as long as you're not stupid), and lots of pretty international people.  Very gay friendly, as is most of Australia.  Bondi is a rather Bohemian crowd too.....not pretentious.  Very laid back.  The area is full of fun restaurants and shops, galleries, to purchase local fare.  It feels a little bit like the beach communities in San Diego, CA.  I would go back again for sure.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold and nice view in Winter
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Because we went in Winter, so not many people swim, can walk on beach freely. Enjoy half day there. If you have time, walk to the northern end or southern end.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great even in off-season
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even though I visited during the low season it's still iconic and a must visit location. Despite the mild weather it was still a great place to spend the day. I understand that it can be quite hectic in peak season so perhaps it was even better to experience in a more relaxed time of year. Nice bars and restaurants line the beach allowing you to spend the full afternoon eating and drinking your away around since swimming wasn't much of an option.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dr.  Aron Kondasinghe Sudath
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Jam packed with people on the weekends.  Beautiful and clean. Breathtaking Ocean View. Great to see people relaxing on the beach.  Understandably more expensive than other parts of Sydney. But worth the visit. Highly recommend it. Dr.  Aron Kondasinghe Sudath

reviewsWithKeywords.title: New Zealand and Australia cruise dairy:  Sydney post cruise, Day 1 Part 4
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On a sunny summer afternoon in Sydney, we took the bus from the CBD to see the iconic Bondi beach.  The ride took about 30 minutes.  We got off at the bus stop near the center of the beach.  From there we made our way to the grassy area to have a picnic.  We proceeded to the white sand to be among the hordes of tourists enjoying the beach and the sea.  There were various nationalities.The area is wide and can accommodate lots of people.  You can find a suitable spot in the sand and enjoy your visit.  Even if we had not brought swim gear, having been on Bondi beach was still a good experience.  The buses were full on the way back to the CBD. It was completely expected because it was summer peak season.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must visit when visiting Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach, with great waves. Really enjoyed coming here for the day. Highly recommended to those who want to say they been to one of the most famous beaches in the world!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Box ticked - but cold
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took the direct 333 Bus from Stand B on Alfred Street, Circular Quay (with Opal card).Beach had a few surfers and even less swimmers as water is too cold. Majority of people walking along promenade and beach were tourists. Several body builders on gym equipment. Fine views of the crescent shaped beach. We had a walk to the far headland and a snack in the Beach Pavillion Cafe. Spotted a couple of the Bondi Rescue lifeguards briefly!- Spent a couple of hours there - not much more to do in 15’ temperature! Then took 333 bus back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good for posers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Caught the bus down from Watson’s Bay. Walking from the main road to the beach involved negotiating a plethora of topless posers, narcissistically using outdoor gym equipment. That aside, the beach was pretty standard. Seen much better elsewhere in Australia and New Zealand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand is super soft but right now, the water is super cold. We enjoyed the view though and the area is very lively!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth seeing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The famous Bondi Beach is worth seeing, a very wide coastline, good for summer beach time. I went on winter day, not much people, beautiful. I heard summer super packed. Sand in beach is the finest I have seen, extremely soft to your feet. Water is clean and beautiful. Some but not high waves, so perfect for swimming. The iceberg swing pool is only $7 a visit if you want to swim beside the ocean. I didn't realized and was surprised by the absolutely stunning walk after you pass the beach. There is a coastal walk that you would walk for 2 hours to many more beach and areas if desire. Even if you take 10-20mins pass the beach to the right, you will see huge natural stones by the coastline, so don't miss out on that! Overall, I found it is famous for good reason. Worth checking it out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean beach with a great view and great facilities. Buses pass and there is a lovely path to enjoy a relaxing walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It’s not the best beach in the arwa
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you have time go to manly on the ferry for great beaches and great food places. Bondi is nice and a must do but for a relaxing beach go to manly instead

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just too many people.  Getting there by public transport is a nightmare.  Be prepared to take a couple of hours out of your day getting to and from this place.  After it took a couple of hours to get here, we took uber back to city, it was just ridiculous by PS.  The sand on this beach was like walking on white fluff and squeaky under your feet.  Was a 22 degree day in winter so everyone was out and about.  I’d hate to see it at 30 degrees 😳.I’ve been there now, don’t need to go back.  Other beaches just as nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice clean beach with lots of life guards everywhere. Great shops and restaurants all around the area. It’s on 5he. Us line so that made it really nice

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach is hard to get too!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As a first timer to Sydney, I presumed you could simply get the train to bondi and walk to the beach. Ummmm - no, it’s some distance still and you may need to get a bus. Avoid driving if you can - it’s a nightmare for parking as everyone (as you can expect) wants to see this beach.Nice beach? Yes - but there are better in Sydney that are easier to get too. Tick it off your list and keep going!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is nice to visit this beach, we had fun walking on the sand and seeing variety of people surfing, swimming and all sorts activities. Also lots strong people but unique. We are very happy made it to this famous beach and find a good place to spent few hours just walk around and enjoy the semicolon and friendly people. Took hundred of photo. It was fun. I recommend you take friends of family to visit this place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: famous surf beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Famous surf beach known internationally by most . Nice sea filled swimming pool to one side which looked inviting . Kids loved playing in the sand and paddling. Beach was busy even in middle of the Aussie winter .Worth seeing just to say you have been to Bondi !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, one of the icons of sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a lovely beach with ample space for doing what you want, be it surfing, swimming, paddling or just relaxing in the sands or on the dunes !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ocean Icon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow! Large beach and blue water forever... there is an ice rink and ferris wheel which is  out of place but somehow works.ample parking and clean sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great views, great surf, relaxing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a great beach...it has spoiled my opinion of other beaches worldwide probably for the rest of my life.  Great views...amazing views and great surf for swimming (or surfing...did not attempt).  One of our best days in Sydney was at Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view is magnificent in my opinion. The beach is big. It was fun to play with my niece, strolling and running around the park. We were also able to fed the birds around the beach. It felt good to just stand at the beach, listen to the breeze and waves, and be grateful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty beach but there are much nicer in Sydney. Its worth going to buy isn't an all day beach. Easy to get to from Sydney center and the surf club restaurant is a must do with beautiful views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic part of Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach,,, what can I say probably the most famous beach  in Australia maybe one of the most famous in the world, myself it’s to popular and to crowded (but that’s me) it seems to be the place you go to be seen,very popular with locals and visitors alike, if you want to get anything to eat or drink take your own or be prepared to pay the price, don’t get me wrong it’s a beautiful beach close to the city and a good place to see,,well serviced by busses from the city,, if you’re visiting Sydney it’s a place to see ,,,,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the beach area is so huge.... there are lots of people especially during summer. we came here last winter (july2016) and there was a ice skating ring in front of the beachhouse. my daughter sprained her ankle while penny boarding along the beach and received medical attention immediately by the lifeguard. they even offer us to send to the clinic nearby. they are so nice and friendly. we could not take a swim last year since its winter, we could not do the same this summer since someone injured...huhu. the beach is pet friendly. you can see dogs (with leash off course) strolling along...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large beach. Clean and nice. You must visit Bondi while i Sydney. Be carefull, becouse of large waves and rips. Be aware of thieves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Been there with my partner and watech dolphins and surfers surfing on waves together it is unforgettable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Surfer paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this beautiful beach while in Sydney. Could just simply sit there watching the waves rushing to the shore. N the surfers with the wakeboard trying to tame the waves. Beside the beach, there are plentiful eateries around to satisfy ur tummy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular beach, lots of happening during weekends
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came during winter, super windy and made it really chilly. But the winter sun was still very inviting. Plenty of good surfers and good for people watching. Will recommend going to speedos cafe for brunch and iceberg restaurant for a spectacular view

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach like no other
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with the finest sand I’ve ever touched! The lifeguard is attentive. There is an ice-skating rink, a row of restaurants, shower rooms and toilets and some shops across the street.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking with friends
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked from Coogee beach up to bondi beach and the view is spectacular and breathtaking. I suggest that you wear walking shoes and comfortable clothes. The trail is easy and very nice to do while in Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous blue waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a good time here, even for the winter.  There were still people surfing, and in the water, though the waves were a bit too much for me to consider getting in.  I would recommend going to BBPB (I think that's it?) - a little restaurant right across the street from the beach.  Their fried polenta was cheap and to die for.  Also, there's a great spot to watch the surfers and whale watch in the winter at the South end of the beach - just look for the infinity pool and head that way - even viewing from the walkway/street was gorgeous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a beach, nothing else, off course there are quite some big waves for the surf fanatics. Quite some eateries and shops on the promenadeNearest stop Big Bus: Stop 30 (Blue)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is iconic for a reason.  It is stunning! The weather was perfect giving us the best possible conditions for our visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots to do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went in June so the beach was not crowded at all. In fact, I could probably count the number of people on the beach.   However, my niece and her family went in January and there were probably 20,000 people shoulder to shoulder.  The beach isn’t huge but it is beautiful!  The girls took surf lessons which were awesome! We had lunch overlooking the water, walked around the shops, stopped and took pictures along the graffiti wall and did the Bondi Coastal Walk which is absolutely amazing.  I would highly recommend enjoy Bondi Beach and surrounding area. Just know in summer months it is very crowded.  We were lucky and avoided all the crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OVER RATED
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was pretty but very overpacked. If you’re staying in Sydney & looking for a beach day, I’d head over to manly beach! Manly is a bigger beach with a lot less people & was actually relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fabulous and easy walk from Bronte Beach to Bondi Beach.  A must do if you are in the area.  The rock formations in-between the beaches add to the beauty of the walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great in winter too
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We all love Bondi beach in summer. But this year yet again there are attractions to make winter pleasurable.  A huge Ferris wheel and a terrific ice skating rink.  So if it’s too cold for swimming ( not everyone feels the cold as I do) go skating instead. Recommended

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful surf!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So this beach was the last beach we stopped at along our coastal walk from Coogie Beach. The highlight of the beach was the restaurant we ate at overlooking the pools that are in the beach landscape. What a view! It is worth going just to see this! Lots of surfers, and cute town across the way!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everyone visiting Sydney has to go to the iconic Bondi beach.Get off the bus at the top on the hill. Walk down to the sea baths. Leisurely walk along the beach past the Bondi Surf life station to the other sea baths.The RSL at the end of the beach is reasonably priced meal with million dollar views

reviewsWithKeywords.title: DIP YOUR TOES IN THE WATER
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi Beach is one of the world's key beach attractions and should be on your bucket list. The magical waters of the Pacific Ocean create this bay and magnificent beach with pale golden sand stretches before you with beautiful headlands either end of the beach and plenty of places to visit and go. There are eateries/restauranta/cafes and fantastic local shopping. Weekends have markets. The local Pavilion has events and art shows ... so much to offer and so much for you to explore. Get out and about;  get into Bondi and get down to those golden sands and dip your toes in the water! ENJOY!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I was enchanted with Bondi Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First of all, I didn't go there with the primary purpose of going to the beach. I had a conference at the Lifesaving Club right on the beach with a great view from the second story window. But my host told me to bring my "swimmers" and I did.Travelling from Sydney, I took the train to Bondi Junction and took a cab from the train station to the beach. Big mistake. I got a rather rough woman cabbie who I am sure took the long way. It was $17 dollars to the beach from the train station by cab. Along the way, she told that the beach was safe because to her recollection, sharks hadn't taken away from the beach in years. Plus there was a shark net out there somewhere.  It didn't deter me.Once there, the beach was everything that one expects from the Australian beaches -- glorious sunshine, golden sand, surfers galore and bathers.  The beach is actually a national surfing monument. There were drinks vendors with colorful umbrellas and the whole scene had a very festive air.  Across the street from the beach were many shops including a McDonalds and an ice cream shop.After my meeting, I had a quick swim, went across the street and got an ice cream and sat down and enjoyed the scenery, including the nubile young surfing bodies of both sexes.  Wondering how I was going to get back to the hotel downtown, I saw a #333 bus that said Downtown.  I got  on it, tapped my Opal card for less than $4 and in about 30 minutes, I was home. It was wonderful -- and all by public transit, on a business trip yet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice neighborhood, with beautiful houses, great views, easy access, nice sands and waves, this beach is great for walking, bathing, eating or taking pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful trail, cool graffiti
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We hiked along the trail near Bondi Beach and ended there to chill. The graffati walls behind were cool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited in August so it was pretty much deserted. Don’t know why but it was smaller than I had imagined and very little in the way of cafes, restaurants or bars in the immediate area. A little disappointed really.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice big beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is one of the most famous beaches in Sydney. Big clean beach with lots of tourists but I find Manly beach more beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Trip with the inlaws
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The in laws enjoyed the bondi tour on the big bus when we hopped off. we had a few photos on the beach and had some yummy asian food around the main street. the kids enjoyed the sand and running around. very safe as police walk by the area and life guards are scattered too. toilets are on a quick access near the beach. walkable to shops and good views. just be mindful with your belongings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most popular beach in Sydney
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice each with lifesavers Change rooms and toilettes All sort of restaurants from budget to very pricy Transport is hideous to get to a train line from the city that never made it to the beach because of the residents but really inconvenient because you have to take buses to get their adding to the unnecessary travel timeParking is really difficult but at the end of all of this still the most popular touristic place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Synonymous with Aussie culture
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A melting pot of cultures flock to the ultimate Aussie beach, even in winter. The white, squeaky sand entices and the waves attracts the surfers - expert and beginners looking to try their hand at the beach culture. Easy access from the Sydney CBD via public transport, lots of food places around the esplanade. Probably easier to get there and get your own patch of sand in the off season as it’s out of control in summer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wouldn’t make my list of the worlds greatest beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Bondi on a cold, windy day so that probably influenced our poor impression of the place. Obviously a great place for surfers (which we aren’t) and the natural shape of the bay is interesting  but otherwise, with the crowds and fun fair rides on the waterfront we didn’t find it a very appealing place to linger.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. I've cold water..didn't stop them from enjoying the waves.V safe and cosmo.Wonderful outing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chillax
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach to go and relax. We went during winter (July) and it was obviously too cold to swim. But it still offers a great beach to relax on and great atmosphere around it. Very accessible by bus and overall would recommend to see - very picturesque

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the beach, people, vibe and the lifeguards. Great walks and lots to see. Kids enjoyed it and many selfies and photos were taken.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice and clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, must visit . Beautiful view from the topIf You like to swim, play, come prepared.Has lots of green grass close to the beach if u don’t prefer to get dirty and enjoy the scenic beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach even on a cool day.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the best beach and easy to get to on the bus.  The sand is very nice,the water is beautiful. We were there on a cool day but there were lots of surfers out and other brave people in the water. It’s a great place to people watch. We went for a swim at the bondi iceberg pool. It’s affordable and lots of fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bondi bondi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we were here in January.  the most famous beach in the world... and I can see why now ! it was extremely busy as apparently is the norm here. the day we were here the waters edge and about 50 meters into the water was full of washed up seaweed which made it difficult to get into the water without getting ones feet  tangled in it.  but once in... the water was amazing. the beach itself is much smaller than we had anticipated  but a very quirky place albeit.  Definately worth visiting if in Sydney  even  if only to sit and people watch. lots of lovely eateries on the prom also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great time on this Beach. It is beautiful, a bit smaller than expected but who cares. Such a great vibe in the area and the water was great for a bit of body surfing! We took the bus from downtown and it was really easy to get there and get back. fyi, if you have kids and are concerned about them seeing some topless ladies, then stay towards the east side of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ice skating
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited it during the winter and still it was fun and alive. We walked down the beach while the kids were ice skating, funny combination. Beautiful views of the beach and tons to see and eat.Great environment for all ages.It is a must when visiting Sydney, only 20 minutes by car/can.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Smaller than I thought, but beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Being a huge fan of Bondi Beach rescue of course I had to visit. It is smaller than appears on tv, however the beach is extremely clean, lifeguards friendly and scenery absolutely beautiful. It's a must see!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the world's best urban beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is probably Sydney´s most famous beach and for all the good reasons.As I already wrote in another review (Blue Mountains review), I consider Sydney a very lucky city since, geographically speaking, it got everything you need, including a spectacular coast.
