Bondi won't disappoint you, with its super clean water (we saw a group of dolphins) and white sand, great day and nightlife, its promenade full of delicious bars- restaurants...its natural swimming pools (some of them are artificial structures though...but they still get filled up by the sea water) and, for those who love surfing, waves are awesome. Water is not that warm though, but hey, is the Pacific Ocean! One thing that I truly like about Australia are their rules, and everybody respects them! The beach is no exception. I heard a lot of people complaining about the too many restrictions (including my favorite one, forbidden to smoke in public areas) that they put, but I like them all. You can't trust humans so better to take extreme measures! Australia should be taken as a world example regarding this aspect.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's alive!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi had extraordinary beach and amazing town. The beach was excellent just for laying down and enjoying the moment. The town offered varieties of stores and good foods. Getting there was not difficult, though took time because we used public bus. We recommend Bondi to you, particularly for extraordinary beach view and excellent foods.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go there during sunset!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The famous Bondi, a tad too crowded if you go during the day with families and everyone out.But if you go there near to sunset, it’s not as crowded and you get to see one of the most beautiful views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Harbour Bridge, Tick; Opera House, Tick; Bondi, Tick!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Mention Australia and a few things come to mind.  The Opera House, Harbour Bridge, Ayres rock and Bondi Beach.  Bondi beach is a go-to place for the tourist and there were plenty there when I visited.  The beach is huge and covered with lovely white sand.  As a people watching beach its fantastic, for sunbathing it is also fantastic and for surfing?  That is what it is known for.The facilities are excellent with showers to wash off the sand.  However, the beach is not the only place to visit in the area.  You must walk to Coogee beach which is wonderful albeit a little strenuous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean, white beach. Not calm waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: June 22, 2018–We went to see this, not swim here.The beach is clean. As a public beach, shower and toilet facilities are some distance from the edge of the water.The sand was powdery. Not white but yellowish.The waves appear to be apt for light surfers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Whilst it's a nice beach, it's a little too touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked from Sydney, where we were staying and came here to start the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk. The closest we got to the beach was the grass embankment.  The beach was full of people (it was a nice day), when you walk to Coogee you'll see plenty more beaches, with much more free space!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean and beatiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sydney's iconic beach. Place gets very crowded during hot days and you can sometimes spot a celebrity here and there. Beach is very clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is by far one of the best beaches in the city place to visit with your friends and family and assure you you are going to have a very good time

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is a Sydney icon and we visited on a bright sunny day. The beach itself is quite crowded and although we didn’t swim many others were enjoying the water. Nearby there are plenty of shops and places for good coffee. Parking though is difficult and expensive. Other nearby beaches are just as lovely and are a little less crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beach walk and sculpture trail
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our trip to Bondi  coincided with the Bondi to Bronte sculpture exhibition trail being on . Apart from the beautiful walk along the rocky shoreline, the sculptures provided us with much thought and discussion. If you can time your trip to Bondi during this exhibition, I would recommend it highly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fresh air
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you stay in the city take a break and get your ocean fresh air fix. Very relaxing with splendid walks all around.It also has a first class skatepark for intermediate to advanced riders.Easy to get there by buss from Bondi junction.Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Shame the weather was bad.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a beautiful beach. We love watching the Bondi rescue show.We went down to have a look but the weather was not to good. It was 12 degrees Celsius and blowing a gale of 60 kph. The sand was whipping through and stinging so we didn't stay to long. Just a quick look due to the weather. I will be going back again when the weather is better.Still worth a visit to have a look at this iconic place. I just hope the weather is better for you. Sunny and no wind and nice waves.Surfs up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cold breeze and sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi beach welcome us with great weather and cold breeze. The sands were very fine and cold and so was the clear sea water. It wasn’t crowded thought it was a Sunday, guess the reason was it wasn’t summer then. It was great to be close to nature with the sea gulls & beautiful waves. It definitely have to be on your bucket list.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not what I expected
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ok so we were a bit underwhelmed by this beach. Everyone knows about Bondi beach and supposedly brags they have been there. Honestly? I have been to more beautiful beaches before and I have heard there are more beautiful beaches in Australia. At least we have been and can now brag about it too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great iconic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hubby had never been to Bondi Beach before, so we took the #333 bus from the city (30 min trip). Eateries along the esplanade. Beautiful day for the beach when we were there. Famous for it’s tv show, Bondi Rescue. No filming that day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach with a dramatic ocean backdrop.  The walk along the top of the beach takes you past numerous little boutiques and restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This has to be one of the great beaches of the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The broad, long beach is clean and white, one half filled with beautiful young bodies, bronzed and sleek, some sunbathing, some surfing; the other half filled with married couples, young families, babies in carriages, toddlers and small children running around, the natural progression of the wilder side of the beach. We loved it.    It also helped that our stroll across the sand was preceded by a great meal at Icebergs, perched high above Bondi.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sun, Sand and Surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We got with the Red Bus, the only way to trave. When we arrived we walked along the main drag as there are many boutique shops to take a fancy to. Across the road is the famous Bondi Beach. Not much change to the Pavilion, you have toilets and change facility with many food and restaurant outlets.Take a walk along the boardwalk. If you did one end to the next it would probably be 2 or more km. Those people living on the cliffs on both sides in those apartments or houses have got one hell of a view. One of the best I'd say.Did not go for a dip but we wet our feet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The seagulls very cute
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Today is really cloudy,so not so much people in here.But the ocean still very beautiful.The seagulls are so cute,they even want to eat my watercolor!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Most Popular Beach in Australia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Bondi Beach is humongous! It is a beautiful beach with lots of people enjoying the sun. Many also were swimming in the ocean. Others were enjoying themselves with the waves. There was a pool for kids as well.Many had parasols. There was also a real swimming pool next to the ocean. That’s amazing!Some were enjoying the sun on the grass, outside of the beach. We walked around the whole beach. We enjoyed the smell of the ocean, the sun and the exercise. What a great day we had! Time for ice-cream!This is a must to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Aussie icon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We picked the worst day possible to visit this iconic beach as it was freezing & pouring with rain. Regardless, we had a good wander along the path & checked out the street art. We were blown away by what a big beach area it is & I could imagine how packed it would get on a beautiful summer day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Large sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Bondi Beach on a recent visit to Sydney and had a lovely afternoon there. We were lucky with the weather, the sun was shining and it was pleasantly warm so we saw the beach and surrounding area at it's best!There were quite a lot of people enjoying the beach, but there are no deckchairs or loungers for hire. Most people were sitting and lying on towels and a few had brought their own parasols

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super famous beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: How many times have we all seen Bondi beach on tv and in films?! Lovely curved beach of white sand with surfing waves rolling in. A very special place, not to be missed visiting Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Massive beach, good vibe!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is huge! Great for surfing (although I didn't surf!) but enjoyed watching those who were. There's a spot for swimmers too. There are plenty of restaurants and bars in the area and there's toilet facilities on the beach as well as a gym!! Thee beach also has some great graffiti around it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not Disappointing at all.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the beach today and although the weather wasn’t perfect the beach was still gorgeous - maybe even more so as it wasn’t packed with tourists! Beautiful views - a must see when in Sydney!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came to Bondi on a colder day but it was prefect! No wind sun was shining and wasn’t busy at all! Heaps of places around it to, to eat !! But be careful parking can be expensive in areas!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The location of the beach was awesome. The beach was beautiful indeed. It was a good place for surfing. We spent our half day at leisure here. Walked around the coast and had plenty of time to sit back relax and enjoy the beautiful view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved visiting this iconic site! Can take some time to get there via public transport but it is quite enjoyable. More trees would make the place better as you will burn fast without sunscreen. But if you protect yourself from the sun it is quite nice. I walked behind the club there as well to discover a Shakespeare play being practiced in a small Ancient Greek styled theatre. Can’t guarantee that’s what you’ll see when you go back there but if you happen to be around give it a little look, might find some other odd things happening back there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Over rated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Get put and explore further. It ok but there are better beaches. Some nice little restaurants but walk round the back streets to find some others. Pack in summer popular with the younger generation!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic Beach Must Do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My daughters and I returned to Bondi beach the day after their surfing lessons to swim and enjoy the sun and sand. There was plenty of room on the beach on this Friday in late March and the weather and water were perfect - 80 degrees and the water was refreshing.The boardwalk area is a bit of a tourist trap but we enjoyed walking along and had a wonderful lunch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go in winter!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I had been wanted that bondi was packed and a bit tacky. However I was there in winter and I had the whole place to myself! Was beautiful and easy to get to on the hop on hop off bus. Get the app for the bus so you can track when the next one is coming in though!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is where I want to retire to, what a fantastic place the sand the sea and the surf all amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What is says on the tin
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You have to visit BONDI ... rub the the soft sand ... grab a coffee at Lush ... try the fresh fish and chip shop ... choose your fish and then grill or fry ... its on the sea front Lovely place to walk. Relax.  Check out the buildings and see the many different influences ...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of Australia’s most recognisable beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Bondi Beach whilst in Sydney recently.My research showed that the quickest way to reach Bondi from the city was a train to Bondi Junction then a bus to Bondi. There are several buses one can catch from the train station at Bondi Junction. The station is located within the train station.Bondi Beach is one of Australia’s most recognisable beaches after Surfers Paradise. Its such an iconic beach destination. It is a picturesque and a virtually u shaped cove and beautiful white sand to match. Not as white and powdery though as beautiful Boracay in the Philippines.There are lifeguards on duty and this beach is the scene of the popular tv series Bondi Rescue, so be very careful when swimming here and do swim between the flags.The area is dotted with cafes, restaurants , bars, accommodation as well as backpacking accommodation.From the top of the hill one gets great sweeping views of Bondi Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everything and more even coming up to Winter.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the idyllic Beach living. Although I never did the surf lessons for injured knee - just swimming in those waves was so much fun. Great food on the beach front too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We also took the 333 or 380 bus, which is easy to do.  It's a nice beach with fine sand, but it is just a beach which you can find in so many places.  Lots of surfers and surf lessons going on.  We tried to eat lunch at the more moderately priced Icebergs restaurant but never found it, even after asking a few people who work at Icebergs other establishments.  Restaurants uptown were either not open for lunch or were very small with very small menus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can get here on a 333 bus from Circular Quay which goes straight  to Bondi? Glad we came even just to see others surfing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I was expecting more
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a nice enough beach, but very touristy and over priced. The beaches either side are much nicer and a better representation of Sydney.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A little Over Sold
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Bondi Beach on beautiful fall day. The sky was clear and the air was warm. The beach was not crowded. It is not as beautiful as the images. There is surfing and swimming. It is an ordinary beach and the scenery is just average. It is obvious that marketing is turned up for this beach and the surrounding area. Manly Beach is much more beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice beach with some restaurants and bars and many beautiful blonde Australian women who are very friendly and nice to talk to

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach and close to city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a fairly nice and moderately large beach close to the city. Which makes it continent to reach and enjoy. On the other hand it could be little crowded at times. Yellow sand and blue water makes a nice view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Smaller than it looks on tv
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We caught a bus here. It is quite cold at the end of May, but there were still some keen swimmers. The sand and beach is lovely. It's really not as big as it seems on the tv show. The beach itself is not super special, there are similar or even better ones in Queensland. However, the Santorini-like setting of houses around the beach as well as the amazing rocks makes this beach a lovely walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach near to city
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Takes abt 45-60 mins from city . Amazing beach .we went on weekday ,so pretty much no crowds.buses run quite frequently from city or Bondi junction

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can be Super Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is extremely popular and can be so packed that the sand is not visible.  The fresh ocean breeze makes for a nice walk along the walkway above the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Had to see Bondi Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We caught the number 333 bus from Circular Quay and just had enough money on our Opal Card! The beach was very busy with sunbathers and surfers alike. It’s worth a visit just to say that you’ve been to Bondi!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning and beautiful! At the evening we flew over Sydney in a helicopter ( which I recommend) and we could see it from bird eyes! The sunset was Amazing !!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just like what you see in the brochures and on tv. The beach itself is really clean and waves seems really good!Lots of seagulls around and also take a walk round the Bondi neighborhood where they have some fun shops to explore and backlanes full of good food!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good beach, but bit crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is clean and you will find lot of people there surfing, riding boats, and like me just walking and enjoying the atmosphere. You will find lot of eateries, shops selling clothing etc...I liked it but my personal choice will be St Kilda beach of Melbourne

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good to watch Surfers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Used the Hop on Hop off bus to get to Bondi plenty of bars and small cafes beach was good but thought Manley had more to offer.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just a beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bondi is not what it's hyped up to be. Don't get me wrong, the Icebergs are cool but that's all it has going for it. Bondi beach itself is crowded and in certain areas has a lot of trash. To grab a decent bite to eat you have to walk far up from the beach and there aren't many shops or good places to eat. It's very spread out and not easy to walk around. If you've only got a couple days in Sydney I would absolutely recommend going to Manly Beach instead. Way better experience for sure. Bondi is just a beach, whereas Manly is a whole day experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Picture paints a thousand words..Check out all the beautiful videos in YouTube. Lovely viewLovely beaches

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach awesome view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited this beach in morning around 9.30am. View was spectacular. You can swim or surf on this beach. Also you can walk further towards Coogee beach. I walked till Bronte beach (towards Coogee) and it was amazing experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Totally meets expectations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clean, sandy beach, not too crowded at this time of year. Plenty of good facilities including fresh water showers. Near to a large selection of shops and restaurants. As public beaches go, this is a good one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great stop for lunch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We wanted to see the beach we had heard so much about. We drive, parking was easy but not free. Beach was busy but we made it a lunch stop and ate at one of the outdoor boardwalk restaurants. There are many shops along the road well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awosme
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water was chillingly cold.. Though our toddler enjoyed.. But there were lots of stinging jelly fish.. We were made aware of it by a tourist.. So just careful

reviews.title: What a great day!
reviews.text: Bondi Beach was definitely a must see stop on our trip to Sydney. The beach was pristine. We went on a Tuesday and the area of beach where we parked our towels was not in the swimming area so it was somewhat secluded with just a few other visitors around us you were able to go into the water to Wade not Swim. We were able to splash and keep ourselves cool, which is about all I was inclined to do as a surf was very rough. The beach is simply beautiful. There's a nice pavilion where you can change and have restrooms and there was also a spot to have lunch were utilized all of the services. The restrooms and changing areas were very clean. We had beverages and pastries as an afternoon snack. My husband really enjoyed his pastry! It was about a 20 to 25 minute drive from the Fullerton hotel in Sydney. We spent the entire day and will be going back after a one day break from the sun.

reviews.title: Sydney visit from Perth
reviews.text: Visited Sydney for four days and did a boat trip to Manley beach, there was a surfing competition going on which was fun to watch. It was very busy lots going on everywhere due to the competition and crowds nice little shops to wander round and get you’re gifts, a lovely place to visit.Having got the bus to Bondi which was about 30 minutes we arrived and were pleasantly surprised the beach was lovely clean white sand and beautiful ocean. Cafe’s and bars a plenty market stalls with all different things of interest, The promenade walk was lovely as the beach curved around lots of people again sunbathing on a beautiful day. Both places had different vibes but equally good.In all we crammed a lot into our 4 days but loved every minute before returning to sunny Perth.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Stopped here on our way from Sydney to Bowral. There's plenty of parking. Somewhat strange was the payment of the parking fee, because you don't get a parking ticket at the end of the process. However, the police can trace that payment has been made by entering the license plate. The beach wr well attended and also some surfers in the water. Climbed past the poll the way in to look at some artwork. The stop was definitely worth it.

reviews.title: Post Tragedy
reviews.text: Visited the beach one day after the tragedy, the foreshore reserve area was still full as many had come laying flowers to pay respects to the victims, but the beachfront area was almost completely empty. That aside there's a skate ramp to the south end of the beach, and good sweeping views of the beach offered from up at Notts Avenue next to the Icebergs swimming club.

reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.text: Very attractive place and amazing view on the ocean. It's easy to get here from the center of Sydney by public bus. I didn't swim because of high waves, but it was lovely to spend time on the sand.

reviews.title: Iconic beach
reviews.text: Sydney’s most famous beach. Prone to dangerous currents. Swim between the flags or don’t swim at all if you don’t know how.

reviews.title: Classic
reviews.text: THE classic beach of Sydney and a good place to take your first dip as well. Lots of restaurants and pubs and a good place to carry on walking southbound along the coastal trek which is lovely

reviews.title: Bandya Mama - very similar to Coogee Beach.
reviews.text: Talk about Sydney and one won’t miss Bondi beach, its always in the list of travelers exploring Sydney. Not my favorite though, but the atmosphere here is happening somewhat, due to sculpture on stones, college crowd, sea gulls and a nice city beach vibe.I recently went to Bondi as one of my friends who came on Holidays to Sydney insisted, so decided at the last moment around 3:00 in the evening of Sunday and we drove to Bondi which was around 40 Kms from my place.

reviews.title: Best place for honeymoon
reviews.text: Best place to be for your honeymoon experience. Nice beach and environment. Pure breathtaking and winds. I recommend it to anyone.

reviews.title: For a walk
reviews.text: Nice beach. There are usually surfers.To the right over the hill there is a viewpoint.We had a hard time finding parking in the area. There are plenty of bars and joints for a drink.

reviews.title: My day at the beach
reviews.text: I made sand castles and pee'd in the water! (Review by my 6yo nephew). The water was cold. It was still fun though!.......

reviews.title: Good … but very windy
reviews.text: We visited this beach as a part if group tour. Unfortunately it was a windy day and bit cool too so we couldn’t go to splash the waves. Just watched the surfing activities from a distance. It had very long stretch of clear waters. Looked great

reviews.title: Iconic beach. Crowded on Australia Day Monday
reviews.text: This is the most iconic beach of Sydney, even the name that comes to mind to first-time visitors when thinking of beaches in Australia as a whole. Bondi was  and technically is still a suburb of Sydney although urban sprawl means the 2 are contiguous now. The beach is the closest to the city’s CBD and most easily accessed from Circular Quay where we were staying by bus (379).  Our friends, however, picked us up and drove us there.It was the Monday of the Australia Day weekend holiday and the beach and surrounding area was packed. Needless to say the parking lots were full and we were lucky to find a spot.  We elected to stay on the grass under the trees closer to the parking lots rather than hang out on the sand. The younger ones among us swam while we walked along the beach and  sidewalks enjoying the view. There were many surfers making the most of the waves rolling in.We spent a couple of relaxing hours people-watching and enjoying the views and energetic vibes of Bondi

reviews.title: Overrated location - but stop by if you're in town anyway
reviews.text: If you’ve been on Australia’s east coast for a while and seen the typical and less prominent locations, you’ll have a somewhat sober view of Bondi Beach.It is a place with a lot of see-and-be-seen factor. Of course,ä is also surfed there as on many other beaches.The lagoon on the right edge of the beach is world-renowned, but as good as any major beach resort in Queensland. And New South Wales has such a lagoon. However, it differs in that it is permanently filled by the waves of the sea, or water flows back into the sea.  At Bondi Beach, there is not much else that would not be in the form or other popular beaches, except for the sculptures on the boardwalk that winds southward from the beach and offers a beautiful view of the surrounding area. Quite typical of Australia is further that the beach offers no shade, no trees, no umbrellas etc apart from a few picnic pavilions at the car park. You just sizzle in the sun in front of you.All in all, so, on, quite a place, but not as spectacular as it is often portrayed. Places like Byron Bay, or Airlie Beach, I think offer at least as much. Surfers Paradise beach is much longer and also offers plenty of glamour.For Sydney residents, the beach is of course an absolute hotspot, as it is right on the doorstep.

reviews.title: Special place
reviews.text: We went on a Saturday so it was busy…..  full of life and fascinating to watch the movement.Many many training schools on view………. Quite a few for children all in bright orange tops.The sand is soft and white.Deserves its reputation

reviews.title: Iconic
reviews.text: Got to be done right? It’s iconic for its  surf scene and the Icebergs swimming pool. Plenty of people on the beach and in the water. Was a little surprised that the T4 train didn’t take you closer than Bondi junction so whilst we had anticipated a fair walk I just wonder why the line was never extended. That said it was nice to just sit and people watch.

reviews.title: City 2 Surf - Bondi Beach Finish Line
reviews.text: City2Surf Finish Line and one of the prettiest and scenic finish line for a Fun Run in Australia.  Plenty of space even on a crowded event such as the City2Surf.

reviews.title: Bondi beach with its golden sand and clear blue waters
reviews.text: Bondi beach as a top tourist destination is great for swimmimg and strolling.The golden sand with its clear blue waters is best for great photos.

reviews.title: One of the best beaches in Oz!
reviews.text: Love Bondi, can easily see why this beach is so popular. Be careful of blue bottles though, if they are washed up on beach they can still sting.

reviews.title: There are cute shops around the beach
reviews.text: We took a bus from central Sydney.The landscape seen in the photo is in front of you and you can enjoy it to some extentWe did not go into the sea, but we enjoyed a snack while looking out at the sea, and it was funThe restaurant seemed more open at night.It doesn't seem like security is bad.

reviews.title: Bondi
reviews.text: A beautiful beach with loads of energy. Great for people-watching, surfing, or just soaking up the sun. Only downside is it gets packed (yes I know), especially on weekends, so don’t expect peace & quiet. Still, it’s a must-visit if you’re in Sydney.

reviews.title: Very Average
reviews.text: I personally find Bondi beach very average. Sydney has more than 100 beaches that are better than Bondi. Parking is very difficult and expensive.

reviews.title: Not the most picturesque but iconic Australian beach
reviews.text: Probably the best known surf beach in SydneyPaid it a visit at the start of a walk down the eastern shores to Coogee to meet relatives Frontage a bit tired (reminded me of a uk seaside town) but nice beach and surfquite busy - not too busy but it is their winter

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text: Loved it here. Such a great spot. It’s public, beautiful and spacious.I’d highly recommend coming here. It’s gorgeous and relaxing.

reviews.title: Over-hyped and under-whelming
reviews.text: What a let-down!! The so-called incredible beach at Bondi is nothing special. I have seen prettier and more exciting beaches at the Great Ocean Road (west of Melbourne) as well as all over Europe (Netherlands, France, Portugal, Italy and Croatia) and the US (Florida). Maybe Bondi Beach has a surf-culture that makes it special, but even that did not show when we were there: maybe a dozen surfers out there that laid more on their board than that they actually surfed. A waste of my time. 😞

reviews.title: Bondi beach, sydney
reviews.text: Bondi beach sydney ...Winter with sunny day, looks bondi beach so busy ....Surrounding by people activities such, running, sunbathing, swimming, playing around .....

reviews.title: Worth the hype
reviews.text: We took the ferry from Circular Quays to Rosewater Bay and from there got the bus down to Bondi Beach which took around 20 minutes. Bondi Beach is exactly how people describe it. It’s a vibrant, busy beach which is perfect for surfing and swimming. There are plenty of places to eat and drink along the beach and different walks that you can take along the coastline. If you are into fitness, there is an outdoor gym space. Get the bus back into the city from Bondi Junction.

reviews.title: Bondi
reviews.text: So we didn’t realise we went to Bondi on a public holiday…boy, was it busy!!  However… we still had a great day!  The sea was clean and warm; plenty of activities, shopping and food outlets around.  Do the Bondi to Coogee walk… you won’t regret it!

reviews.title: Relaxing and Iconic Beach Spot in Sydney
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is a stunning spot in Sydney with golden sand, clear waves, and a great vibe. Whether you're swimming, surfing, or just relaxing by the water, it's a perfect place to unwind. Plenty of cafés and the scenic coastal walk make the visit even better. Definitely worth it!

reviews.title: Sun, surf and sydney vibes
reviews.text: We joined locals gathering at Bondi on a gloriously sunny day and immediately understood its appeal. The atmosphere was electric with a perfect mix of relaxation and activity.

reviews.title: My opinion - over rated !
reviews.text: Bondi beach - well, iconic beach in Sydney and probably most widely known globally.In my opinon - Surfer's Paradise / Gold Coast is better than Bondi beach. This is in terms of general crowd, weather, facilities, cafe/pub/restaurant in/around the beach.However, many will differ wrt Bondi beach vis a vis Gulf Coast / Surfer's Paradise.

reviews.title: Beautiful ❤️
reviews.text: Everything you want in a beach, soft sand, clear water, waves and  a beautiful view. There's shops a short walk away where you can find  great sushi, pizzas and Anita's ice creams. There's also swimwear boutiques that made me wish I hadn't bought one in the UK, and obviously everything a surfer needs, a Billabong T actually from Australia is a must buy !

reviews.title: A bucket list place, But I dont know why.
reviews.text: Well, If you are visiting Sydney, you just have to visit Bondi Beach its a bucket list place.. But in all Honesty, I could not understand what all the fuss is about... Its just a beach, and not too spectacular at that. I suppose it was not helped by the fact it was a cool miserable sort of day, no glistening sunshine.. We used the hop on and off bus to go there .. There is also a couple of cafes, with a limited range of food.. Nice murals along the sea wal... lAnd that is it really..

reviews.title: You have to visit them!
reviews.text: I love this place! The food is really good! I recommend sushi, meat from grill and salted fish. Always when I'm there, I have a lot of fun with stuff and live music. Salva and Munir always take care about good atmosphere so every time I come back with pleasure!

reviews.title: As impressive in reality as on TV
reviews.text: Beautiful unmissable beach easily accessible from the centre of Sydney!I recommend taking the boat from Circular Quay to Rose Bay Wharf. Just walk and cross the Bellevue Hill neighborhood to Bondi.

reviews.title: Beautiful but busy
reviews.text: People always say Bondi Beach is a must-visit in Sydney, so I decided to check it out.The beach itself is beautiful, but it felt a bit too touristy and crowded for my taste. That said, I did find a few nice cafes around the area that are great for relaxing and people-watching.Bondi is definitely iconic, especially known for its surf and coastal walk—but probably better if you don’t mind the crowds.

reviews.title: Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is a world-famous destination known for its stunning coastline, golden sands, and energetic surf scene. Whether you're an experienced surfer or just looking to relax by the shore, Bondi offers a picturesque setting with breathtaking ocean views. The surrounding area is filled with lively cafes, coastal walks, and vibrant street art, making it a perfect spot for both adventure and relaxation. With its welcoming atmosphere and iconic beauty, Bondi Beach is a must-visit for anyone exploring Sydney.

reviews.title: A must see beach
reviews.text: I had a blast while in Sydney. Got a chance to learn to surf and see the lifestyle it has in the area. Beautiful view and vibe.

reviews.title: Joyful place
reviews.text: Incredible place, beach awesome. the only issue is that the shop fronts facing the beach were very touristie. I would recommend back streets

reviews.title: Riesiger Strand
reviews.text: Toller, riesiger Strand. Perfect for walking, relaxing but also for swimming. Either in the nature pool or in the sea.

reviews.title: A Scenic and Popular Destination with a Lively Atmosphere
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is undoubtedly one of Sydney’s most iconic and beautiful beaches, offering a pristine stretch of golden sand and clear, inviting waters. The beach is well-maintained, making it an excellent spot for various activities, whether you're swimming, surfing, or simply enjoying the coastal views.The surrounding area is vibrant, with a variety of cafes, restaurants, and shops offering both casual and more refined dining options. The convenience of having amenities close by enhances the overall experience, making it a great place to spend a day.However, it’s important to note that Bondi Beach can become quite crowded, especially during peak tourist seasons or weekends. The large crowds can sometimes detract from the tranquility one might expect from a beach outing. Additionally, the parking can be challenging, with limited spaces available around the area, making access a bit more difficult for those driving.Overall, Bondi Beach remains a must-visit destination for both locals and tourists. It offers a dynamic, lively atmosphere, combined with beautiful scenery and a wide range of activities. While it can be busy at times, the beach’s appeal and offerings make it well worth the visit.

reviews.title: Beautiful & dangerous
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I've ever been to. Listen to the frickin lifeguards and you'll be fine! Read the signs and stay within the flags. I'm a strong swimmer who knows the ocean, and this is the toughest ocean experience I've had. I loved it, and my partner did too, but you should be aware of the ocean here and trust the lifeguards and flags as a result. Don't go in too deep - the undertow is very strong. We were stung by bluebottles, but the signs were up, so it was no surprise, and we got through it just fine.

reviews.title: Sydney Beach, although a little too touristy, is still a stunning spot.
reviews.text: For a more intimate experience, you can take a lovely walk along the coast to Clovelly. It’s a much quieter and more peaceful area, making it a great escape from the crowds.Just minutes from the heart of Sydney, this beautiful sandy beach offers great views and a lively atmosphere. It's a fantastic surf spot, and the outdoor pool is perfect for watching the surfers' performances while also being a place to see and be seen.

reviews.title: Iconic location worth visiting
reviews.text: spent the day in the Bondi area, easy to get to from Sydney by bus, we swam in the iconic Icebergs Pool, sad to see it was damaged by storm weather after our visit.   We walked along the beach and then to the shops, had fantastic brunch in one of side streets.  Loved the vibe and when we were there it wasn't too busy, bucket list item ticked off on my Australian travels.

reviews.title: Enjoyed the views and a gelato
reviews.text: Last stop on our tour, time enough allowed to visit the beach, enjoy the views or a snack. We choose to enjoy the views as we headed to the gelato outlet nearby.  A good number of the 'beautiful' people enjoying the beach, a few peacocks flexing their muscles and showcasing bronzed torsos, many of the peahens equally interesting. Great vibe in the area.

reviews.title: The Famous Aussie Beach itself !
reviews.text: The great famous Aussie beach ! Shops, bars, restaurants the famous Icebergs !It has everything for a great day or evening out ! Great coastal walks too !

reviews.title: Nice area
reviews.text: We went here for a few hours.  The beach is wide and looks like it would be nice on a day with better weather.  The waves were massive today!  The beach is surrounded by a main street with a few shops and lots of small restaurants.  We took the 333 bus from the city but there are other ways to get there.

reviews.title: Picturesque beach
reviews.text: We visited this famous beach as part of a group tour. This was a windy day, after a cool front had just come in. The beach looked very nice, with good rolling waves. There some men working out and showing off. Near the beach, we had a brief tour of the Bondi Surf Bathers Life Saving Club, established in 1907. A nice place and well-worth a visit.

reviews.title: Best view of Bondi for photos
reviews.text: The best view and to take photos of Bondi is the high footpath on Campbell parade just near the North Bondi RSL. A beautiful view facing south. Bondi is one of the great city beaches of the world. It’s a majestic wide fine sand beach. There is nearly always somewhere relatively calm to swim. Pools, close to shore etc.

reviews.title: Busy place! Listen to the  life guards
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is an absolute icon! The golden sand, rolling waves, and buzzing atmosphere make it a must-visit in Sydney. The surf is amazing, but it can be dangerous if you don’t follow the flags and listen to the lifeguards—they’re there for a reason! It gets super busy, so expect crowds, but that’s part of the experience. Tip: Bring plenty of water and sunscreen because the Aussie sun is no joke!

reviews.title: Busy beach with lots to do
reviews.text: Such a fun time! Easily accessible by transit. Parking (especially free parking) was exceptionally hard to find. Lots of amenities around the beach - change rooms, wash rooms, restaurants, outdoor gym, water fountains, etc... The beach is patrolled by many lifeguards, so we felt very safe. The north end (farthest from the Icebergs pool) is by far the calmest area. If you are into surfing the south end is the best. This is definitely not a "float around in the water" type of beach - the waves are quite big but great for body-surfing. The actual beach can get crowded, but it is so big that finding a spot to set up is not difficult. Stay between the flags!

reviews.title: Disappointing. Too big, too crowded, too dirty.
reviews.text: Very disappointing. Very much mill in the sand, great distance to the water, strong waves, no umbrellas or sunbeds for rent. It wasn't fun.We stayed at 4 beaches in Sydney. Dear Manly Beach.

reviews.title: Fun to check off of the Sydney bucket list
reviews.text: As something that is a must do on a Sydney bucket list, I had a good time. The beach is nice and there’s lots of room to spread out from others. If you want to swim, north side is for you, surfers are on the south side. It was fun watching surf school and the professionals. There are umbrellas for rent on the boardwalk - I believe the sign said $15/hr. Lots of lifeguards and surf patrol making sure everyone is ok. It enjoyed it a lot but if you want less of an “attraction” there are prettier, quieter beaches to the south of Bondi.

reviews.title: Sunny afternoon at Bondi Beach.
reviews.text: The beach itself is not special, but people and animals add a lively and relaxed flavour to it. Enjoy a nice sunny afternoon here! Very good experience, love comes from above the sea.

reviews.title: Fun with friends
reviews.text: Amazing pristine beaches with a swimming pool pristine white sand turquoise blue water excellent surf conditions boutique shopping in Sydney. I went with a group of friends and had a really great day in the sun. Don’t forget to slip slop slap because the sun is strong.

reviews.title: Great place to holiday plenty to do for the kids and lovely places to go out and enjoy a fantastic meal fantastic place.
reviews.text: Amazing place great spot for kids . We loved every single thing about the area the weather was amazing and the people where lovely

reviews.title: Great holiday!
reviews.text: Love trip advisors they look after you all the way, One of my most memorable holidays trip away! Thanks guys!  Can't wait too see you again!

reviews.title: Poo  beach
reviews.text: What a poo beach.  No reason for coming other claiming going to Bondi.Dirty and run down.Sand was full of rubbish.Don’t waste your time go to the other beaches down the coast

reviews.title: Ocean dive
reviews.text: An amazingly huge beach for sunbathing and dive into the Pacific Ocean! The waves are great for surfing as well! The sand as smooth and you can walk without shoes!

reviews.title: Must go
reviews.text: Amazing beach, clear water I have been here many times with my family and it is the most wonderful beach ever it is sometimes a little crowded but over all it is beautifulTips:Go early in the morning it is less crowded and the sunrise is amazing Grab an ice cream from Anita’s or Messina’s (I think Messina is better) and sit at the beach

reviews.title: Go elsewhere for cleaner water and better waves.
reviews.text: There are far better beaches in Sydney. Try Manly, Palm Beach, Coogee for example. Bondi is for tourists, the locals know where the water is cleaner

reviews.title: Love the Beach and plenty of Bars & Restaurants
reviews.text: We jumped on a government bus in Sydney city centre to Bondi Beach just for day trip  It's about 40-45 mins depending on traffic, but worth it to see a bit of Sydney and it's suburbs.   These buses run past Bondi beach almost every 5-6 minutes so it was easy to jump on a bus back to the city.  They don't take cash though so make sure you have a contactless card to board. Bondi beach is a superbly clean beach, well guarded with experienced lifeguards to keep you safe if you're venturing into the waves, which can be very high and there's a strong RIP current to watch out for in certain parts of the beach.  Best advice is swim between the flags!    The facilities are excellent, with showers and toilets all free to use in the changing area.  It's a lovely building with a few shops with local artisan pottery, a small art gallery and clothing stores.     There are a few restaurants directly on the beach in this same area so easy to grab drinks, snacks or lunch without having to go to far.  Above the beach there's some good independent shops for Australian clothing/swim gear etc (go to Budgy Smugglers for some iconic Australian trunks and swimsuits).Overall, we enjoyed the beach, and the small town.  It's not huge (think Margate), but if you're a keen surfer it's ideal.

reviews.title: My favourite beach
reviews.text: Frankly, I am not sure what makes it so attractive to holidaymakers. But I can name at least three reasons for this. Firstly, it is located closest to the city centre, in the Bondi area, about 20 minutes by bus to the City. There is a bus from the beach to the centre. The second reason is that there is a large shopping centre not very far from the beach, so people can combine shopping with a beach holiday. There are also buses and trains from the shopping centre to the city centre. Thirdly, it is quite large, 3 times larger than Kudzhi Beach, which I wrote about earlier.

reviews.title: A certainty
reviews.text: Wonderful beach and full of young people. There are no services (except rescue), but it is beautiful for that. Recommend

reviews.title: super
reviews.text: Bondi Beach – The most famous beach in this city. Of course, there was a lot going on here. The waves were relatively big, but people were bathing. There were also free toilets available.

reviews.title: A day at Bondi
reviews.text: A day spent at bondi is definitely worth it, but would advise getting there early if looking to park nearby.Some nice food places to grab an early breakfast or snack at lunchtime.We ventured into the iceberg pools at the end of the beach, $10 each for the day well worth it if you want to have a dip without all the sand.As with all the places we visited the cleanliness is of a high standard.Can’t wait to get back there one day

reviews.title: Don't stop knowing!
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with a sophisticated atmosphere, beautiful people and many shops, restaurants and good beach! There is a swimming pool that you can pay to just take drops or to enjoy. Many surfers and great places for photos.

reviews.title: Beaches in Australia
reviews.text: It's amazing. Another continent, another world. Be sure to visit, and certainly not in the European summer, but in the Australian!!!

reviews.title: Bondi beach is a great place for a swim
reviews.text: Beautiful beach not far from the city center. You can take a bus and you will reach Bondi beach i haft an hour. There, you find nice restaurants, shops and coffee shops. A nice little excursion on a hot day.

reviews.title: Wow, what a wonder full experience
reviews.text: Clean and clear, one of the most active beach. I was able to experience a walk early in the morning and access the beach with showers to rinse off the sand.

reviews.title: A nice beach but even better starting point for the Bondi to Coogee walk
reviews.text: It’s a beautiful and famous beach and while I did enjoy my time here, I definitely recommend walking a little bit along the Bondi to Coogee walk because there are so many better beaches along the way that are way less busy. But the Icebergs poolon the Bondi beach is nice and it wasn’t crowded.

reviews.title: Great energy, lots to do, eat and drink.
reviews.text: Bondi is a beautiful location, huge open beach with a big prom to walk along. The pavilion was always buzzing with energy when we were there. A huge amount of food and drink option. There were tonnes of surfers out and people swimming and playing ball games ect on the beach. Yet very clean and well kept. You can also walk between the beaches on a costal path. The place has a great energy.

reviews.title: Relaxing day at the beach.
reviews.text: Wonderful beach very close to the center of Sydney.White sand clear and cold waters small wave enough world but there is plenty of room for your towel.Highly recommended for a relaxing day on the beach.

reviews.title: Sun, Sand, and Endless Summer Vibes
reviews.text: A visit to Bondi Beach is a must for any traveler to Sydney. It's a place where you can relax, rejuvenate, and immerse yourself in the vibrant coastal culture.

reviews.title: Sydney Beach, although a little too touristy
reviews.text: Beautiful sandy beach just minutes from the centre of Sydney. Beautiful surf spot and incredible outdoor pool to both admire the surfers' performances and see and be seen.Departure of a very nice walk along the coast to Clovely much more intimate

reviews.title: What an awesome place to go!
reviews.text: Bondi Beach’s full of energy and surf culture. The clear water and reliable waves combined with the breathtaking coastline makes Bondi Beach iconic and picturesque. The Graffiti Wall, which changes every now and then, complements the vibrant atmosphere of the beach as well. So many fun things to do around the beach too! The beachside offers decent restaurants, cozy cafes and great shopping. Definitely a chill hang out place in Sydney! These all explains why Bondi Beach attracts thousands of tourists and locals to visit.The beach is absolutely easy to access by public transport. If you’re taking a train, you can go to Bondi Junction Station first and transfer by bus. There are also different direct buses from CBD. Either way takes you 30-45 minutes. Include this spot in your must-go list!

reviews.title: Loved Bondi Beach
reviews.text: We visited Bondi in early March. It was a fairly warm day, but it happened to be sprinkling. This small bit of rain guaranteed we had the swimmers section of the beach ENTIRELY to ourselves. The water was warm, the waves were so fun to play in. We had the absolute best time. After we were done playing in the water, we went and got crepes nearby at a creperie, then went and got some great Bondi Beach shirts. Such a fun and memorable day at a great, historic beach. We would go back.

reviews.title: Historic beach not worth the hype. Manley beach more fun to get to and better vibe
reviews.text: Historic beach one felt one had to visit but felt overrated. Got there by train and bus from CBD 30min approx. Got off the bus a little early and saw the area towards the beach; not exciting a little down at heal like a lot of English seaside resorts. Beach was quite, as weather had not yet reached summer temp. Nevertheless the Manley beaches are much better and more fun to get too with a 20min fast ferry ride

reviews.title: The place to be!
reviews.text: The name speaks for itself. The heart of Sydney, the place to be. Don’t need to say a lot about this place. Pristine white sand and crystal clear water, everything you could ever want is on and around Bondi. Gets crowded in the afternoon but that comes with the name. Despite that, the beach is spotless

reviews.title: A Beach Anyone on a Trip to Sydney Must Visit
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is perhaps Sydney's most notable beach - and quintessential to Aussie culture. So, if you're visiting Sydney, head on over. An easy way to get there is the bus terminal across from Westfield Shopping Mall at the bus depot. Take bus # 333 and it will let you out at Bondi. Also, the stop before that is the famous Bondi Icebergs, which overlooks Bondi Beach, the ocean pool and ocean in general. It's a famed place that you don't want to miss - but it is a little tucked away. Take the same bus. Get off the stop before you get to the beach, cross the road and you'll see it on your left.

reviews.title: Good to visit but didn’t live up to the hype!
reviews.text: Bondi is obviously a must do when you visit Sydney and was a good one to tick off however we found that the actual beach didn’t live up to the hype and can be extremely busy in peak season, on top of that there wasn’t loads to do in the surrounding area. Furthermore, we found that other beaches in the area such as Manly beach were in our opinion far better and had more to do on the actual beach and in the area surrounding.

reviews.title: Must see?
reviews.text: Bondi is a must visit just to say you have! Full of mainly young people surfing and posing on the beach. Loads of eateries and bars.If you have take out food, (fish and chips!) watch out for the seagulls!!Best to go by public transport because parking is near impossible!

reviews.title: Its Bondi
reviews.text: We stayed in Bronte and did the cliff walk to Bronte a couple of times which is plenty but can get crowded.Bondi beach itself is only 1km so not huge but sandy and surfi with plenty of folk enjoying.Its famous and many flock there, but not as many restaurants as I thought there might be on the front.

reviews.title: after watched it in tv show, finally i have a chance to visit bondi beach. and its amazing
reviews.text: What a wonderful beach. Australia is so lucky it has many beautiful sandy beaches so close to the city. when i visited australia, i only visited Bondi and Manly. Bondi is more famous because of one of the TV show. i love this place. there is kids friendly pool for safe swimming, the sand is so soft and clean. many cafes, and very easy to access by bus.

reviews.title: Serene beach for vacationers
reviews.text: Its a pristine and beautiful beach for beach surfers. Excellent beach outing for family as well as water sport enthusiasts. The well made promenade is well laid n maintained giving opportunity for joggers n fitness lovers. Wind sand with aquamarine water is a delight to our eyes. One of the very good places of interest near Sydney.

reviews.title: Definitely coming again! Great beach!
reviews.text: Very good experience, lots of sand to play with :). There were loads of sunbathers, so snag a spot earlier in the day if you like it. We enjoyed shopping in one of the coastal shopping villages; so awesome! Definitely coming again.

reviews.title: Water and more
reviews.text: One of the main and famous beaches around Sydney. Nice area for a tan and swim. Also famous for the Iceberg pool by the ocean

reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.text: Pretty crowded, but still worth a visit. Public transport is probably the best option to get here if you're not a local as parking is tricky.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is a gem! The golden sands, vibrant surf, and lively atmosphere make it a must-visit. Perfect for sunbathing, swimming, and people-watching. The coastal walk offers stunning views and the local dining scene is fantastic. A true Sydney highlight

reviews.title: It's just a beach
reviews.text: Sure it is a famous beach. It is clean, shops and restaurants around and there are nice houses with a view of the beach. But in the end, it is just a beach. The nice thing is that it is a stop on the hop on/hop off bus. We were there on a relative cold day. Not many people around, just some people surfing. We had the beach practically to ourselves. I can imagine that with more people around there is more of a vibe

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: I really liked Bondi Beach. The vibe is really cool and there are nice restaurants and cafes around the area. Lots of swimming and surfing also. The view on Icebergs Pool is legendary.

reviews.title: Wanted to go for years. Bit of an anti climax in reality
reviews.text: Always wanted to go. Finally made it on Christmas Day 2023 . It was ok, but something of an anti climax. I've been to many better sandy beaches.

reviews.title: Worth a photo stop
reviews.text: Beautiful views, highly priced shops and very busy even in winter. Would suggest q quick visit unless surfing is your thing.

reviews.title: Bondi beach steak rewies
reviews.text: we were a group of 16 friends. many of us ordered meat medium rare and got shoe sole as steak. we complained and were then served completely raw beef. and one of the gang didn't get their order until everyone else had finished. Very bad entrecote but good burger.

reviews.title: A nice beach but nothing super special
reviews.text: It’s very clean and it looks stunning, but at the end of the day it’s just a beach. It’s very crowded, even in winter, so it’s probably not the best choice if you want a calm beach day. Unless you are big into the surfing scene etc. you might find this kind of boring.

reviews.title: Very busy beach
reviews.text: Small but busy beach right off the street. Too crowded for us to feel comfortable swimming. Still worth a trip just to say we went. We grabbed some drinks and snacks and had a little picnic.

reviews.title: Lovely
reviews.text: We visited during the off season and everything was absolutely lovely. The beach was not crowded and the water was decently warm for the season. We got to visit lots of shops and restaurants on the beach that were very nice.

reviews.title: Didn’t disappoint beautiful beach
reviews.text: Bondi Beach was a must-visit for me because of its legendary status, and it certainly lived up to the hype. The beach is stunning, with plenty of surfers and people enjoying the sun and sea. The area also offers great shopping and lots of restaurants, making it a must-visit destination.

reviews.title: Not the best
reviews.text: I lived on the island for years. That's one of the reasons the beach didn't impress me. Nice restaurants around and parking facilities available.In my opinion probably overrated.

reviews.title: Bondi is a state of mind
reviews.text: Iconic beach living on its reputation. Bondi is not the most scenic beach in the world, it lacks the white coral sand, it is not all that big or long, the surfing doesn’t seem all that particular. I guess Bondi is more a state of mind more so than anything else.

reviews.title: Great place for early morning walks
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is always worth a visit, it is very touristy and there are many other notable beaches but it is still an iconic place that is definately worth a visit whilst in the Sydney area. On our most recent stay we visited quite often in the early mornings before first light when it was busy with joggers doing the Bondi circuit. There have been some changes since the pandemic but it is still a beach that has great appeal.

reviews.title: TV beach
reviews.text: Nice to have been here, easy to take bus 333 from Hyde Park here. 20 minutes and you are there. Good weather and it was a relaxing afternoon on the beach. As for the beach, of course it's lovely sand, but there are many other beaches that are at least as good or better

reviews.title: Excellent clean beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with nice soft sand. Got crowded as we went on a Sunday but the atmosphere was great.  Restaurants next to it are pretty expensive..

reviews.title: Must see in Sydney
reviews.text: Great and above all clean beach. Easy to reach by public transport. But on the weekend it's more of a matter of luck to get a place.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach + coastal walk
reviews.text: Parking in the area is 10AUD per hour. Went there on a week day and it was crowded and with a lot of traffic. Better to go as early as possible. You can go in the water but being careful. Water was nice and clear. The coastal walk is beautiful.

reviews.title: Unique Experience
reviews.text: If you like the ocean and watching/participating in surfing, this place is amazing.  It is HUGE.  For me, a walk up and down the beach was a perfect distance.  There are some elite beaches in  the world and  this is one of them.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach.
reviews.text: A very famous & pretty beach but crowded (it was the weekend though) with shops selling very over priced coffee & ice cream. I ventured down to the water & OMG it was FREEZING!!  Being a soft Brit, I was expecting the water to be a bit warmer than it is in Cornwall but the sand made up for it - so soft, it was like walking on air.When visiting Australia for the first time, you gotta do these things & find out for yourself that it's not all hot weather, warm water & kangaroos - but it is awesome :-)

reviews.title: Nice Beach
reviews.text: We did the walk from Coogee to Bondi and it is a nice long walk, about an hour.  Had lunch at Iceburg Pools (bring ID) and took pictures of the famous pool and beach.  Then walked to the beach, nice clean large beach.  No need for watershoes, the sand is soft.

reviews.title: Jumped at Christmas
reviews.text: Sydney's mythical beach, at Christmas it's fun for families with temperatures approaching 40 degrees, a surfer's paradise

reviews.title: Amazing Beach
reviews.text: Most gorgeous beach with iconic coastal views. You’ll get the best vacation pictures of your life here so head back at sunset. Bondi has a very strong current so keep your sunglasses in your bag or you’ll get hit by a wave and lose them like I did. Be sure to swim between the flags and wear plenty of sunblock. Don’t be deceived by the clouds.

reviews.title: Bondi beach
reviews.text: It was very good. Beautiful scenery and vibe. It is hot with no shade so bring sunscreen. And make sure to swim inside the flags

reviews.title: Nice, nothing really special
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, smaller than I thought, just wanted to go there and check it outNice to check off my bucket list but Australia has beautiful beaches everywhere

reviews.title: Not for me
reviews.text: So while the beach itself and the Bondi town is lovely, the crowds are too much for me to take. This starts as soon as you get to the Bondi Junction to get on the bus and continues non stop. It's a pity, as the beach is really nice - somehow the area developed into a tourist trap (to give you an idea, a small bottle of water costs $5).

reviews.title: Australia Icon....wear a hat and use sunblock!
reviews.text: I watch Bondi Rescue frequently. We heard Manly and it's area is nicer to visit. Everyone has heard of Bondi. We went on a beautiful, warm day on a Sunday in January. We got there around 11 am and spent an hour there. We had our bathing suit on, but the water was a bit cold for us. Tickled to death to see the lifeguard building,   lifeguards, surfers,  and the beach. The sand is very fine. A real family beach. Lots of activity of little kids to seniors doing lifeguard camp/training . Another thrill was seeing the Iceberg pool. Shark nets and boars keep an eye out for those unwanted sharks. Took a cab VA using a ferry , or bus. Restaurants nearby. A bit touristy, but around 1 pm it started to get very busy.

reviews.title: Iconic beach
reviews.text: Great beach, we went on a Monday so it wasn’t super busy. The water was clear, the lifeguards putting up the red and yellow flags always makes us feel safe. Lots of restaurants and shops on the Main Street.

reviews.title: Iconic Beach
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is iconic, probably the most famous beach in the world. I loved it. People are chilled, beach is great. I was surprised that the sea wasn't as warm as I'd expected. Once you are in the water, it's great. The surf smashes into you and really takes you off your feet. If you have children, they will need you around in the water with them. Great place.

reviews.title: Beach time
reviews.text: Visited this Iconic beach setting in Sydney.  Glad I went, but not as good as Manly Beach.  Plenty of shops and restaurants, but a little pricey!

reviews.title: Iconic surfing beach in Sydney.
reviews.text: Iconic beach in Sydney, especially for surfers, it is very large and open, but what we really liked was taking the walk along the coast from Coogee, about 6 kilometers of walk where you pass other beaches such as Gordon's Bay, Clovelly Beach, Waverly Cemetery, Bronte Beach, Tamarama Beach, ending in Bondi.On the beachfront you can enjoy multiple fast food restaurants.Must visit in Sydney.

reviews.title: Now to the 4th course
reviews.text: Bondi. Excellent views. With a pool looking over the sea. Would recommend the bars & restaurants. With a balcony view. With amazing desserts.

reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.text: We had to go to Bondi at least once while we were in Sydney and it was worth it.  The waves were amazing and we had a great time playing in them.  They do get quite large so you need to pay attention and know what you are doing.  We also walked the path  south of the beach and the views are fantastic.

reviews.title: Fabulous beach -better for fun or surfers than swimmers.
reviews.text: approx 25 mins from the city or airport Bondi beach is an amazing , huge beach with gorgeous white, clean sand. ( no smoking or dogs).Plenty of space but the majority sit between or near the flags- this is where you are supposed to swim as monitored. Many swim/ surf outside this area but there are rips which can drag you back so take care. Waves are the main fun part of the beach- great for teenagers & adults to have fun in but there are other beaches eg Rose bay nearby which are flat & good for kids & swimming in. Bondi Iceburg pool costs apx £9 for adults- salt water & not always calm but the small pool attached is nicer. You need ID to get into the restaurant there (adults only) & it serves nice food/ drinks.There is a popular walk along the coast ( lots of steps up/ down) to Coogee- worth doing.On the beachfront there are souvenir shops, chemists, supermarket and a Mcdonalds plus lots of smaller cafes and one very popular bar on the corner of Hall st. ( 18-40's range). Most importantly next to the beach there are excellent facilities to change , basic showers & toilets & a lovely restaurant. There are also large grass areas & trees to get shade. The bus stop is next to the beach-333 will take you direct to the city- or go to Bondi junction (10 mins) & change to the train -this is quicker but more hassle- although the transport system in Sydney/Bondi is cheap and very good whether you use bus/ train / tram or uber.You can just pay with your bank or credit card- no need to get an Opal card- same price -tap on/ off. I recommend buying sun protection there as the quality is far better than Europe lotion.

reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.text: Every trip to Sydney includes a stop in Bondi.  I have never been particularly fond of this beach.  While the beach and fine sand is nice, it usually is very crowded, not so much on this visit in July.  I noticed more garbage on the ground than ever before.  Bondi Beach is easy to get to by transit.  I prefer the beaches to the north, particularly Palm Beach.

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: We had the best time looking at tide pools and exploring the area. Some kids pointed out an octopus in the tide pool and that was super cool to see. We saw lots of different sea creatures including starfish and large crabs. It was a beautiful Saturday and quite busy, but we had a lot of fun at this famous beach.

reviews.title: Very nice beach
reviews.text: It is a very beautiful beach located in Sydney with beautiful fine sand.It was one of the things to see on our group trip. The sea was rough. We got our feet wet and the water was pretty cold.

reviews.title: Best Beach 🏖️ in Southern Hemisphere
reviews.text: Best Beach 🏝️ in the Southern Hemisphere. Another thing there are big waves 🌊. Also the ocean 🌊 is very clean 🧼 too . Lastly, there are lifeguards at this beach 🏝️ too which is nice  👍.

reviews.title: A lot to do by the beach
reviews.text: Great thing about Bondi is that you have plenty of accommodation, shops and restaurants all by the beach. The beach itself is over crowded and the sand is dirty.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach to relax and enjoy views
reviews.text: We spent about an hour on Bondi Beach just walking around and enjoying the views. Took the Sydney Hop On/Hop Off Bus and it was one of our stops on the blue line. Definitely worth the quick stop. Next time I'd bring swimsuit/towel and enjoy 1/2 day there including lunch and shopping.

reviews.title: Beach looked nice, but it was a cold and very windy day, so not much action that day
reviews.text: As part of a tour of Sydney, we stopped at Bondi Beach for 30 minute stop.  Unfortunately, the day was a little chilly and very windy, so it was not very enjoyable as the wind was blowing sand in your face and eyes.  Our tour guide assured us this was a very enjoyable beach on most other days with the weather is cooperative.

reviews.title: Beautiful views of Bondi Beach from the Coastal Walk
reviews.text: We took a walk at Bondi Beach along the Coastal Walk on a Sunday morning.  The weather was sunny and unseasonably warm for July.  There were tons of people around the area just enjoying the beautiful views of the beach.  The Coastal Walk was well paved and is very dog friendly but I would say that it is not an easy low key stroll since there were some sections where there are some stairs to climb.  There was a section along the side of the path that was set up like a small dog park with a water fountain for dogs.  After our walk, we took a stroll around the nearby shops and restaurants.  It was such a pleasant day and I would go back to Bondi Beach if we ever visit Sydney again.

reviews.title: Bondi beach with kids
reviews.text: We went with family and my kids w such a good time. It was easily accessible via train and bus. Definitely must go with loads of sunscreen lotion

reviews.title: Not to be missed!
reviews.text: I went to this beach one day taking a taxi from Sydney. The beach is beautiful, clean, the sea is a little rough but the water is still very clear. On the seafront there are many shops and restaurants. Not to be missed!

reviews.title: You have to have been there
reviews.text: The ultimate experience in Sydney! The backdrop of the beach with the surfers 🏄‍♂️ is amazing.. the bars are a fantastic experience, as there is something for every taste! Big waves, great atmosphere 🥰

reviews.title: Lovely beach with entry level surfing
reviews.text: lovely beach though smaller than some pictures portray!  Not too many places for such other than the Promede which is excellent and highly recommend.  Though I'd been to Sydney 4-5 times previously had never gone since logistics to get there seemed complicated.  They're not.  Jump on a 333 bus and you're there in 30 minutes.  Won't be disappointed!

reviews.title: Great!
reviews.text: The photo here is of Tamarama Beach not Bondi Beach. Bondi Beach is a kilometer long. I lived here a long time ago and it has not changed, it is brilliant! If you're in Sydney, you must make the effort to walk on the beach.

reviews.title: Check out the icebergs if you want safe swimming
reviews.text: We took a look at the beach and decided to go to the icebergs instead and then do the coastal walk. Well worth walking along to get  to the free pools though rather than paying for the icebergs. The beach was too busy for us but the waves and surf looked good but it wasn’t as spectacular as we were made to believe.

reviews.title: Not sure what all the fuss is about
reviews.text: Well it’s a beach. Quite busy. A few people trying to surf. Not much in the way of good eating or drinking places. I thought Manly beach was much nicer

reviews.title: Take something to settle in or buy on site.
reviews.text: Nice beach, quite clean with nice waves.A spot popular with surfers.Luckily it wasn't too busy during our visit.What is missing is beach beds to rent and umbrellas. Which may be a disadvantage or an advantage for others.It is possible to buy all the equipment (parasols, tents, games for children) in the shops opposite.

reviews.title: Bondi Beach is a beach
reviews.text: It was cool to go. A lot of surfers. Iconic. But just a beach. OK restaurants along the beach promenade. Good that they have showers along the beach though!

reviews.title: Bondi fever - Bondi draws the crowds
reviews.text: Took the train and bus to Bondi - head for the beach at Bondi, when we visit Sydney. Beach, glistening ocean still draws the crowds, the life-saver statue is a reminder, though, of caution.  The Bondi Pavilion has been updated and has undergone an amazing transformation. Not been to Sydney in a long time, we'll come again soon. (I have gait/walking challenges (stroke), wear a legbrace.)

reviews.title: Family trip 4 days in Bondi
reviews.text: The waverley walk is amazing and very well worth while.I would stay at Bondi Hotel if you can.  The cocktails are $14 about £7 and it is open mon-sat till 12 and till late.   Closed early on a Sunday.Other bars are open but can be expensive as shots can be $30 each.The staff at bondi hotel are amazing and just across the road from the beach.The Pavillion restaurant breakfast from 930-11am is amazing.  The bacon and eggs on toast are fab, as is the yogurt granola (incs liquorice and surprising great).   Breakfast including, coffee 2 drinks, 1 granola bowl and 2 bacon eggs toast about £35.  This is a contract to 2018 when would have been double even though the exchange rate is about the same 1.8 to pound in 2018 and 1.9 in Nov 23.We went to Coggee Bay in 2018 and that was fab too but prefer Bondi Beach as a little more going on and access to other places is great.Tip   - get the 303 bus into Sydney for $20 from the shop.  We had 4 trips into Sydney off peak and a trip on the ferry from Sydney to Darling Harbour and back.  A bargain for £10.  A must.the supermarkets are so much cheaper than 2018, a great surprise.  However, if you smoke they are $65 for 25...yes £33.   My one son smoked so a bit of a shock, but I agree keep them expensive to discourage smoking.Their local chemists are really cheap so no need to pack suncream (a bucket of factor 50 is £7.....to encourage you to use it, great idea), shampoo etc.Really loved Bondi Beach, so clean and beautiful.

reviews.title: Maybe a little bit disappointed
reviews.text: Maybe a little disappointment.Much smaller than what you imagine from tv and movies.The trip from the Sydney center by bus took much longer than expected.Heavy traffic.

reviews.title: Stunning Views
reviews.text: Beautiful area with a great beach and trendy shops and restaurants.  We really enjoyed taking the coastal walk and taking in the stunning views and rock formations.

reviews.title: Surfers paradise
reviews.text: Famous beach, 20 minutes by bus out of Sydney Harbour. Incredible fine white sand, a few restaurants to eat or drink. One of the most famous beaches in the world...so you must visit.

reviews.title: Alright
reviews.text: This was an alright beach lots of space and sandy I say it was ok simply because I do t think it’s worth the hype there are better beaches in Australia probably even Sydney

reviews.title: Beach is synonymous with Australian culture
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is synonymous with the Australian beach culture, to relax and enjoy life and soak up the rays. These days, you can catch some waves and avoid the effluent that once plagued the beach. Bondi Beach is now pristine, and it's only a few miles from the center of Sydney. By the way, be careful with your trash and avoid stubbing cigarette butts into the beach sand.

reviews.title: Sunny day!
reviews.text: Perfect weather on Spring time. People are sun-bathing and do water activities. As a tourist and did not research the temperature, we were walking with long pants. Enjoyed walking around.  The restaurants are packed with people.

reviews.title: Kiding you
reviews.text: We went to the restaurant and ate three hamburgers. They were very poorly prepared and meat of no quality, and the minimum price was €22 per burger. A real joke

reviews.title: Beach day
reviews.text: Always been a fan of Bondi Rescue and finally got to see the beach for myself. Lovely beach with the best lifeguards, extremely helpful and always down for a chat!

reviews.title: Iconic beach
reviews.text: Lovely beach and area, great for beach and surf lovers, a must see, or visit regardless of season. Iconic place to visit when in NSW and Sydney.

reviews.title: Must do walk!
reviews.text: We did a great walk from Bondi beach to Bronte beach. We had a stroller which did require regular carrying up and down stairs, but it was worth the effort!

reviews.title: Clean beach
reviews.text: Another visit with new family members. Although parking is a nightmare, the beach is tidy and clean with plenty of space for visitors. There are plenty of restaurants and cafes nearby, and a great place to visit on a warm day.

reviews.title: A Must visit
reviews.text: Can’t believe I’m actually in Bondi beach after been watching it on tv for so many years. Beautiful, well kept, and lovely walk on sand . Lovely eating places nearby and parking is very easy close by . Definitely worth a visit

reviews.title: Nice beach and surrounding area
reviews.text: Nice beach and surrounding area (with some nice walks around the edges), loads of places to grab food and super clean! Overall impressed

reviews.title: One of the most important and busiest in Sydney
reviews.text: It is one of the most important beaches, located 9 km from the center. We arrive by public transport in about 35'.It is extensive with clear sand and waves suitable for surfers who usually come daily in the early hours. Next to it is the Bondi Beach Park (large green space with barbecues) and a wide esplanade that runs along it, ideal for walks or sitting and contemplating on some of its benches. There is also Bondi Pavillion, a pavilion that houses restaurants, a cafeteria, bathrooms, changing rooms and lockers (fees apply).When we went it was a splendid sunny day and the beach was quite busy, even several people in the sea.The avenue that borders it, Campbell Parade, offers a number of cafes and restaurants, as well as some accommodation options.A few meters from the beach is the Icebergs Club and the trail begins that continues to Coogee Beach.

reviews.title: Lots to see and do
reviews.text: Really amazing beach and recommend for everyone visiting Sydney to visit Bondi. Lots to see and do. Great restaurants and bars. Beach is very clean and amazing surf.

reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: Not as good as I thought it would be. I went for the famous name. It was ok. I went to Manly the next day which is so much better

reviews.title: Well worth going to say been there done that.
reviews.text: Visited on Thursday 25th May. I spent a couple hours wondering around checking out Bondi Beach, the cliff walks, the pavilion and the main street. Well worth going to say been there done that.

reviews.title: Ticks all the boxes....
reviews.text: With its white sand, accessibility, excellent amenities and cafes for visitors this stunning beach ticks all the boxes, for visitors and locals alike.

reviews.title: Bondi Bliss
