reviews.text: I've been a huge fan of the TV sho 'Bondi Rescue' for years & always wanted to visit the famous Bondi Beach.  I couldn't believe how magical it is in real life.  It was even more enjoyable as we visited on a weekday & there were very few people on the beach.  I was able to get photos of some of the most famous scenes from the show, but I wasn't able to get a photo with one of the lifeguards.  I will definately be coming back, hopefully when its a little warmer so I can swim in the ocean & possibly dine at Icebergs restaurant.

reviews.title: Got the t shirt
reviews.text: It was days before showers I was there. I got the feeling that everyone who comes here comes for "been there, done that" experience only. Crowded and overrated.

reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit
reviews.text: What a happening place on the weekend. We didn't sit at the beach, but walked from one end to the other. Just lovely. Great town adjacent to the beach for lunch. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.title: A bit too commercialise.
reviews.text: We didn't enjoy Bondi as much as Manly beach. Not sure we liked the commercial side of things as much as a natural beach.

reviews.title: A beautiful beach well worth the visit
reviews.text: This beach is stunning! With soft powder white sand which is clean tidy well looked after with life guards and safe areas to swim / surf. The water was clear and cool on a hot day. There are fresh water showers and a changing area and toilet facilities in the pavilion. Al' top tipsCatch the 333 bus from Circular Quay in Sydney all the way to the beach.

reviews.title: a must-see for any visitor
reviews.text: With easy public transport access, playgrounds, historic landmarks, and rock pools, there is something for everyone. Whether you're looking for a place to relax, or get your adrenaline pumping, Bondi Beach has it all. From the iconic Bondi Icebergs to the stunning coastal walk, you won't be disappointed.

reviews.title: It was nice, BUT not sure what the big deal is...maybe if you're a surfer?
reviews.text: Nice beach. It was not crowded the day we went. It was part of a tour we did of Sydney. We had lunch at a restaurant located on the beach and later relaxed here for a short while. The sand was soft, and the water temperature was okay. I'm not a surfer, so I can't address that aspect. Overall, it was a nice beach, but nothing exceptional.  What DID work? I don't generally like beer, but the restaurant waiter suggested one popular in Australia (Bundaberg ginger beer) and I loved it! I have found it here at home!

reviews.title: Nice but not very nice
reviews.text: Nice beach especially good for surfers, for swimmers like us it is somewhat risky. I have seen much better beaches around the world and I suppose the marketing for Bondi Beach and the TV series makes it as famous as it is.

reviews.title: Mandatory
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is an iconic place close to Sydney. It's well known abroad and deserves this qualification. The beach is simply stunning. Brave, big and very beautiful. We obviously took a bath there and the experience was amazing. Then you've got a walking promenade, plenty of shops, restaurants, etc... and the town itself is very nice.  Definitely, a mandatory place to go

reviews.title: So many better beaches
reviews.text: If you want to be seen or people watch this is a great place. It’s busy. The water is rough most days. The sand is lovely though. Beautiful to view from the walking trails north and south. But if you want beautiful beaches with locals go north to one of the 4 other beaches. My pick would be Coogee or Bronte.

reviews.title: Infamous Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Not much to say. World renowned surfing location. Sun, sand, people, ocean....Great area of Sydney and there's even a Canadian pub up the road.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: This is a nice beach area. It gets very crowded but it's a nice visit not too far from Sydney proper. If you want a relaxing beach day, there are better places, but this is not a bad stop for a quick stroll along the beach.

reviews.title: Cold
reviews.text: It was a cold water. We couldn't swim. The fact that not many people use buses to get here made us unhappy.

reviews.title: Over Rated
reviews.text: The beach is ok I went because I felt I should. Mannly Beach is much nicer. Although it was not sunny when I went so that doesn’t help.

reviews.title: Beautiful Water Views, but Crowded
reviews.text: Beautiful water and nice views of nearby housing developments; however, it is very crowded and the water very cold.

reviews.title: Good day out
reviews.text: Enjoyable day out on Boxing Day. Leisurely ride on the bus from Elizabeth Street, Central Sydney. The beach is clean and safe. A lot of places to eat and drink. Friendly service everywhere. Cheerful, caring lifeguards. We had a pleasant conversation with a couple of lifeguards. One used to live in London Putney. Thank you for making our day memorable.

reviews.title: Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is famous for its pristine beach and surfing and since the 1980s topless bathing! It is 4 miles east of Sydney. Bondi is an Aboriginal word meaning surfing

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: I guess this is really a must do when visiting Sydney and you can take a nice walk along the horseshoe shaped beach ,The day we were there it was very choppy so apart from paddling we just watched all the surfers which was good fun , a few shops and cafes along the main road , we did the bondi to coogee walk (separate review) which was very nice , Definitely worth a visit from the city

reviews.title: Bondi a must but average
reviews.text: You have to visit because it is Bondi but pretty average and quite tacky in parts. Take the Big Bus tour and stay on itEnjoy

reviews.title: Enjoyed the walk, the views and of course the swim at Bondi
reviews.text: Made a day of it and got off the bus at the Waverley Cemetery at Bronte, and strolled through this interesting place with magnificent views of the ocean until we reached the walking trail along the foreshore. We then took in all the fantastic views while walking past Bronte beach and Tamarama beach before reaching the famous Bondi beach. We had a very relaxing swim (between the flags of course), until it was time to leave.

reviews.title: Iconic location that has to be done.
reviews.text: Iconic beach in Sydney, the locals will say it's not there best but if like us it is one you just have to do. Good parking right at the beach and the costal walk that runs along the back of it is great to stroll along.Nice wide white sand, life gaurds are on duty but if not a string swimmer take care with the currents.The street looking into Bondi has a number of shops and cafe's.All in we enjoyed our time at this famous location.

reviews.title: Best beach in the area
reviews.text: Bindi is probably the best beach in the area.  We did the Coogee to Bondi Beach walk.  Bondi is a big beach with sun bathers and surfers.  The Main Street runs parallel to it.  The city bus stops are right there making it easily to get to and fro.  The cliffs around the beach give it a great coastal feel.

reviews.title: amazing place
reviews.text: i would say it's a must see place, once you get here you wont be disapointedas it is spring the waves were not that big, but loads of waves to test your skillsamazing place

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: We took a bus to Bondi beach from Sydney, only cost us $3.  It is an iconic beach both for its sands and sharks.  The sand is fabulous, if a little hard to walk on.  Parking is good with plenty around.  The surf was fabulous

reviews.title: Awesome beach
reviews.text: We staryed 5 days near the beach and enjoyed walking the beach. Great surfing spot, beach is busy, especially on the weekends. Lots to do here, even if you get some rays.

reviews.title: Bondi- a small nice beach
reviews.text: A nice beach with scenic views and walkways.    With bondi iceberg swimming pool on one end and kids pool on the other end of beach... a very nice place for a quie evening or a family day time at beach..  it has surf boards rental available as well..

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: It's a very nice beach, no stones. Very good for surfing. There are also rock pools nearby and other walking trails that gives good views along the coastline.

reviews.title: Must visit when in Sydney
reviews.text: Beautiful beach to visit when in Sydney. Great selection of shops along the promenade. Don't miss the markets if visiting on the weekend. You can easily spend few hours here just walking along the beach. Children's pool also available at one end. Many rock pools to get down to as well. Lots of grassy areas too to have a picnic and enjoy the views.

reviews.title: Charming even in the shoulder season
reviews.text: A bit off-season, however, some people were braving the water for swimming and surfing.  We found it easy to reach via public bus; it is convenient to downtown Sydney.  Its own neighborhood is less urban than Sydney's core and was a relaxing place to visit.  We walked on the beach and on the trails along the water nearby.  It may be livelier at other times of the year.  Maybe not a must-do for September, however, I was glad we went there.

reviews.title: Iconic beach. There are far better in Oz but it’s still worth a visit
reviews.text: Virtually everyone who comes to Australia has heard of Bondi Beach. It’s fame enhanced by the fly on the wall docu Bondi Rescue. There are far better beaches in Australia but there’s no denying that Bondi is in a great setting with more surfer dudes and chicks per square metre than anywhere else! If you’re not in the water there’s a great walk around the back of the beach, about 1km length in total and all on the flat. Further back are an array of shops, cafes and restaurants. It’s a great spot to come to and spend a few hours if not all day.

reviews.title: Nice but
reviews.text: Nice beach but I couldn't see anything special. Plenty to do for kids with the skate park Like most beaches nice to walk along.Heaps of dogs everywhereHappy to see it but will not rush back.

reviews.title: Beautiful again today!
reviews.text: It was certainly great to be back here and we got the first nice day in ages. It's still winter so this was a walking tour rather than a swimathon. But it was great to be reunited with my son and his new Australian family ahain and enjoying the primo location of Bondi Beach once more! Separated by the Pandemic but finally reunited.

reviews.title: Australia's most famous city beach
reviews.text: Backpackers from around the world gather at Bondi Beach to celebrate Christmas Day every year. This pristine strip of white sand, 1 km long, is 7km from the Sydney CBD, It's around half an hour travelling time. Bondi Beach is Australia's most famous urban beach. "Bondi" is Aboriginal for "water breaking over rocks."

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Visited in june-july so it was winters in Australia. The beach wasn't as crowded (that was a saving for people who want peace and solitude 😋

reviews.title: A must go
reviews.text: Unfortunately I went there when the weather was at its worst! Torrential rain! However, that didn’t stop me from seeing the amazing view and despite the nsw gov warning to avoid water sports, there were still lots of surfers. Definitely will visit there again when the weather is better but A MUST VISIT. Take the train to Bondi Junction and catch bus 333 or 380 (u will see the beach and you can stop at any bus stop along the beach). First time in Sydney and the people and place is just beautiful.

reviews.title: Blue water and clean beach
reviews.text: The beach is well connected from the city using Bus and Rail.The views on the way are amazing. The walkway has beautiful laid back feel with all kinds of restaurants and activity wear shops dominating the streets.The beach was very clean, people were minding their own business. As it was the cold season so not many people were in water and we observed that helicopters hovering to monitor the people in waters inciting them to return to the sand.The water was clear blue but the waves were high. Probably that is the reason this place is famous for surfing. It would be necessary to look over young children here.

reviews.title: Worlds most overrated beach
reviews.text: Probably the most over rated beach on the planet. Crowded full of arrogant people and feels like everyone is in a bad mood.

reviews.title: Visit to Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Well what can I say about Bondi Beach you seen reports & reviews this place does not let you down. The Beach was clean the sea was nice its all you could wish for. Its a dream to come here from the UK.

reviews.title: Best meal in Bondi
reviews.text: Omg delicious best meal in Bondi to date We had the sharing lamb with lots of sides of veg. Delicious the meat was so tender, meat melted in our mouth - obviously a great cut of meat and cooked to perfection. Washed down with a Pinot noir. Great service and then to add to our experience live music. Great night

reviews.title: Famous beach
reviews.text: Beautiful long wide popular clean beach with an ocean pool. It is patrolled so a good place for a dip.Easy to get to from the city by bus or train. Thanks for the vote if you found this review helpful

reviews.title: Undeniably the best beach in Sydney
reviews.text: Beautiful location, beautiful people around, you dont need to check weather to come to this beach, whether you are getting into the water or not, this is the best place to be when you feel like hanging out. Bustling cafe scene and great night lifee to around this area.

reviews.title: Beautiful place for a walk eventho its cloudy and windy
reviews.text: Extremely cloudy and windy but that doesn’t stop people from having walks here at Bondi Beach like my partner and I. We love the sound and the calmness of the waves, what a beautiful place to catch up with you love ones.

reviews.title: The Beach of Sydney
reviews.text: Bondi Beach: a name, a warranty. If you think about a beach in Sydney, surely Bondi will be the first name which will pop up to your mind. It’s very big and you can take breathtaking photos, the water is quite cold but at least you can take a bath.

reviews.title: Sydney’s iconic beach
reviews.text: Along with Surfers Paradise, Australia’s most famous and iconic beach. Best way to get here is via a bus or train to Bondi Junction, then take any of the buses to the beach. Although it’s picturesque and has excellent views, it gets very crowded so you may want to visit one of the other beaches in the area if you want some privacy.Lots of cafes and shops around if you don’t wish to visit the beach.

reviews.title: Australia's most famous beach
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is 100% Aussie, even though every backpacker  in the country seems to turn up for Christmas. The water is clear and normally the surf isn't threatening, and the sand is golden.  Life Savers patrol the beach, but please, if you can't swim, restrict yourself  to paddling.

reviews.title: Beach Visit - public lockers available?
reviews.text: Hey Everyone I attempted to go to Bondi beach & hire a surfboard & a public locker After asking lots of people ( life guards, ticket inspectors, ice cream vendors etc ) and no one knew ! Their pavilion is under construction where they used to be & Bondi looks like it needs some much needed attention! Considering the wealth around you’d assume it’s happening soon After an hour of walking around  I found lockers for hire @ icebergs ocean pool I could not just pay for the locker only but had to pay for admission as well, so $12 aud in total Note to council * maybe some signs to let travellers know where they are ( lockers ) or an information booth with a phone support central to the beach The Bondi people are soo friendly and the beach is amazing itself & we had a great time once settled

reviews.title: Sublime again last year!
reviews.text: We had such a varied travel diet last year before everything closed, including time spent in Australia and then the United Kingdom on the other side of the world. Bondi had been fabulous with limpid blue waters lapping at the edge of the golden sands. It was amazing to come on an uncharacteristically swell free day last summer. The waters ere quite calm and still for its being Bondi.

reviews.title: One best beaches in Australia
reviews.text: Bondi beach with its vast stretch of beach and families, nippers, and surfers are amazingly beautiful. There’s real difference between north and south shore of beach. At present one side sits iconic restaurants and cafes, others have North Bondi surf club. An easy way to spend time together, bring your chair, beach towel, and please watch out surfers and stingrays, or else Bondi patrol will come to rescue. A breathtaking and beautiful place, Bondi Beach.

reviews.title: Great place to spend New Year’s Day
reviews.text: I highly recommend visiting Bondi Beach when exploring Sydney, it’s a great place to spend the day if you’re looking to relax and have a beach day and for us there’s no better place to start the year than on the world famous Bondi Beach!The beach is very well protected by lifeguards, even though the sea was a little rough I felt safe at all times, I don’t think I’ve ever visited a beach so thoroughly patrolled as Bondi is.

reviews.title: One of the best beaches.
reviews.text: Bondi is a great beach, with gorgeous white sand. It’s got a public pool at one end and Icebergs at the other which there’s a fee to enter. There’s lots of cafes along the main road and Esplanade. There’s the Bondi to Coogee Walk. It’s easy to get the 380 bus from Watson’s Bay.

reviews.title: An iconic Australian landmark!
reviews.text: Sydney has an abundance of iconic landmarks  which most visitors to the city put on their sightseeing schedule.  And Bondi Beach is certainly one of them.  It’s probably true to say that  the 1km stretch of  that picturesque and sweeping white-sand crescent of Bondi is one of Australia’s most iconic beaches. Bondi Beach is definitely worth a visit, for some surfing, or swimming, or sunbathing, or walking along the sand, the beach promenade, and the lovely  coastal cliff walk that heads south from the beach to Coogee Beach.Whatever you do at Bondi Beach,  do it sensibly.  If you intending to swim or surf, use sunscreen as the harsh Australian sun can be cruel on your skin.  There are lifeguards on duty, and clear rules for swimming and surfing are in place for your safety.   Take care of your belongings; most beach-goers keep their belongings close to them, though I believe there are lockers in one of the pavilions.  There’s ample changing and showering facilities.Even if you don’t want to swim, surf or sunbathe, at least go to Bondi Beach to get a feel for  the beach and surfing culture which  is a part of the Australian lifestyle. The beach itself is attractive, but it becomes extremely crowded in the warmer months.  There’s also lots of other stuff you can do when you get to this beach.  Walk along the fine sand, or the beach promenade,  or rest awhile, and simply take it all in.  There’s some fine street murals to check out on some of the concrete walls by the beach. There’s cafes and shops right in front of the beach, but they do  get crowded.  Step behind the beach onto Campbell Parade for a plethora of shops (many with a recurring ‘beach theme’), cafes, restaurants and bars.  It’s a great stretch for browsing, and for sitting outside watching the passing parade.  One of my favourite activities is the Bondi to Coogee cliff top walk.  It takes a couple of hours at a leisurely pace; you may even find the smaller Coogee Beach less crowded for beach activities. Even if you are just going to say you’ve been to Bondi Beach and to get the obligatory selfie, do go to Bondi Beach.  The beach is around 7km east of the centre of Sydney; I usually take the 380 bus from Circular Quay; it takes about 45 minutes.

reviews.title: An experience
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is one of the most iconic places in Australia. It is famous for its waves and its sand. It's a beautiful place. Great for a swim and great for just a walk. We have been there many times. We love to just stroll around. There many cafes and eateries as well as other types of shops. It gets quite busy during warmer months.

reviews.title: It should be called SHARK BEACH!
reviews.text: My wife and me went there and went swimming. I have to say that although the water is nice, the beach is terribly sandy. It was really white. Be warned, if you go onto the beach wearing socks and sandals like we did, be prepared to get sand all over your socks. Also, make sure you take sunscreen or you will end up really burned all over. I wish someone had told me that as well. We couldn't move for the next 4 days and stayed in our hotel on the bed. At least the room service had plenty of good food in our hotel which was great. The other thing that I wish I had known about were the SHARKS! I never knew that Australia had sharks in the water. It's crazy! Worst of all is that they JUMP OUT OF THE WATER!!The whole place is full of sharks. One guy told us that because we are from the USA they like to eat Americans more than Australians. I saw one jump out of the water that was huge but he said that was just a baby. I got a photo of it to proof it. The people down there are crazy, no way would I ever swim in their sea water if I had known it was infested with sharks.

reviews.title: Always a good day out at Bondi.
reviews.text: Certainly the best known of the Sydney beaches - it is always a pleasant day out ta Bondi. Although I would try to avoid public holidays when it can get very busy. Nowadays (with COVID) I would suggest Bronte as the more enjoyable alternative. .

reviews.title: Spinal Injury
reviews.text: I had a spinal cord injury and Jethro and Hoppo were so nice in helping me and getting me stabilized and I truly appreciate that.

reviews.title: Out of season
reviews.text: August is not a good time for the beaches in Sydney. It was cold and windy, with some rain, deserted but one can imagine what it looks like when it's in full use. Definitely a must when you visit Sydney. A good way to see it is to take the blue line on the Big Bus hop on - hop off tour and get off at the beach, takea stroll to the next stop and catch the next bus.

reviews.title: Best beach in Sydney
reviews.text: Perfect place to sunbathing, try to surf, skate, practice yoga and do shopping.. I love watching waves and surfers ! I recommend to walk on coastal walk from bondi beach to coffee beach.

reviews.title: An Icon
reviews.text: Its Bondi, you've got to go.But dont expect the cafes to be value for money... they are expensive! but some of the food is pretty good, even if the staff are unfriendly, snooty gorgeous people !!!!!!

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: A great place to visit, swim, or workout first thing in the morning or early evening. It can get packed at other hours. Seasonal of course.

reviews.title: Great Beach
reviews.text: This beach is a great way to spend a day wether it’s just doing a good walk or laying on the beach. I highly recommend the Bondi RSL for lunch or dinner as it has the best views of Bondi & has really good prices, just remember to wear a collared shirt (Males) Enjoy....😎

reviews.title: Just as good as it looks on telly
reviews.text: Another iconic location, the beach was clean and full of people. Lots of pubs and restaurants around. Sat and watched the life savers for a while and soaked up the sun.

reviews.title: A Must Visit
reviews.text: A very popular place with the locals since Australians loved the sun, sand and sea. Other than the beach, there are lots of restaurants and shops in the area. A great place to rest and relax.

reviews.title: Bondi beach
reviews.text: Visited here recently on a visit from ireland. I've always watched Bondi rescue and was dying to get to bondi beach. When I got there I was kinda shocked at how small it is in real life. Lol the t.v show kinda makes it seem alot bigger. Anyways it was a nice beach. The waves and currents are very strong. It's a nice beach to sun bathe but a bit too strong for me to swim in lol. I was in for about 10 minutes and I had enough of being bashed by the waves. You do need to be a strong swimmer to take on Bondi. It's a nice beach just to chill and people watch.

reviews.title: Great to have seen it over summer!
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is always an iconic place to visit and it was great to have caught it just before the huge shutdown. It was packed at that point with wall to wall acreages of displayed flesh.

reviews.title: Spend The Day
reviews.text: A great beach to explore and enjoy the sea life. There are bars, restaurants, and local shops. It was winter so it was slow and we didn't swim. I can only imagine how crazy it would be in the summer. Good times.

reviews.title: A must see when in Sydney, but not the most scenic place in the area
reviews.text: Had to go here whilst in Sydney. It's a good resort, but not the smartest (recommend Manly as a classier beah resort). Beach is large, but not the expnse to me that it's reputation made it out to be. Popular, as you'd expect.

reviews.title: Get Your People Watch On
reviews.text: If you find yourself in the Sydney area and have half a day to spare head down to Bondi Beach.  Simply board a MTR to Bondi Junction followed by a bus, which are easily found once you arrive at Bondi Junction.  Join the surfer dudes and dudettes, hang out with the hippies, or drink espressos and eat vegan food with the trendies.  Worth 2 or 3hrs of your time...even if it's just to take a stroll along the beach.   For the full experience head along to The Icebergs.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We stopped here for a quick visit with our tour group.  The beach is very nice and was empty when we visited, which was during the week.  Another couple on our tour stopped at the beach a couple weeks prior when the weather was extremely hot and they mentioned that there were so many people that you could not even see the sand.  Our tour guide also provided information regarding the Bondi Beach Lifesaving Program, which we found very interesting.

reviews.title: Not that impressive
reviews.text: We were unimpressed with Bondi, we were not there for all that long, but it was nothing outstanding, just a beach and the day we were there the waves were nothing to shout about - did expect something more spectacular - have been to many better beaches - we were not in the water - just had a walk along the prom - the murals were quite interesting.

reviews.title: Nice romp by the sea
reviews.text: There’s a life guard school with eye candy to see as well as many beach goers. It’s a nice beach, but nearly nice as manly beach.

reviews.title: Bondi!!
reviews.text: Finally made it to the famous Bondi Beach. I’m not one for the sand and beaches, however this was a must. I loved taking the cliff walks around Bondi, and don’t feel like you have to walk the entire thing. We just did a short 15 minute walk around and saw some great cliffs and rock formations along with good views of Bondi.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: We were disappointed with Bondi beach as it was extremely crowded on the day that we went. Most people seem to go for a quick dip and to pose for selfies etc. Nothing wrong with that but we expected a cooler beach than the one populated by people taking pictures.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Wanted to visit the famous bondi beach when in Sydney hopped on a bus which took us right into the centre it is a marvellous beach but to be honest less than I expected it was very busy with plenty to see in the surrounding area so having seen it I can write it off my bucket list !!

reviews.title: Iconic & Worth a Visit.
reviews.text: Always wanted to visit Bondi Beach, high on the "bucket list" so really happy to have done it.I realise there are better beaches locally, Manly, etc. but this is Bondi.Loads of people around, all nationalities, so great for people watching.Great bars & restaurants, cafes, etc. everywhere, lots of shops selling the usual surf & beachwear, so bring your credit card.A great few hours visiting, was a bit rushed, but well worth it & recommend a visit if in Sydney.Chose the nearest cafe for a snack & drinks, service, food, drinks all amazing, loved it.A great few hours at Bondi, the beach was as advertised, just fabulous.

reviews.title: Famous beach with lots to do
reviews.text: Expansive beach with lots of shops and restaurants about. Visited 20 years ago, the place has cleaned up quite a bit ...

reviews.title: Infamous for a reason
reviews.text: We have visited this beach in both the winter and summer. When we visited in the winter we were the only ones there, and for good reason as it was very cold, but it was still nice to sit down and chill out. In the summer it was relatively packed but there was still ample space to lye down. The transport links to the beach are okay, although you have to get a train and then switch to a bus at Bondi Junction which is a pain, and despite the buses being frequent, they are very full in the summer months. As this is a world renowned beach, there is no shortage of shops and eateries lining the back of the beach so there is no need to worry about food etc. and the beach itself is well maintained and extremely safe with an amazing lifeguard service. Keeping to shallow water it is safe, however rip currents are common and the waves, further out, are massive. The iceberg pool is also situated on the southern end of the beach and is a nice place to visit if it is not too busy! If you're visiting Sydney then I definitely reccomend a day trip to Bondi if you are there between the spring and autumn months.

reviews.title: Beautiful and iconic beach, crescent shaped, sandy, nice surf and ambiance
reviews.text: Probably the best beach in Sydney, favorite of surfers and the young crowd, with lots of sand, sun and fun things to do, with lots of restaurants nearby.

reviews.title: Great beach, beautiful
reviews.text: Had a driver show us Sydney and ended up here. Had lunch at Iceburgs, amazing views, great views and reasonably priced. The beach was loaded with young folks, must be a college somewhere near. Good shopping across from beach

reviews.title: Its Good
reviews.text: We loved Bondi beach and the vibe but thought it to be overrated. Probably the sea waves are perfect for beginners to learn surfing and that's how it garnered so much attention. The town maybe tiny but has some amazing cafes, restaurants and has the most happening (lively) crowd The walk from Coogee to Bondi is a must though.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Always wanted to come here and it really didn’t disappoint.. Beautiful golden sand, clear water and manned by lifeguards who are professional and always seen so you feel safe.. Close to cafés and shops so always easy to get a drink.. I love it here!

reviews.title: Very nice Beach for Surfers
reviews.text: Do you arrive Bondi Beach by car, Tram or Bus via Sydney/Bondi JT in 20 minutes. The Beach is very nice and has very good conditions dir Surfers. Also you can there Go to swim, but there are very heavy sea. On the beach you can find a very good restaurant. Not far from the beach do you have a lot of Shops, Cafés, BarsThe beach invites to stay.

reviews.title: Bondi beach
reviews.text: Thank you to the Waverley Council for providing free Wi-Fi at bondi beach  and parks.  Great place to spend the day !!!

reviews.title: taken there by a super knowledgeable guide
reviews.text: the walk along the coast from Bondi to coogee would have to be one of the most spectacular scenery one can encounter in Sydney. No wonder Bondi is classified as the real icon of Sydney and a representation of all Australian beaches with their bronzed and healthy bodies

reviews.title: Surfing with Lets go surfing Bondi
reviews.text: The best thing about Bondi beach -learn surfing. The waves are little and not something a real surfer would write home about, but for beginners it was ideal. The instructors were patient and friendly too.

reviews.title: Detour
reviews.text: It is a detour but a must do. We enjoy seeing the surfers and the pool at the far south of the beach. we didn't go in, a bit chilly for us.

reviews.title: Gorgeous crescent beach
reviews.text: Simply a stunning location!  The beach is enormous with beautiful wave action for surfers and swimmers.  Stroll along the cliff walk and take in the fabulous views!

reviews.title: Sunrise
reviews.text: Staple beach for early morning visits. Plenty of leisure spaces for stroll and picnic. Excellent beach patrol always felt safe to swim

reviews.title: Iconic Sydney beach
reviews.text: We took the Big Bus out to Bondi and were not disappointed. It’s quite a large beach, with clean soft sand and the big breakers. Lots of surfers to watch.

reviews.title: Concrete and crowds
reviews.text: I can't see anything attractive about Bondi, except possibly closeness to the city. The place is so heavily overpopulated, with apartments everywhere you look. Concrete is everywhere. Where is the nature?

reviews.title: Ordinary nothing special for a top waterfront
reviews.text: Considering its one of the top destinations here in Sydney, this hotspot needs notable improvements by authorities(tiles, walkways, signs, public bath, lights..etc.), all are outdated and in relatively miserable conditions. I saw construction works are ongoing and hoping the new infrastructure will match the level that Sydney name deserves.

reviews.title: Breathtaking in more ways than one.
reviews.text: Four of us spent a wonderful afternoon and evening enjoying the beach,surf and evening dining around Bondi and all of us were in full agreement that Bondi lives up to its reputation and some!The beach itself is vast and it seemed to accommodate the many enjoying the weather quite easily,we managed to throw down towels to the rear of the beach wall so to offer at lest some shade and spent an exhilarating time in the water being dragged here there and everywhere.The currents are really strong and the rip tides too,so do be careful,although the Lifeguards were constantly warning people and are obviously very diligent.After a few hours on the beach we called into the North Bondi RSL for drinks to meet up with family and were highly impressed with the silent tribute observed at the designated time,something we did not know of so total respect to this tradition.From the RSL we strolled along the promenade to the South end of the beach for dinner and an enjoyable evening relaxing and catching up.So a wonderful day spent amongst an incredible and iconic beach,we loved it and can't believe how people now seem to recommend Manly over Bondi,no chance,Bondi everytime for us.

reviews.title: Understandable reputation
reviews.text: A wide expanse of fine white sand, which gently slopes into the sea, which reliably delivers a decent surf. All this and only 4 miles from the centre of Sydney. I went there expecting to be underwhelmed but I wasn't. One sad note. Someone was washed out to sea and drowned on the day we went so I would keep away from the rocky extremes of the beach.

reviews.title: Bondi Beach Walk and beach
reviews.text: The beach was a can't miss site when in Sydney. The beach, surfers, water and views were outstanding. The beach walk / coastline trails had amazing views of cliffs and ocean views. The path is not the place for those with balance issues or mobility impairment. The stone steps very in size, angle, height and make this rather dangerous for those with any walking issues. There were not always great handrails either. The walk was worth it if you are  mobile and in decent shape. Be careful if you guy. Folks have died on this walk. The views are worth it.

reviews.title: It's a beach.
reviews.text: If you're into surfing and a surfer, then I can see the appeal. We went to say that we had been. A stretch of retail outlets mixed within eateries and bars.

reviews.title: Guess I just didn't see the excitement about this beach
reviews.text: This was part of a local tour.  It just was not as exciting as they make it to believe, but then we are not surfing people.  It looks like it was more exciting in years past.

reviews.title: Beautiful Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Was at Bondi Beach late afternoon and it was great not crowded enough room where your not sitting on top of each other, highly recommend visiting the beach later in the day in summer. The was was really warm and clean. With a dinner on the grass area viewing Bondi turning into evening was breath taking.

reviews.title: Nice little beach
reviews.text: Crowded but a nice beach to swim ,surf, and walk in the water.  Worth the trip to see while visiting sydney.

reviews.title: Smaller than the reputation
reviews.text: Biggest reputation for a beach in Australia.  It may have a great surf reputation and swimming is fine but it is a relatively small beach

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Pretty cool beach! There’s a cool graffiti wall and the beach is clean. I went when it was still chilly (I went last May) so we didn’t go in the water, although that didn’t stop the locals. I would definitely recommend going and walking around even if it’s too cold to swim. It’s a short drive away from downtown Sydney.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Iconic! Clean and fresh which was very pleasant refreshing. Great walk on the sand and lovely climb on the rocks

reviews.title: Sun Sea Sand
reviews.text: Sydney is surrounded by beaches but Bondi is the main one and located in the city. This beach is paradise for surfers & they create a magnificent view on the sea. The beach is really vast & Bondi to Coogee coastal walk is really sprawling & scenic. One can spend a whole day in the beach. People are always busy with different activities like volleyball, surfing n all. Not only human even dogs also come for a coastal walk.People do picnic at the beach side & it's really well connected with the other sides of the city.

reviews.title: Golden Sands
reviews.text: Went to Bondi Beach yesterday at the end of the Coogee to Bondi Coastal Walk.It is an Australian Icon, so therefore very busy. A tourist Mecca even now with the Covid-19 virus threatening.Too busy for me, but if it is your scene you should check it out!

reviews.title: Bondi Beach
reviews.text: We live in Florida,USA and found Bondi Beach stunning. We found it clean, the locals pleasant and the cliff walk awesome. We also rode the hop on hop off bus which was very slow to pick us up BUT it was Friday rush hour so we just took it to the last stop and walked to our hotel through one of the parks. Wonderful!

reviews.title: Breathtaking Views!
reviews.text: My husband, son and I took the Coogee to Bondi walk for the first time in many years and it was just as gorgeous as we remembered! Walking along the sea cliffs, through several lovely beaches, and ending at Bondi is a terrific way to experience the best of Sydney. We went on a Saturday but there was smoke that likely kept some of the crowds away. Still, there was a steady flow of people, mostly tourists. Next time we might go on a weekday.

reviews.title: Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach but didnt really live up to my high expectations.  We took the Hop on Hop Off Bus just to take pictures of it.  We didn't get in the water.  It was really too hot for us to be there without doing so.  I think that may have prevented me from enjoying it as much as I thought I would.

reviews.title: Must See
reviews.text: World famous ad certainly worth a visit. Awesome to see the rocks where the pool juts out into the sea. We did a walk from Coogee to Bondi Beach and found some of the other beaches nicer! Bondi beach is quite busy

reviews.title: Not my favourite destination
reviews.text: Unfortunately, Bondi Beach and surrounds are overcrowded, poorly maintained by Waverley Council and there's litter everywhere !!!

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: You must visit this beach. The water is beautiful and the sand is clean. You can walk near the cliffs and see spectacular views.

reviews.title: Nice beach nothing special
reviews.text: The sand was beautiful, white, soft and nice to walk on, the sea was warm very salty though! There were sun loungers and deck chairs to hire for $10 for 3 hours, worth getting though. Little shops dotted around, showers and toilet facilities. The beach is good for water sports. Nothing too special but is a nice beach

reviews.title: Beautiful Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is easy to reach by bus from Sydney CBD. It is a beautiful 1000 meters of golden sand and warm gentle waves. The water is clear and refreshing, but the sun is intense. There is no natural shade, however umbrellas and cabanas are available for rent. Plenty of restaurants and shops line the street. Public washrooms and changing facilities are available. Take a walk south for some smaller, less touristy beaches like Bronte Beach. The coastal walk is incredible and keep going further all the way to Coogee Beach if you have the time and energy.

reviews.title: Icon
reviews.text: Bondi beach always a beautiful site. Easy to get there by walking from Bondi junction or directly but bus. Water is always cool but enticing. The boulevard is tired so you can imagine the era and who has enjoyed this icon. Beautiful memories

reviews.title: Yep, it’s ‘The’ Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Great to visit this iconic beach, just to see what all the fuss is about (we’ve all seen at least one episode of Bondi Rescue!)Overcast when we were there so the 20,000 plus visitors they can get per day was down to about 150!It’s a lovely clean beach and we enjoyed a good swim.The beach isn’t as big as I was expecting and don’t think I’d like to be here when it’s packed.Enjoyed our time here, but there are (in my opinion) better beaches around.

reviews.title: Packed
reviews.text: Spent some time here on New Year’s Day.  Naturally, the beach was packed. It was a very lovely day. The temperature was just right and everyone were having a great time. Got a chance to walk around and explore the area. Very nice beach.

reviews.title: No Cigars!
reviews.text: During our Sydney stay we decided to visit the iconic Bondi Beach.The beach is a great place to visit a stroll along the shoreline We started off at the Icebergs swimming pool with the fantastic view across the bay

reviews.title: Wear your sunscreen.
reviews.text: We took the public bus from Sydney, they get packed tightly to the beach. The beach is quite beautiful, such white lustrous sandy beaches and some kick arse scorching sun, like you have never experienced ever before.My friends and I were out hanging out watching peeps and by the water for about 45 minutes and I had blisters on the back of my legs from that short time out. We didn’t have any sunscreen on since we really didn’t intend on sunbathing and were hanging out at the cafes and restaurants nearby. The sun is intense and the claim is that even the SPF from home has zero efficacy against the Australian sun at all. Buy it there. I think Australia has the highest rate of skin cancer and I get why. Wear a strong SPF even if you are out briefly here walking. The sun blister was painful for days and kept us hotel bound for several days.

reviews.title: Family
reviews.text: Great beach , clean , water was beautiful, easy to catch bus there  from city , met a couple of the lifeguards! Great walk from Brontes pools ! Lots of food choices across the street!

reviews.title: Always a popular location
reviews.text: Stopped here for a wander after getting off the Big Bus tour and found some lovely shops, bars and restaurants. Also had a stroll along the lovely beach. Well worth a visit.

reviews.title: Fun beach but crowded
reviews.text: Bondi is the iconic Sydney beach, and it’s a lot of fun. The retaining walls have wonderfully colorful art painted by local artists, there are plenty of concessions, showers, and changing rooms, it’s easily reached by public transportation, and you can surf, swim, sunbathe, or sit in the shade of a rental umbrella as you like. And, if you like crowds of nearly naked folks sitting, surfing and sunbathing within inches of you, it’s the place to go. I prefer secluded, pristine beaches, so Bondi’s charms were limited for me. It’s a scene, fun to watch, not a place I’d want to stay.

reviews.title: Obligatory Check-in
reviews.text: It's part of the must do experience when you hit Sydney however if I am honest I was a little disappointed.  So many more beautiful beaches along the coast. It was really busy!

reviews.title: Bondi Rocks !!!
reviews.text: Though it was too cold to swim during my visit I loved the beach itself and the massive waves! We also loved the rocks and got some great photos! Recommend a visit to Bondi!!

reviews.title: Good facilities but not as picturesque as hoped
reviews.text: We walked to bondi beach from potts point. Great walk and bondi was nice. Good restaurants and good changing/shower/beach facilities. We hired an umbrella and 2 x loungers for $35 for 4 hours which was a lot but worth it. Was expecting a more picturesque beach but it was pretty standard. It was a nice day but wouldn't rush back.

reviews.title: BONDI Beach Sydney is Gorgeous
reviews.text: Date of experience: 26 December 2019Bondi is one of Australia’s most iconic beaches because of its sweeping white-sand curved shape. Bondi gas its own dramatic scenery. Bondi is attractive to walkers and joggers. Reliable waves draw surfers while, nearby, hardy locals swim in the Icebergs ocean pool year-round.Bondi Beach has been used and is still used as a location for numerous films, television series, music videos, and a video game. The tour manager of Thomas Cook said that numerous festivals and events such as the annual “Miss Bondi beauty pageant” have made Bondi Beach a popular destination among travellers. The beach has long captured the attention of poets including legendary Les Murray, Joanne Burns and Brook Emery.

reviews.title: Simply gorgeous
reviews.text: We were recommended to trade Bondi for Manly Beach but were keen to say we’d been to Bondi. We loved it! For someone who hates sand, I loved the feel of the sand at Bondi. So much in the way of people watching and the water was gorgeous. We laid on the beach, went for a swim and a stroll and enjoyed coffee at one of the little shops along the foreshore. Keen to check out Sydney’s other beaches next time.

reviews.title: Rain!
reviews.text: Went here twice in January- once rainy, once sunny and very different experiences. Loved needing the Bondi lifeguards when they were filming.

reviews.title: Right out of the TV series
reviews.text: An absolute “do not miss” when you are in Sydney! Together with Copacabana and Waikiki Beach probably one out of three of the most famous beaches in the world. And dramatic with the strong currants and high waves!

reviews.title: One of the lovely place in Australia.
reviews.text: Fantastic beach. People look very happy. Very clean and safe. Beautiful wave. We spent few hours in here.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Everything is awesome. The beach, the mood, the people. We had a wonderful time. People from all over the world are there. We made the walk trough the beaches and the landscape is breathtaking. I recomend!

reviews.title: Just an overall Greek beach town with an amazing nightlife and food scene
reviews.text: So I stayed and bond I beach for four days I hate the trails north to Manley and south to Cordia Beach what an amazing experience to walk those trails. The beach itself is utterly amazing and you have so many people at the beach at all times the water was clean and clear cool refreshing and if you serve early morning had some of the best surfing I so I stayed in Bondi Beach for four days I hate the trails north manly and south to corgi beach what an amazing experience to walk those trails. The beach itself is utterly amazing and you have so many people at the beach at all times the water was clean and clear cool refreshing and if you surf early morning had some of the best surfing.I stayed at the week up hostile right in the heart of bond I beach which I recommend pretty much anyone because of how nice facilities are. Are you sure if you were there on a Sunday to go to the Bondi market great experience if you like flea markets and small vendor foods

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: This is a a beautiful clean beach the sand was soft and the sea clear if a little cold, we had our 3 year old so we didn't venture to far into the sea, there is a small seawater pool next to the beach which was perfect for us it has a seating area. There are lifeguards and set areas to swim and surf. The waves are big and the current strong. We had to walk a fair bit to find a restaurant that had space as it was busy. We took a taxi to the beach which I was glad of as the parking seemed full. There are beach showers available which are handy. This is a lovely beach and a must if your visiting the area.

reviews.title: Bondi beach
reviews.text: Easy to access from Hop on bus stop.Clean sand with Lifeguards on duty.Surf beach so large waves with undertow so swim only between the flags. Lovely walk to Iceburg pool then local shops for great priced souvenirs such as good quality tshirts at $40.

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: Our favorite beach...the very fine sand feels great beneath your feet.  Many places to eat nearby completes the experience.  Getting train away from beach is a challenge because of big crowds so we took a taxi back to Sydney.

reviews.title: Surf paradise
reviews.text: Soft white sand and big surf waves!! What a great experience other than the parking fee $25 for 3 hours😩The lifeguards set up a good stretch of beach for safe swimming.The cliff walk from Bondi to Coogee Beach is an amazing way to see the different rock formations and beaches along the way Just under 7 km hike Lots of joggers and training parks along the way if you’re inclined to do it as a workout

reviews.title: A short stretch of paradise
reviews.text: I have visited many of the famous beaches in the world, but few as lively as Bondi ! The sandy stretch is relatively very short, as compared to Copacabana Ipanema but it's the cleanest and well maintained. The beachside restaurants offer some of the best food and drink in Sydney! One can relax with a chilled beer and watch the waves surge ashore over the thousands of young beach enthusiasts sunning themselves!

reviews.title: Surf’s up!
reviews.text: Took a stroll on an overcast day.  It was only an hour long walk as the tour bus was waiting.  However, it would have been a sin had we not done so.A neat bar/restaurant nearby for a drink to complete our tour, perfect!

reviews.title: Typical Sydney stop
reviews.text: Beautiful beach but definitely highly touristed. Still a needed sight to see while in Sydney a cant miss

reviews.title: Good location
reviews.text: If your a tourist it’s a few restaurants and pubs around , a lot of people walking around and at the beach was a good vibe.

reviews.title: Beautiful.....crowded!
reviews.text: The beach is beautiful but also very very crowded. we were there on a Saturday and there was little place to move. We still spent several hours there and had a great time. Please keep an eye on your tweens and teens as it is easy to get lost. Take a lot of water, umbrellas and maybe your boards. Also sign up for surf boarding lessons early as the time is determined by the waves. Options are limited.

reviews.title: Not what we expected
reviews.text: We visited Bondai Beach as part of the hop on hop off bus tour.It was a miserable rainy day and it didn’t look very inviting.Guess it’s fine for surfers but the water was too rough for us to venture in.

reviews.title: Famous Beach
reviews.text: Even thought the beach was really busy as it was New Year's Day,there was still plenty of space to spread you towel and catch the rays, take a dip or watch the surfers. The iconic life guards were in abundance,  Being a smoking free beach it was nice to find a cigarette free beach, in fact there was next to no rubbish on the beach.

reviews.title: Great beach, be smart about public transit options
reviews.text: So the beach itself is great, lots of space even on a hot summer day.  When we were there, the part of the beach closest to the ocean was obviously the most packed however the back half of the beach still had plenty of real estate to go around (and we were there on a summer Saturday).  Lots of kids but can easily be avoided due to the ample space.If you intend to take public transit, do yourself a favor and begin at locations where most don’t or you’ll be standing for a 20-40 minute ride depending on where you get on.  To ensure you get a seat going there, get on the bus at circular quay.  Coming back, walk to the far north end of the beach first, and then get on the bus.  Going there, if you take the train and then get on the bus at Bondi junction, it’s standing room only.  Similarly going back, if you get on the bus at the south end of the beach, all the seats will already be taken.An option if you don’t want to sit on the actual beach is the iceberg pool located on the southernmost end of the beach.

reviews.title: New Year’s Day visit
reviews.text: It seemed such an iconic way to spend New Year’s Day at Bondi beach - oh my goodness so crowded  !Unbelievable numbers and I truly think it’s not even the best beach !Just the most famous - haha Fabulous people watching and still a must do if you come to Sydney

reviews.title: Fun place to hang out!
reviews.text: As a British tourist I really enjoyed a short visit to Bondi! We walked up to the pool and enjoyed watching the famous lifeguards do their thing. Beach got busier as the day went on and I particularly enjoyed the street art all along the boardwalk!

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: First time to Bondi Beach. Cold sea water and fine beautiful sand. Spending half day morning at the beach with nice cool weather. Suited for surfing than swimming.

reviews.title: Bondi Beach
reviews.text: We had to go to Bondi you couldn't come to Sydney and not visit Bondi. The sand was beautiful, the sea more suited for surfing than swimming but the lifeguards were definitely on the ball at all times keeping you fully informed as to safe swimming areas etc. We spent a lovely day there soaking up the sun,  beach beds umbrellas etc in abundance - cost for three beds and one umbrella for 65 dollars (approx £30). Lovely restaurants and a good amount of shops. All in all a lovely day.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Great beach but be prepared for how cold the water is.  Lots of cafes and shops makes for a great day out

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: Visited the place for new years.It's a good beach, saw plenty families there. The water was apparently cold because, it was getting cloudy when I reached there.It's one of the must go places in Australia.I enjoyed the white sand. I'm sure you'll enjoy.  And yes, there are lifeguards at the beach

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: The beach itself is pretty but right by a noisy road. There is no shade anywhere. On the day we visited the surf was dangerous and water was freezing. Maybe we just picked a bad day!

reviews.title: Very busy!
reviews.text: The beach is nice, but there are far too many people there, luckily I hadn't arrived just to see Bondi!

reviews.title: Top 10 beach
reviews.text: Having beautiful beaches at my country home and visiting the most beautiful beaches in the world I can say that bondi is almost perfect. The sand is soft and white as you can get, the sea is a beautiful blue BUT the water is freezing cold. That is the reason I don’t give it a 10 but an 7. Despite that, the vibe, sand sea and restaurants around makes it great. Be aware, if you go with kids, that there are ton of topless all around.

reviews.title: Gem
reviews.text: On our first trip to Sydney we wanted to make sure we made it ti the famous Bondi Beach. We were not disappointed. We enjoyed a lovely lunch at a beachside cafe and watched those brave enough to go into the water. Although it was December and summer it was still pretty cold out there.Still there were lots of people on the beach and in the shops and cafes. Wish we had more time to spend out there as it beautiful.

reviews.title: Most happening beach
reviews.text: There a few beaches along the coast but this is probably by far the most crowded and most happening. Despite being crowded, you can still find a spot to lie down to get a tan.

reviews.title: Different
reviews.text: We were here for a short visit but this place was packed. It provides lots of options for food and shops. Although it wasn’t a very hot day the beach was packed.

reviews.title: Walk from Coogee to Bondi
reviews.text: End the coastal walk at Bondi for a cool beer but holiday crowds everywhere and weekends make areas like Bronte full. Enjoy lunch or dinner at the Coogee Pavilion though!

reviews.title: Loved Bondi Beach
reviews.text: My favourite part of our trip to Australia.  We loved the trails along the beach and walked about 16km’s that day.  Highly recommend it if you love to walk.

reviews.title: Over rated
reviews.text: A beautiful and popular beach, but there are others, just as and more scenic around Sydney that eclipse this one.

reviews.title: Great Australian icon
reviews.text: Location, charisma, fun.  Bondi is known around the world. A place to be seen and to see people from around the world who come to soak up the sun, surf and atmosphere

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: It was dirty and not enough toilets and the toilets where dirty and smells plus no toilet paper would never go again

reviews.title: Family Friendly Must-See
reviews.text: We packed our stroller full of beach gear and took the bus out here from downtown.  Worth the visit.  Very clean and something for everyone.  Our 2yr old splashed in the little pools at the north end.Be advised it is very busy and the change rooms are kind of gross.

reviews.title: Bondi
reviews.text: It's just the name Bondi which brings people over here. Found this place to be an average beach. The cafes and bars over here a little expensive.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach and walking track
reviews.text: We walked from Elizabeth Bay to Bondi Beach, which is a beautiful 3 hour walk, and then carried on along the Coast on the South side of Bondi Beach before coming back to the beach itself for some sun bathing. A great day in a beautiful area. People from Sydney are lucky to have such a beautiful beach at their door step.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Beautiful long stretch of beach.  Good for boogie boarding, light surfing and sunning.  Even some shade under trees by parking lot

reviews.title: Bondi beach
reviews.text: The most beautiful  beach of Sydney. A must visit place. Spent few hours there with my teenager daughter who loves beach and difficult to drag her out from there as it’s quiet amazing beach.

reviews.title: Morning walk & coffee
reviews.text: Bondi Beach is the destination of my morning walks at least 2-3 times per week. A couple of laps of the boardwalk and if there’s time I’ll enjoy a coffee at Sejuiced juice bar.

reviews.title: Great Place for Having fun
reviews.text: Diving with the Waves will take a lot of fun. You feal Save under the eyes of the lifegarde team. The Beach is clean and you have the opportunities for restrooms, shower facilities and changing Rooms. They are many possibilitys for having Drinks and Snacks .

reviews.title: Crowded, dirty, and with polluted air.
reviews.text: This grossly overused beach is most time extremely crowded, dirty with litter, oil slicks, and ash.  The overheated crowds are also known to be rather hostile.  Polluted air from the city and the nearby burning national parks tops off the experience most people would prefer to miss.

reviews.title: Iconic
reviews.text: Very easy to get there, bus 333 from downtown Sydney, goes really often. The beach was just a perfection for the a day of. Very soft and sad and nice waves.

reviews.title: Beautiful Clean Beaches
reviews.text: Just love this place - it’s the perfect spot for some time out of the hussle of the City Parking can be a bit challenging so take the puck transport into Bondi - very walkable too

reviews.title: LOVE THIS BEACH
reviews.text: First time I come to white people beach. It is excellent. The view is good. The restaurant near by is very nice. The people has good body that make me work hard to keep as well!

reviews.title: Lovely beach & Art Work alongside!
reviews.text: It is the iconic Sydney beach and well worth the visit. It has cafes and restaurants upstairs along the beach (mostly expensive). Right next to the beach, there is a pathway, where you walk along and can see the art work of different artists and is worth a visit. The beach is hot fav among the locals/surfers.

reviews.title: Bondi beach
reviews.text: Amazing beach,  heaps to look at, well paroled,great eateries and coffee shop within walking distance

reviews.title: Beautiful, beautiful, beautiful.
reviews.text: Took the bus from Taylor Sq. to bondi beach a journey of around 25minutes and arrived at this beautiful site. Pristine sand and a vibrant ocean combined. It wasn’t the busiest of days but it was truly lovely. Well cared for, no rubbish in sight, lifeguards on station, it was great.  There’s a walkway at road level if you don’t want to get sand in your toes. But you’re at bondi, get stuck in! Plenty of souvenirs and eateries of all description to choose from.  If you choose the right time this would be heaven.

reviews.title: It has to be seen and it has to be visited.
reviews.text: Iconic yet a beach for everyone. In Italy it would be covered in beach umbrellas and roped off into sections by the beach mafia. Not in egalitarian Australia. Here it is open for all comers and it is a joy to look at and to admire. Sun bathe - no one seems to pay any attention to the Cancer Council mantra of “slip, slap, slop, slide” though perhaps more “slide” on the designer sunnies than the rest. At least they have got rid off the oil dispensers that used to be available to ensure skin cancers got a good chance to develop. Or surf or just play in the surf. All tastes and all styles are welcome. But why does the council allow cars to park on prime space overlooking this stunning bay and beach? The bus service into the city is frequent. The beachfront businesses cater to most tastes.

reviews.title: Bondi
reviews.text: Its a beach.  Dont put more into it than you should.  If you really wanted beaches you wouldn't be in Sydney.  It has good atmosphere and is overhyped but it has an amazing trail system to walk and free toilets.

reviews.title: Great Beach
reviews.text: Soft sand, clean, & clear blue water!  Great place to relax. Great location within walking distance of food/drinks and shopping.  It can get crowded.

reviews.title: Awesome waves, great beach
reviews.text: Came with kids and they immediately started swimming by the surf area. A local let us know that there's some bad rip-currents on the beach so we should stay "between the flags to swim." The waves were large as far as I was concerned and the kids (age 10) had an absolute blast playing in the surf. There was metered parking and the day we went, we were able to get a spot without any problem but it might be a hassle on busy days? There's lots of shops and restaurants right next to the beach and surf shops and people giving lessons and stuff. Great beach!

reviews.title: Stunning views
reviews.text: Be prepared that it is VERY busy on a Sunday. From casual holiday makers, older people doing their best, to rude runners trying to do a PB. If you are a tourist from overseas, last can be a bad reflection. It will be a good idea to limit running at certain times of the day/week. Take water and wear flats. Not ideal, but not impossible, to go with a pram

reviews.title: Best beach in the world?
reviews.text: This beach proves its one of the best in the world. The sand is clean and deep. The girls are gorgeous and many are topless. You want food and drink? You’ve got fifty choices with a ten minute walk.

reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.text: I suppose this is a must visit place. Areas could do with an upgrade but the beach  is wonderful and clean.

reviews.title: Bondi
reviews.text: Well not as big as I expected. Didn’t look too safe for swimming with young children. Very big waves. A good place to hang out with friends though and the life guards were plentiful. Good bars and restaurants also

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Beautiful beach.  Lots of people swimming and surfing.  Be aware that if you do want to swimming in the water, there are flags marked on the beach.  That is the safest area where there is no riptide.

reviews.title: Really cool beach
reviews.text: Really cool beach. It’s famous, iconic and touristy. Very beautiful views. A bit overpriced on everything. But still must visit when in Sydney!

reviews.title: Best part of Sydney!
reviews.text: We were told by many to avoid Bondi beach that it’s too touristy and there are better beaches. I’m very happy we ignored that. We actually did not care for the city of Sydney and felt that Bondi was one of it’s redeeming factors!

reviews.title: Amazing walk if you like beaches
reviews.text: Took the 6km walk from Bondi to Congee beach and took us about 3 hours at a leisurely pace. Could see people fishing, surfing and swimming along the way. It was very windy and even though it was summer, we hardly sweated! Would recommend using sunblock :)

reviews.title: Iconic Beach
reviews.text: I just had to visit Bondi whilst in Sydney and was so glad I did. Lovely clean beach and when we visited it was pretty quiet due to the weather not being the greatest. However stepping foot on the iconic beach was a great moment and one I will never forget.

reviews.title: Bondi beach - tourists everywhere
reviews.text: Must see, very touristy but iconic. Glad we came but still prefer Manly beach worth a breakfast or lunch visit

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: This is a must see lovely and clean just what I thought it would be like after watching it on tv didn’t see the life guards lol lots of places to eat and drink enjoy a lovely glass of wine looking out at the beach

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Very nice beach to go to.  Has a lovely expanse.  Is a good beach to look at - either from close up or from "high" up nearby.  Am sure it is also a good beach for swimming.  I've seen it a few times when I visit Sculptures by the Sea from year to year.  There are good cafes nearby from which to view the beach while eating/drinking.

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text: Perfect sand, clean and friendly.  This is one of the best beaches and water in the world...see for yourself.

reviews.title: Iconic beach
reviews.text: Had a great day on this iconic beach , not as amazing as I thought but clean white sand and a good day out Mike uk

reviews.title: Very impressive beach
reviews.text: Obviously the most famous and iconic of all the Sydney beaches. A beautiful and long stretch of coastline boasting beautiful spots for surfing and swimming.One has to be conscious travelling alone with valuables - as it is more crowded and has more tourists. I had no issues but if you want to lock away your possessions you can only do so until 1630 at beachside facilities.

reviews.title: Bondi's up!
reviews.text: Bondi is an Aboriginal word for surf, and there's plenty of it on this beach. While the northern end is gentle, the southern end has a rip current known as Backpackers' Rip. We chose to forego swimming or sunning and just viewed the beach from overlooks near Notts Avenue and looking back from the Bondi to Coogee Beach Coastal Walk (see my review, "Put Bondi Beach in your rearview mirror").One of Australia's most visited tourist sites, Bondi Beach hosted the beach volleyball events at the 2000 Summer Olympics. Near the center of the beach, Bondi Pavilion hosts major festivals. There's a fascinating oceanside swimming pool at the southern end (see my review of Bondi Icebergs Swimming Club, "Wave pool -- literally!").TIPS:* Consider taking a city bus from the Central Business District. It's easy, though it can be crowded with other beachgoers.

reviews.title: Iconic Beach
reviews.text: We were not disappointed when we visited Bondi beach. It is very popular with so many people but still plenty of room to spread out on the beach. Great place for people watching!

reviews.title: BEST BEACH IN SYDNEY
reviews.text: Our party of 6 adults and 2 kids from Singapore selected Bondi Beach in Sydney to get a feel of the sun,sand and sea available in Sydney. We were very happy with our day trip to Bondi. The beach was popular with swimmers and surfers. There were good food options. We were lucky to catch performers near the Heritage Pavilion .

reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: I found Bondi to be very average - it was probably a great beach before, but now it's just too full of tourists. The shops were overpriced, and I didn't find the beach itself to be particularly beautiful. It is really the type of the place where you go to be seen and to say that you've been - if I go back to Sydney, I would probably go to Manly instead.

reviews.title: Iconic and beautiful
reviews.text: This is one of the worlds most iconic beaches and it certainly doesn’t disappoint. You can get there via the 333 bus from the city or T4 train to Bondi Junction and then either the 333 bus or 380 from the bus station just outside the train station.The waters are unbelievably clear and so blue. I’ve never seen anything like it. The sand was beautiful and the beach incredibly clean. There are lockers, changing rooms and even a place to hire things like towels, chairs and buy sun cream. There are also some great places to eat.We went on a warm week day and it wasn’t very busy which was fantastic. A must when visiting Australia!

reviews.title: Fine
reviews.text: Great sand now with umbrellas and loungers for rent.Excellent lifeguard beach coverage.All in all looks great, but can be windy, as today.Crowds are large, be warned if you are catching the bus.

reviews.title: Very Pretty
reviews.text: I didn't go swimming because I didn't have time, but the area is super cute and had tons of places to shop and eat. I walked around and took pictures. I wish I had the time to go swimming.

reviews.title: Perfect for a Long Walk
reviews.text: We liked this beach better than Manly Beach. The boardwalk was fun for a long walk. We found a small cafe at the end with good food.

reviews.title: Must visit beach in New South Wales
reviews.text: I went there for Sculpture by the Sea and it was amazing! The sun was shining and everything perfect. You should visit this place if you come to NSW

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: While on Sydney worth the trip to see the beach! Stunning panorama , good shops and restaurants. Recommend!

reviews.title: Superb ocean beach
reviews.text: Just a superb ocean beach.  Big, wide and handsome and so close to the centre of Sydney.  A great beach to visit, whether you’re planning a swim or a sightsee.  If you’re doing the latter, make sure you take the paths up to the headlands.  The view back to the beach or out to the pacific ocean is superb.  It’s also a short walk to the more compact but also very beautiful Tamarama beach.  Don’t miss this fantastic experience folks.

reviews.title: An icon of Australian culture.
reviews.text: There is not a lot else to add about Bondi Beach. A large sandy beach, surrounded by coastal footpaths, parks and suburban streets. Very popular on a warm sunny day.

reviews.title: Must see Sydney beach
reviews.text: Dont miss out on Bondi - easy to reach Bondi Junction by train, and then a quick bus ride right to the beach. The surrounding area is beautiful, the beach is huge and clean, and there are many costal walks you can take to surrounding beaches. It's famous for a reason!

reviews.title: Iconic Bondi Beach
reviews.text: Hot and sunny with an great range of amenities, shopping and eateries within a 2 minute walk from the beach. Easy to get to on the train or bus from Sydney

reviews.title: MUST SEE
reviews.text: Went to see the Sculptures by the Sea and walked from Tamarama to Bondi past all the sculptures, we caught bus 381 from Bondi Junction to Tamarama and it was an easy walk along the beautiful coastline to Bondi Beach, we had lunch at the Bondi Icebergs which has a magnificent view of Bondi Beach and the food and drinks were delicious, we then walked past all the Murals on a wall right opposite the Beach which are great to see, if you swim here make sure to swim between the flags, Bondi Beach itself is stunning and a must to see if in Sydney.

reviews.title: Fantastic beach with Chill sea breeze
reviews.text: The Bondi beach is picturesque with different colors and lovely surf. In September the sea breeze was real cold. Nice place to surf for the surf lovers. Really refreshing to sit there. Lot of eateries around.

reviews.title: Sculptures by the Sea 23rd annual exhibition 2019
reviews.text: We viewed the sculptures by the sea at Bondi on Monday, 28 October.  It started out a little bit drizzly, but cleared up to be a great day for viewing the sculptures.  We started at Bondi where we were able to purchase a catalogue and site map for the price of $12.  This year the exhibition was held from 24 October to 10 November.  We walked along the bottom area of the exhibition, Bondi to Tamarama, inspecting the various sculptures and then on the way back, we viewed the top area located in Marks Park, South Bondi headland.  Here also is a covered viewing area where small sculptures are on exhibition.  There were many sculptures, some of the ones we liked were David Ball sculpture called "Celest", Egor Zigura sculpture called "Colossus Awakens", and Sallie Portnoy sculpture called "Sea Garden".  We started early and by lunch time the crowds were beginning to come, so best to avail yourself of an early start to avoid the crowds.

reviews.title: Best Aussie beach
reviews.text: A must see if visiting Australia and whilst in Sydney. The beach has good facilities and cafe. The sand and surf can be really busy, and A lot to view, boobs out is legal. Good skate park and parking, does fill up easy on nice weather days.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: My Daughter & I loved Bondi Beach & we are due to go back soon. We went by train & then took a bus. There is also some great shopping to be done in Bondi Junction.

reviews.title: Beautiful Bondi
reviews.text: We enjoyed Bondi Beach even though it was windy and a bit cool (Spring in Sydney).  The Bucket List cafe was OK - beer selection fair compared to California.  All in all we thoroughly enjoyed Bondi.  We did have trouble getting the parking meter to work; however, Urs left a note on the windshield and 4 1/2 hours later - No ticket‼️

reviews.title: Dissapointment at Bondi
reviews.text: We were so excited, but when we arrived there was no where to park at all.  All carparks where full, and many of them you could only park for 30 mins.  the beach and dining looked amazing, but it was absolutely packed.  we were so stressed driving around looking for a spot we ended up leaving and got too see nothing.If you go, go super early as going mid morning like we did is a nightmare

reviews.title: Excitement, fun, security
reviews.text: A beach for all ages and tastes. It even has a seawater swimming pool. For those who do not want to swimm there's a beautiful lawn to lay down and apreciate the view and the sun. Many restaurants, stores and cafés will make your stay much better. The lifeguard team is the best in Australia.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: Visited this iconic beach went by train from central station to Bondi junction and  then bus 333 very easy to do , just get an opal card to tap on and off not expensive . You also get to see the surrounding area . Spent a beautiful morning sat on the beach watching to surfers and even ventured in the see my self a bit on the cold but with the experience. I suspect it can get very busy at a weekend . There are lockers, changing room and showers (free to use ) at the Bondi beach bath building in the center of the promenade. I think lockers were 4 dollars.

reviews.title: Great spot
reviews.text: First visit, not much surf happening but enjoyed the walk along the track of the Sea sculptures there for a period of time. Breach is beautiful white sand, we tool a walk along to Tamarama and Bronte beaches and overall I think Bronte was nicer. Bondi just has the name

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: After hearing about Bondi Beach for many years, it was great to finally see it.  The beach is wide and sandy, perfect for sun bathing.  It also is famous as being one of the best places to surf in Australia.  When we were there in the late afternoon, there were lots of surfers catching long, slow waves.  Bondi is easy to reach from Sydney via bus, Uber or taxi.

reviews.title: Most famous but not the best beach in Sydney
reviews.text: This iconic beach is a tourist trap If your looking to tick it off the list then it isn’t such a bad spot Head south along the Bondi to coogee walk and you will be amazed at the views and you’ll probably find a nicer beach on the way.

reviews.title: A day trip from Stdney
reviews.text: We took transport for Sydney for those who are maybe planning to do the same!We took a train from Martin Place to Bondi Junction - cost $2ish and took around 15 minutes on an Opal card (which we purchased in the train station at a kiosk for €10). We then took a 333 bus from stance A in the bus station and it was another €2ish and 20 minutes bus journey. We were dropped right beside the beach. The actual beach is as expected; super busy!!! The only facilities we used were the toilets before leaving. The ladies toilets needed a good clean! I would not have put my bag down for love nor money - but they do the job and no charge is applied so can’t complain TOO much!

reviews.title: Sydney's most famous beach
reviews.text: Not a lot has changed over the years.  This is still one of the most popular beaches to see and be seen.  It has nice sand, surfing, a salt water pool at one end (8aud per person) and the typical tourist stores/bars you find at every popular beach.

reviews.title: Great brach
reviews.text: Wow what a great place, pure white sand, blue sea what more could you want.   Just as appears clean and locals appear proud of it

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: Bondi is one of the most famous beaches in the world for a reason! From the environment surrounding the beach to the culture around the beach, everything adds to the vibe. Just grab a drink from one of the surrounding cafes and watch the waves hit the icebergs pool, take a walk along the beach or just be there. It's wonderful!

reviews.title: Smaller than I thought
reviews.text: After all the hype I heard of Bondi Beach, it was disappointing.  Smaller than I thought and not a lot to do.  A few restaurants and bars, but nothing else.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach busy
